notes: These vectors pin CBA dual-plane semantics. DataEvent vectors use effects + seal_ref + auth_context and never use preconditions. Control Move vectors use effects + seal_basis and may use preconditions.

Seal delta entries reference only newly sealed control-plane event digests. Cumulative coverage is derived from predecessor_refs[] plus delta[]. DataEvent digests may appear in data_event_set_root / data_view_root observations, but those roots do not confer control-plane finality.
Cell ids follow ak:cell:ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n>:<subject>; subject placeholders use dot-safe strings to keep examples unambiguous.

vectors.name: data_event_accepts_without_seal_finality
vectors.description: A message DataEvent is locally accepted when signature, actor chain, seal_ref, auth_context, capability and data-plane Lattice validation pass. It does not wait for Seal coverage.

vectors.name: data_event_observation_does_not_seal
vectors.description: A Seal may observe DataEvents through data_event_set_root, but the query grade is observed, not sealed.

vectors.name: control_move_requires_seal_basis_and_seal
vectors.description: A membership ban Control Move uses seal_basis for authorization and preconditions. It remains control_pending until covered by a valid Seal.

vectors.name: same_batch_does_not_advance_authorization_basis
vectors.description: An Event earlier in the same submit batch may resolve bytes and causal refs for later Events, but it cannot create a grant used by a later Event in the same batch.

vectors.name: data_plane_conflict_returns_bottom_without_winner
vectors.description: Concurrent incompatible writes to a data-plane cas_register cell return structured bottom. The reducer must not choose a winner by HLC, actor id, arrival order, or Seal observation order.

vectors.name: seal_delta_excludes_data_event_digest
vectors.description: A Seal delta contains newly sealed control-plane event digests only. Including a DataEvent digest in delta is a seal validation failure.

vectors.name: open_set_compaction_preserves_control_roots
vectors.description: A signed compaction Seal must be equivalent to the deterministic control view of its predecessors and preserve control_event_set_root, state_root and fault diagnostics.

vectors.name: seal_canonical_no_self_reference
vectors.description: Seal canonical bytes are computed from signed top-level body fields only. The Seal id and notary_signature are excluded from the transcript.

vectors.name: cas_mixed_basis
vectors.description: cas_register writes on a non-initial settled value require an explicit CBA basis; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.

vectors.name: auth_context_epoch_pinning_reject
vectors.description: Verifier evaluates key and credential epoch validity at the event seal_ref, not only against the current DID document.

vectors.name: seal_compaction_interval_enforced
vectors.description: Realm seal_compaction_max_interval_ms is a structural obligation: valid full-coverage compaction enables bootstrap, mismatched coverage rejects, and overdue compaction raises health alarms.

vectors.name: inclusion_list_obligation
vectors.description: A multi-signer notary Seal must discharge valid inclusion-list obligations by inclusion, signed reject, or pre-state verification failure proof.

vectors.name: notary_fault_equivocation_quarantine
vectors.description: Two different Seals signed by the same notary in the same slot authorize public equivocation evidence, quarantine the fork, and reject later Seals from that signer.

vectors.name: threshold_forensic_attribution
vectors.description: Threshold notary forensic_attribution must match the quorum-intersection arithmetic rule.

vectors.name: open_set_concurrent_revocation_fail_closed
vectors.description: A DataEvent whose seal_ref is locally valid is re-evaluated against the joined multi-leaf control view when a concurrent revocation branch is observed.

cases.name: late_revocation_leaf_retroactive_removal
cases.description: Ordered sequence, not a single joined-view snapshot: E is first accepted and its effect materialized into data cell X under the initial joined view that has NOT yet joined the revoke leaf R. Dependent event D is then accepted with E as a critical causal dependency and materializes an effect into data cell Y. R arrives later; once joined, E loses seal_ref authorization, so E and the complete direct/indirect dependency closure rooted at E MUST leave accepted projection inputs. The final state MUST equal that of a receiver that joined {S0,R} from the start, independent of arrival order.

vectors.name: actor_chain_realm_scope

fixtures/circle-scope-fixture.json.description: Machine-contract fixture for Circle effective_scope semantics and lifecycle basis evaluation. Splits actor submit-payload (scope_circle_id only) from canonical reducer-output (tagged effective_scope on Event envelope and materialized object). Covers rebind transitions, DataEvent seal_ref and Control Move seal_basis evaluation, linear and concurrent archive, tombstone, restore barriers, and negative cases. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md §6.1 / §6.2 / §7 / §9.2 / §10.2.

submit_payload_shape.description: Actor-supplied input on ak.strand.create / ak.message.create / ak.morph.create / ak.relation.create / ak.space.* writes. MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). MUST NOT carry effective_scope.

canonical_reducer_output_shape.description: Reducer-stamped, immutable tagged scope written to Event envelope and materialized object cell. Two discriminated forms: kind=realm | kind=circle.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). No-op rebind; reducer MUST accept.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=null -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=null. True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

negative_cases.name: submit_payload_carrying_effective_scope_rejected
negative_cases.description: Actor MUST NOT supply effective_scope in submit payload. Reducer MUST schema_violation with reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed.

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_targets_inactive_circle
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle with state != active. Reducer MUST failed_precondition reason=circle_not_active.

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_realm_mismatch
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle whose realm_id != object.realm_id. Reducer MUST schema_violation reason=circle_realm_mismatch.

negative_cases.name: accepted_event_missing_effective_scope
negative_cases.description: An accepted durable Circle-scoped Event (e.g. ak.message.create whose Strand scope_circle_id is set) MUST carry the reducer-stamped effective_scope on its envelope. An offline validator / cotest MUST reject an accepted event whose object is Circle-scoped but whose effective_scope is absent, otherwise the §9.3 'Circle scoped event not delivered to non-members' invariant cannot be deterministically replayed. event-envelope.schema.json carries effective_scope as a reducer-stamped field; this vector pins that accepted (post-reducer) Circle events MUST populate it.

negative_cases.name: effective_scope_mismatches_scope_circle_id
negative_cases.description: The reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST be derived from the object's scope_circle_id: scope_circle_id=null -> {kind:realm}; scope_circle_id=C -> {kind:circle, circle_id:C}. A materialized object / accepted event whose effective_scope.circle_id disagrees with its scope_circle_id is corrupt; reducer MUST schema_violation (effective_scope_reducer_managed) on write and a validator MUST reject on read.

negative_cases.name: seal_leaf_effective_scope_tamper
negative_cases.description: effective_scope is part of an Event's canonical bytes, so event_digest = H(canonical bytes) binds it directly. If a Seal later reports the DataEvent inside data_event_set_root, that root is an observational availability/projection proof, not control-plane finality. Mutating effective_scope after signing changes event_digest, so the recomputed digest no longer matches the signed event. Receivers MUST reject with digest_mismatch; this forbids silently re-scoping an accepted event and is why no separate scope field is added to seal.schema.json (the binding is the digest).

negative_cases.name: content_plaintext_under_e2ee_required
negative_cases.description: Realm.content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required requires every Strand/Message/Morph/Blob content effective_scope to be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS). A ak.message.create carrying plaintext content (or whose effective_scope resolves to a plaintext Circle with encryption_profile=none) MUST be rejected with failed_precondition reason=content_encryption_floor_violation.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only. Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.

vectors.name: ak.vector.encoding.crypto.es256_detached_jws.v1

vectors.name: ak.vector.encoding.crypto.mldsa65_raw_detached_signature.v1
vectors.description: ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS 204) raw detached signature over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind = raw_detached_signature; no JOSE wrapping). PQC suite gated by ak.profile.signature.pqc.v1.
vectors.keygen_note: Public conformance test key only, derived via FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen from the recorded 32-byte xi seed (bytes 0x00..0x1f). Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.
vectors.raw_signing_input: UTF-8 bytes of canonical_binding_payload (detached_payload_b64u is its base64url form, provided for cross-checking only; the signed bytes are the unencoded canonical JSON)
vectors.signature_note: Recorded value produced with the FIPS 204 deterministic variant (rnd = 32 zero bytes). Verifiers MUST only verify; producers are NOT required to reproduce these exact signature bytes (hedged signing is allowed).

negative_cases.name: reject_flipped_signature_bit
negative_cases.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped (first signature byte XOR 0x01); everything else is byte-identical to the valid vector.

expected.reason: signature bytes do not verify against the canonical proof binding object

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_none
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares alg=none. The signature segment carries well-formed base64url bytes so the rejection MUST come from the algorithm allowlist, not from shape validation.

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_key_type_mismatch
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares ES256 and the signature genuinely verifies under a P-256 key, but kid resolves to the Ed25519 OKP verification method. The verifier MUST bind alg to the resolved key type (jwk_kty/jwk_crv per signature-alg-registry.json) and fail closed.

expected.reason: declared alg ES256 does not match the resolved verification method key type (OKP/Ed25519); implementations MUST NOT verify with a substituted key

negative_cases.name: reject_truncated_public_key

expected.reason: verification key fails to parse (31 bytes is not an Ed25519 public key length); key material errors MUST fail closed, not fall back to another key

negative_cases.name: reject_non_empty_payload_segment

expected.reason: detached_jws payload segment MUST be empty in compact serialization (encoding.md section 6) even when the attached form would verify

negative_cases.name: reject_es256_truncated_signature

expected.reason: ES256 detached JWS signatures MUST be exactly 64 raw bytes (r||s)

negative_cases.name: reject_es256_truncated_public_key
negative_cases.description: The P-256 x coordinate is truncated to 31 bytes while the detached JWS is otherwise valid.

expected.reason: ES256 verification keys MUST contain valid 32-byte P-256 x and y coordinates

negative_cases.name: reject_mldsa65_truncated_signature

expected.reason: ML-DSA-65 signatures MUST have the exact FIPS 204 byte length

negative_cases.name: reject_mldsa65_truncated_public_key

Convergence is OR-Set on (actor_id, target_ref, key); see zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8 (Reaction model + authoritative OR-Set semantics) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 (plaintext-vs-encrypted visibility).

cases.notes: Two events from the same actor with no causal_refs between them; default view applies per-actor causal closure — concurrent (add, remove) collapses to the remove because the remove is itself a tombstone for the actor's adds in the concurrent past per OR-Set semantics chosen for ak.reaction.

cases.name: e2ee_routing_digest_dedup
cases.notes: In an E2EE realm the plaintext key is the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag: HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("arkret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji)); see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9. The 32-byte tag is carried in `key` as a 256-bit hex digest (the sha256: prefix below denotes the digest wire-encoding, not the derivation). Two adds with the same routing tag from the same actor in the same epoch collapse to one OR-Set membership; the tag differs in a different epoch because the MLS exporter secret rotates on every commit, so it does not dedup across epochs. realm_id is bound via the exporter context, providing defense-in-depth even if mls_group_id is reused across deployments.

cases.name: e2ee_epoch_rotation_breaks_dedup
cases.notes: Same canonical emoji yields a different routing hash after MLS epoch rotation; the new add is a fresh OR-Set entry, not a duplicate of the pre-rotation one.

cases.name: capability_revoked_blocks_subsequent_add

grade_definitions.V: Black-box verifiable by canonical conformance vectors and fixture runner results.
grade_definitions.A: Verifiable by the public SDK API shape and inventory; no implementation-private inspection is required.
grade_definitions.U: Verifiable only by implementation, configuration, or data-flow audit evidence.

sdk_conformance_contract.evidence_coverage_semantics_note: A clause's required_evidence enumerates the ACCEPTABLE evidence kinds for that clause (acceptable-set semantics), not a mandate that every listed kind be present. For a clause claim with result=pass or result=fail: at least one evidence entry MUST be present (already required by the schema when result != not_applicable), and every evidence[].kind MUST be a member of that clause's required_evidence set in this contract. Evidence whose kind falls outside the clause's required_evidence set MUST NOT be accepted as substantiation for that clause. result=not_applicable is exempt from evidence-kind coverage but MUST carry a machine-readable rationale.
rules: Each SDK release claiming Arkret v1 conformance MUST publish one claim object against this exact contract digest.
The claim MUST bind the exact SDK artifact digest and spec revision, and MUST carry an issuer signature over the domain-separated RFC 8785 JCS claim bytes with proof omitted.
Every evidence reference MUST carry a non-zero immutable content digest; consumers MUST verify all digests and the issuer verification method before accepting the claim.
Every applicable clause MUST appear exactly once; not_applicable MUST include a machine-readable rationale.
Evidence references MUST be content-addressed or carry an immutable CI run identifier.

A verifier MUST enforce evidence_coverage_semantics: for every clause claim whose result is pass or fail, it MUST reject the claim unless at least one evidence entry is present and every evidence[].kind is a member of that clause's required_evidence set. A pass/fail clause substantiated only by evidence kinds outside its required_evidence set MUST be rejected. This check is independent of, and applied in addition to, the digest and signature checks above.
Section numbers and table row numbers are not clause identifiers; only clause_id is stable.

clauses.summary: Validate Event Envelope and payload class before consumption
Do not expose a bypass for proof, HLC, actor sequence, prev refs, or authorization refs
Do not expose configuration that disables authorization constraints
Fail closed for causal, revoked, and invalid-proof states
Model cursor values as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Reject malformed or non-canonical JSON without repair
Reject malformed HLC without normalization or truncation
Preserve prev refs, authorization refs, and actor sequence constraints during retry
Verify governance binding and KeyPackage DID before decrypting or encrypting
Do not disclose plaintext or keys to unauthorized services
Light clients must not authorize a DataEvent from a single leaf proof
Apply late-key-recovery visibility checks before decrypting
Fail closed on unknown critical features or unmet requirements
Reject production use of test DIDs, keys, and trust domains
Reconcile trimmed build capabilities with every published profile claim
Preserve unknown values from open registries without failing whole-object deserialization
Preserve explicit extension-slot content through canonical round trips and forwarding
Model ack_token as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Do not automatically replay retry_safe=false operations and rotate the request key when content changes
Honor Retry-After without clamping it into an earlier retry
Continue pagination only when has_more is true
Expose the canonical confusable check as a callable SDK utility

profile_sets.test_build_stance_rule: Test/conformance builds are marked solely by the canonical development_mode=true flag on the ServiceDescribe (see zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1.2 and zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.0), which gates the test-only /_arkret/_conformance/* debug namespace and forces verified_profiles=[]. There is no separate ak.profile.* test-build profile: a test build is a deployment stance, not a negotiated interop capability.

profile_set_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
profile_set_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
profile_set_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

profiles/conformance-profiles.json.candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ak.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profiles/conformance-profiles.json.profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1.description: Fail-closed Realm role profile for the canonical two-principal Direct Conversation Collaboration Realm. The role is identified only by schema_refs containing this profile together with fields.collaboration_role=direct_conversation.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: not applicable: a receiver that cannot enforce this role MUST reject or quarantine the Realm create as unsupported_feature and MUST NOT treat it as an ordinary Collaboration Realm

binding_invariants: schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and fields.collaboration_role MUST equal direct_conversation; either marker without the other is schema_violation.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both equal e2ee_required.

The ak.realm.create Event requirements.schema MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requirements.critical_extensions MUST contain fail_closed=true id ak.feature.direct_conversation_realm_role.v1 for payload scope.
Exactly the two stable subject DIDs in the canonical active binding may be active Realm principal members; any third-party join or invite MUST be rejected.
Space events are forbidden in a Direct Conversation Realm with direct_conversation_space_forbidden; additional ordinary Strands remain allowed.
The canonical main Strand MUST be active, belong to the Realm, have no Circle scope, and expose an active primary discussion track.

Cross-Principal-Server creation MUST complete the participant-authorized peer KeyPackage claim authoring step before the binding authoring step; Direct Conversation claims MUST bind pair_key, intended Realm, main Strand and MLS group and MUST NOT use a last-resort KeyPackage.

A participant leave or ban, Realm tombstone or destroy, or main Strand archive or tombstone retires the active binding and requires a fresh Realm, main Strand and MLS group for the next create=true resolution.

Contact tombstone and direct_message consent revoke block new resolver success and default message send but do not by themselves rewrite Realm history or retire an otherwise structurally active binding.

ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.description: Realm profile for a principal-scoped durable control stream (the Principal Control Realm role; see zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7). It is an ordinary Collaboration Realm at the envelope level, but reducers MUST treat fields.purpose=principal_control + this schema_ref as an allowlist-bound control stream, not as a user collaboration space.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 MUST treat the Realm as an ordinary Collaboration Realm and MUST NOT accept device/session/cross-signing state from it as principal control state.

rules: Agent PCR events MUST target the Agent DID bound to the Realm; controller execution uses actor_id=Agent DID, executed_by=controller DID, and a verified authorization_ref.
Controller-owned accountability and selector facts MUST target the controller PCR and reference the Agent DID; they MUST NOT be moved into the Agent PCR.
Pairing requests and account approval notifications MUST NOT be written to any PCR or Collaboration Realm.

binding_invariants: realm_id MUST equal the principal_control_realm_id resolved for the principal DID.
fields.purpose MUST be principal_control and schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.
encryption_profile MUST be mls_rfc9420; PCRs MUST NOT use none or external.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both be e2ee_required; a PCR genesis declaring either floor below e2ee_required MUST be rejected (no plaintext-floor PCR exists in v1).

history_visibility MUST be restricted; new same-principal devices obtain prior control history via durable device-list / normalized principal view baseline and policy-gated MLS history key share, not by joining at the current epoch.
Control events MUST bind principal_id / device_id / session grant audience to the same principal DID or an explicitly trusted recovery/session issuer.

A managed Agent principal_control_realm_id and immutable requested_scope commitment MUST be verified from the unique ArkretPrincipalControlRealm DID service entry at accepted-at; the public entry fixes only realm_id, controller_did, authorization_ref and the domain-separated requested_scope_digest. The complete scope MUST come from a controller-signed verifier/audience/challenge-bound private disclosure whose digest matches that commitment. Implementation-private deterministic derivation or a service-local Agent row is not protocol evidence.
Managed Agent PCR genesis created_by and notary MUST equal the Agent DID; a controller authoring under delegation MUST be recorded as executed_by and MUST NOT synthesize an Agent signature.

ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / ak.realm.policy_components writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

downgrade_declaration_obligation.policy_declaration_required: Realm create or ak.realm.policy_components MUST explicitly declare ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 before mls_send_pause="advisory" is accepted. Out-of-band deployment config, UI-only labels, or a missing governance_binding GroupContext extension MUST NOT be treated as a valid downgrade declaration.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.service_describe_required: The serving implementation MUST advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and the claimed profile in ServiceDescribe before accepting advisory writes or projecting the Realm as relaxed to a peer/facade.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.binding_profile_required: Every MLS governance_binding emitted for a relaxed Realm MUST carry binding_profile="ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1" and the negotiated reducer_profile. Missing binding_profile, binding_profile="ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1", or an unsupported profile id is a fail-closed mismatch.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.export_marker_required: Sync metadata, snapshots, backups, exports, and interop mapping receipts that summarize the Realm MUST preserve e2ee_relaxed=true and relaxed_window_max_ms. Consumers that observe advisory semantics without this marker MUST assume the downgrade is undeclared and reject new old-epoch decrypt admission.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ak.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window
each federation peer explicitly advertises ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 when it is expected to accept relaxed old-epoch decrypt admission
federation_guard.interop_floor: Full MLS governance binding (ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1) remains the federation E2EE interoperability floor. The relaxed profile (ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1) is a declared downgrade below that floor and is accepted across federation only for restricted/closed deployments that satisfy the bounded-SLA requirements above.

fail_closed_conditions: combination of ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1, compliance-tier E2EE, active Audit Applet Binding, federation_policy=open, or federation_policy=quarantine
restricted federation without peer fanout SLA bounds within relaxed_window_max_ms
governance_binding.binding_profile missing, unsupported, or inconsistent with the Realm downgrade declaration
receiver old-epoch decrypt gap exceeds relaxed_window_max_ms or the absolute hard ceiling of 300000 ms
ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1.description: High-assurance / sovereign / regulated / multi-writer federation profile. Adds mandatory proactive frontier exchange with fail-state semantics on top of the ak.profile.federation_minimal.v1 baseline. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3 and zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §11.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject claim of ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1 if proactive frontier exchange or stale_peer fail-state is not implemented

additional_requirements.frontier_probe_capability_must: Peer MUST expose capability-gated frontier probe endpoint per federation.md §4.5.1.
additional_requirements.proactive_exchange_must: Per federation-visible Realm, per authorized peer, frontier probe interval MUST be <= 3600 seconds.
additional_requirements.fail_state_must: Three consecutive probe failures (peer unreachable or signature failure) MUST mark the peer as 'stale_peer' for that Realm. Separately, an aggregate-commitment difference MUST first be reduced via per-actor challenge/backfill on the intersection of replicated actors, comparing each (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) as a canonical sibling SET of (event_id,event_digest,prev_frontier_digest), not as a single hash. Different event_id/hash siblings at one actor_seq are legal within the event-and-patch.md §2.6 limits and MUST converge by validated set union. A same-event_id/different-digest conflict, an over-limit sibling set, a profile-declared non-joinable sibling conflict, or inconsistent witness payloads for the same complete attestation scope MUST quarantine the affected increments on the FIRST confirmed occurrence and MUST NOT be folded into the three-consecutive-failure window. Raw frontier_root/heads/range-root differences across different scopes, and incomplete subsets of a legal sibling set, MUST NOT alone count as probe failure or witness_disagreement.
additional_requirements.stale_peer_behavior_must: While a peer is in 'stale_peer' state: MUST quarantine its push payloads for the affected evidence scope (no local frontier advancement from that scope); MUST surface state via operator alarm channel; MAY refuse to fanout new Events to that peer. Stale status MUST clear after the original evidence is resolved: the disputed event id/digest or over-fork/non-joinable sibling bucket has an authorized canonical resolution and the peer matches that canonical sibling set, or witnesses for the same complete attestation scope again sign one consistent payload. Scope-different peers MUST NOT be required to have globally identical heads.

ak.profile.auth_server.v1.description: Arkret v1 Auth Server profile. All implementations claiming this profile MUST also implement ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (default interop privacy baseline) — see zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §5.1. ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

additional_requirements.default_claim_must: Any implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile and MUST NOT advertise downgrade switches that disable blind wakeup.

ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notifica.description: Opt-in push gateway profile for deployments that require visible notification fields (e.g. titles, sender labels) in provider payloads. Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1.

additional_requirements.policy_gate_must: Realm policy MUST list the gateway service DID in plaintext_visible_services with visible_notification explicitly allowed.
additional_requirements.device_opt_in_must: Each receiving device MUST record an opt-in flag in its authorization state; absent opt-in, sender / Realm service MUST fall back to blind wakeup.

additional_requirements.payload_minimisation_must: Even when claimed, payload MUST NOT carry message body, DID URLs, cross-Realm stable correlation keys, IP / geolocation, or untyped free-form text.

Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. Requires ak.realm.media_service to declare a multi-focus list with backend type discriminator; defines normative token exchange, session focus selection, participant binding, E2EE key injection via MLS-Exporter label ak.rtc-frame-key/v1, and recording artifact pipeline. Specific backends (livekit / arkret_native) declare an additional sub-profile. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §2 / §3 / §5–§8 and zh/crypto-media/call-state.md §4.

additional_requirements.e2ee_key_source_must: Client binding adapter MUST derive frame keys from Arkret MLS-Exporter with label ak.rtc-frame-key/v1 (length=19 bytes, Context=canonical_json({realm_id, call_id, focus_id, epoch_id, participant_identity, device_id}), KDF.Nh=32 bytes), where participant_identity/device_id come from the verified call roster participant value and participant_binding. Empty Context, missing sender fields, or epoch-only binding MUST be rejected with e2ee_key_source_unauthorised. MUST NOT accept keys from backend cloud key escrow; reject with e2ee_key_source_unauthorised.
additional_requirements.recording_pipeline_must: Backend-generated recording artifacts MUST strand through Arkret authenticated blob upload (media-and-blob.md) with recording_initiator_capability_ref. Direct backend-to-storage paths are forbidden (recording_artifact_pipeline_bypassed).
additional_requirements.recording_key_source_must: Recording artifact encryption keys MUST derive from Arkret MLS-Exporter label ak.rtc-recording-key/v1 with Context=canonical_json({realm_id, call_id, focus_id, recording_id, media_service_id, recording_start_event_id}) and 32 output bytes. Mobile energy saving may batch private sub-seal upload, but MUST NOT relax the public Realm seal cadence.

period_ms.rationale: Public Realm seal commitment cadence is fixed at 5 minutes for this profile.

max_jitter_ms.rationale: Bounded scheduling jitter; implementations MUST NOT encode activity by delaying beyond this window.

empty_batch_commitments.rationale: No-activity intervals still emit commitments to avoid leaking activity frequency.

ak.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept ak.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor ak.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `ak.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor ak.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

Reducer MUST reject any submit payload that also carries effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: Reducer MUST stamp tagged effective_scope on accepted Event envelope and materialized object cell. effective_scope is immutable per-event; later scope_circle_id rebinds MUST NOT re-interpret historical events.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ak.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ak.realm.policy_components or ak.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ak.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ak.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver events with effective_scope.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.

Authorizes durable history-key delivery after the independent membership, device, history-sharing policy, source_authorization_ref, and recipient checks succeed. This explicit high-risk action is not implied by ak.realm.admin.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.
