registry/service-kind-registry.json.description: Canonical service_kind vocabulary. A service_kind names one deployed wire role. This registry is the single source of valid values and per-context eligibility for Service Describe, Realm sync endpoints, Realm join candidates, ServiceRegistrationKey, and the MIMI provider directory. Consumers MUST derive their closed value space from active rows whose valid_in includes the applicable context.
registry_rules: A service_kind id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is lowercase snake_case. Only ids present as rows in this registry exist; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

Value spaces are NOT interchangeable. Each row declares valid_in, the set of contexts the id may legally appear in. A service_kind valid for Service Describe is not thereby valid as a Realm sync endpoint class or as a ServiceRegistrationKey component. Consumers MUST derive their enum from the rows whose valid_in contains that consumer's context, never from the full row list.

Schema enum values for every service_kind selector field MUST be generated from active rows filtered by valid_in; tools/lint_artifacts.py check_service_kind_registry asserts each declared JSON pointer.

service_registration_key is the most restrictive context: it admits only service types that are a standalone deployment owning a service DID under a canonical public base. Adding a row to this context means that service type can hold a service identity and appear in ak.root.identity.service_registration.* operations.

The registry is additive. New service types enter as new rows with their own valid_in set; existing wire values never change meaning. Widening an existing row's valid_in is a registry release, not an implementation decision.

service_kind is a role name, not a product name. Deployment or implementation identifiers (for example a binary called soland or starid) MUST NOT be registered. A single physical deployment MAY fill more than one role, but each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role. Co-located roles sharing a public binding are selected with GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>; each response advertises only that role's exact supported_operations, profiles, authentication metadata, limits and plaintext visibility. Compound service_kind values are forbidden.
This registry governs service_kind selector fields, including the policy source_service_kind attribution field.

contexts.description: Top-level service_kind of a Service Describe document (schemas/service-describe.schema.json). Every deployable role may describe itself.
Service class of a Realm sync endpoint (schemas/realm.schema.json $defs/sync_endpoint).
Service class permitted to receive join-side submissions (schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json). principal_server is the normal candidate; the others only when Realm policy authorizes them.

The service_kind half of a ServiceRegistrationKey (service_kind + canonical public_base). Only roles that own a service DID under a public base belong here. Producers and validators MUST reject any service_kind absent from this context.

Provider directory descriptor of the MIMI interop surface (schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json $defs/provider_directory). Pinned as a const rather than an enum because the context admits exactly one role.

service_kinds.description: Account-owning home server: event ingestion, sync, authz projections, key backup, federation. Also acts as an embedded did:webvh host for the identities it serves, which is why it is valid_in service_registration_key both as a subject and as a Service Identity Provider.
OIDC / token issuance and account lifecycle. Hosts no DID documents of its own; obtains its service DID from an external Service Identity Provider.
Standalone did:webvh registry: DID documents, key logs, receipts, watcher/mirror. Self-hosts its own service DID through its local store.
Event sync surface without account authority.
Discovery ingest/query with anti-enumeration and takedown audit.
Long-term archive storage and retrieval surface.
Cryptographic key backup and recovery surface.
MIMI interop provider facade. Deliberately NOT valid_in service_describe: it names a facade role inside the MIMI provider-directory descriptor, not a standalone Arkret service describing itself.

registry/signature-alg-registry.json.description: Canonical signature algorithm vocabulary for v1 proof alg and raw signature_algorithm fields.
registry_rules: Schema enum values for proof alg fields MUST be generated from active rows' proof_alg only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version.

Schema enum values for raw signature_algorithm fields MUST be generated from active rows' signature_algorithm only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new algorithm requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).
Algorithms not present as active rows MUST fail closed with unsupported_signature_alg on critical proofs.

A reserved hybrid row is a single negotiated verification policy over two independent proof entries, not a new unregistered compact signature encoding. Both components MUST bind the same canonical payload and proof purpose; accepting a stripped single component as hybrid-verified is forbidden.

algorithms.security_note: Classical Ed25519 default signature suite; not post-quantum.
Classical ECDSA P-256 suite for WebAuthn/FIDO2 and PKI interop.

NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA category 3 suite for post-quantum hardening profiles. JOSE/JWK serialization follows RFC 9964: alg=ML-DSA-65, kty=AKP, required pub, optional private seed in priv, and empty ML-DSA context.

activation_requirements: Publish canonical proof-set ordering and duplicate-component rejection rules
Publish anti-stripping vectors proving that both components bind identical canonical payload bytes and proof purpose and that either missing/invalid component fails hybrid verification
Define verifier capability tiers and downgrade display semantics without ever reporting a single-component result as hybrid verified
Publish a new negotiated proof contract release; reserved policy MUST NOT widen frozen proof_alg or signature_algorithm enums in place
algorithms.security_note: Reserved hybrid verification policy. Before activation, the canonical_id itself is not a wire alg and MUST fail closed if presented as one; active Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 proofs retain their independent existing semantics.

data_versions.precis: RFC 8264 derived-property tables at Unicode 6.3.0 plus RFC 8265 UsernameCaseMapped; mapping, normalization, and bidi tables at Unicode 17.0.0

registry/string-profile-registry.json.upgrade_rule: Changing Unicode, PRECIS, UTS #39, or UTS #46 data is a reviewed v1 artifact update. Existing canonical identifiers and signed bytes are never rewritten. UTS #39 upgrades rebuild authority-local derived collision indexes; newly assigned code points are rejected by receivers whose pinned profile does not yet recognize them.

profiles.name: arkret_human_identifier
profiles.canonical_equality: exact prepared Unicode code point sequence
profiles.authorization: may be uniquely indexed but is not a principal identifier
profiles.registration_collision: optional authority-local UTS #39 Highly Restrictive assessment and skeleton index; never canonical equality

profiles.name: arkret_external_string
profiles.canonical_equality: delegated to external standard, DID method, or provider profile
profiles.authorization: Arkret-wide NFKC or case folding is forbidden

registry/vector-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Service-level submit_seal admission covers genesis completeness, current device generation, recomputed roots, predecessor notary authority and non-terminal future-clock deferral.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated at the Event CBA basis; linear archive uses the revocation freshness window, tombstone and concurrent archive fail closed immediately, and restore never rehabilitates a pre-archive basis.

Generated limit-1 / limit / limit+1 matrix for MLS Governance Proof response bytes, logical item bytes, chunk count, collection totals, per-chunk item counts, Merkle proof length and chunk request pinning semantics.

Pins strand update/tracks update to data-plane mv_register target_ref routing while stage.set remains control CAS; data-plane patch effects are recomputed from the single causal_refs base head, remain independent of receiver-local current heads, hold on missing dependencies, and reject missing/multiple bases or non-canonical full post-state effects with effects_payload_mismatch.

Requires every active reducer-input kind to have a complete machine-readable cell contract and pins exact multi-target atomicity, missing/extra effect rejection, and data/control plane-cross-write rejection.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.
Managed-agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.

Controller-owned recovery_public_key backup of managed Agent PCR MLS state, canonical managed-principal binding across public/plaintext/AAD views, pairing recovery-readiness gate, and prohibition on Agent runtime private-key backup or per-Agent human mnemonic.

Native Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.
KeyPackage upload, entry upload, consume, and revoke signatures use one byte-exact operation-id domain plus typed unsigned-request JCS transcript shared by ordinary devices and Native Agent runtimes.

Provision requested_scope is a required immutable global ceiling rather than a grant; narrower key scopes and Realm grants are accepted, while action/resource/mandatory-constraint widening fails closed and provisioning emits no Realm grant.

The public managed-Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.

Applet transaction push source signature anchor: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, source_signature_anchor persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/anchor conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.

Realm create is atomically paired with one immediately following closed-form self founding grant for created_by; missing, widened, third-party, reordered, or post-bootstrap replayed founding grants fail closed without leaving a partial Realm or membership.

Hard quota counters use one logical linearizable authority across every service node: a race for the last slot cannot overshoot, idempotent retries count once, unavailable authority fails closed, and calendar-month periods are rejected.

Temporal action gates are neutral for unrelated actions according to effect, while edit/redact windows use the verified target created_at and the fixed verification time/skew to accept inside the deadline and fail closed outside or on missing target time.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).
resolve_agent_selector failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized selectors return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
resolve_handle failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized handles return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
on_last_read converges by principal-level aggregate contributions and read_trigger_window_ms; offline devices receive expiry stubs and shred keys when they reconnect.
Read-trigger expiry anchors are derived from anonymous aggregate contributions and MUST NOT reveal reader identity or reader counts to other clients or services outside the aggregate boundary.
Duplicate, stale, out-of-order, or cross-bound read-trigger contributions MUST NOT refresh anchors, double-count readers, or expire the wrong message.

Opposite delivery orders at two aggregate services converge through per-token and aggregate min joins; a late earlier valid contribution can only move expiry earlier and can never restore shredded content.
BLAKE3 KAT over fixed UTF-8 bytes plus wrong-prefix, wrong-length, Realm-suite mismatch, and unknown-suite downgrade rejection cases.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) raw detached signature golden vector over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind raw_detached_signature; keygen from a recorded xi seed, signature published as a recorded value that verifiers only verify).

Executable signature negative family for Ed25519, ES256, and ML-DSA-65: bad or truncated signatures, alg/key-type mismatch, malformed algorithm-specific public keys, and detached-profile confusion; every case MUST be rejected with the recorded error_code.

Event Batch Receipt events[] is a canonical set projection sorted by UTF8(canonical_json(item)) with duplicates removed before signing; receivers reject unsorted or duplicate signed wire arrays before digest verification.

Hand-written deterministic CBOR bounds: a definite-length array declaring/carrying 65537 items (generator-described, built by the runner) exceeds the v1 cap of 65536 items per array/map and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) without preallocating from the declared count.

CBOR indefinite-length item (raw bytes bf616101ff, the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1}) violates RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_not_deterministic); locks the SDK's existing indefinite-length rejection on the mls_governance_binding decode path.

CBOR capacity bomb: a byte string header declaring 4294967295 bytes with only 4 bytes of remaining input (raw bytes 5affffffffdeadbeef) MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) before any buffer is allocated from the declared length.

Canonical structure depth cap: a JSON object nested 65 levels deep (generator-described, built by the runner; top-level container = depth 1) exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined) and MUST be rejected (reason_code structure_depth_exceeded) with bounded recursion; a depth-64 control input MUST be accepted.

Federation ingress authentication-failure family (unknown peer / not authorized / target absent) returns indistinguishable responses within one timing bucket per relation.md section 4.5 sampling rules.

service_binding_ref.reducer_profile_digest is computed per federation.md section 4.1.1 from a locally rebuilt content-addressed resolved_digest_input closure; event-kind or schema content mutation changes the digest, canonical key reordering does not, and the receiver rejects the whole batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on divergence.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_p256_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM, profile-gated interop suite): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.
RFC 8265 human-identifier preparation, canonical-receiver rejection, Unicode localparts and Agent slugs, UTS #46 A-label conversion, and dual code-point/octet limits.
UTS #39 skeleton collision state is scoped to one registration authority and one namespace and never defines canonical equality or wire bytes.

Failure-indistinguishability vector covering both the third-party claim endpoint and the invite-locator resolve endpoint; each endpoint's failure classes MUST share one external response shape and bounded timing distribution.

Realm reducer authority for ak.invite.claim: binding_proof and subject_proof signature transcripts, token_commitment match, verification_service_id allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, pending -> claimed membership-proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup are enforced before acceptance.

New passphrase_kdf backup envelopes below the unconditional base KDF floor (Argon2id memory_kib>=65536 / iterations>=3 / parallelism>=1; PBKDF2 iterations>=600000 with allowed digest_algorithm) MUST be rejected.
Key backup retrieval requires a session-bound unlock proof (ak.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1); any binding mismatch or bearer-token-only access fails closed before ciphertext is returned.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST publish fresh init key material, transition the old package to revoked with revocation_reason=keypackage_rotated, and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity, optionality, and profile gating: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported; high_security_organization and sovereign_deployment Realms MUST treat last-resort as forbidden even when the service supports the feature.

Cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim linearization and uncertain-outcome recovery: claim CAS, request ledger and serialized result commit atomically; same source/id/digest replays byte-identically; another digest conflicts without a second claim; query recovers the original outcome.

Peer KeyPackage claim requires both a participant signature bound to the exact request/service destination and the source-service HTTP Message Signature. Destination authority, contact, consent, capability, freshness and Direct Conversation no-last-resort gates fail closed behind one claim_failed surface without inventory leakage.

Concurrent Direct Conversation candidates may claim different single-use KeyPackages, but only the canonical binding winner activates Welcome and consumes; the loser Welcome is quarantined and its unconsumed claim expires to revoked, never published.
MIMI Provider Facade directory claims are accepted only when the Arkret profile and pinned MIMI Internet-Draft versions match.
ak.mimi.room_binding projects a MIMI room onto a Realm or Strand scope without making the MIMI room canonical truth.
MIMI key-material exchange maps to the Arkret KeyPackage claim lifecycle: the claimed package is single-use, becomes consumed after Welcome, and enumeration-sensitive failures share one public shape.
MIMI message/content ingress preserves the original envelope digest and MIMI message identity when mapping into Arkret events.
MIMI identifier queries use private-contact-discovery semantics and do not expose a raw contact graph or reachability proof.
MIMI consent state is isolated from Arkret Realm read/write capability grants.
MIMI proxy download obeys asset privacy policy and does not return direct object-store URLs when provider proxying is required.
Unsupported MIMI draft versions fail closed or require a new profile without silently mutating the v1 reducer profile.

Byte-level complete_control_state_v1 acquisition KAT and SDK verifier mutations for trust anchors, Seal paths and authority, chunk commitments, covered/state/frontier completeness, Event signatures and scope, governance roots, and commit binding fields.

Server materializer KAT that reconstructs the exact bounded four-chunk proof acquisition and returns no partial manifest for unreachable anchors, missing/forked/unverifiable source state, Bottom, visibility denial, or limit overflow.
Byte-level KAT for MLS ciphersuite 0x0001. The in-tree fixture pins the MLS WG corpus commit, every source-file SHA-256 digest, the ciphersuite selector, and fail-closed runner behavior.

Appeal verdict transitions are atomic: overturn requires a same-batch ak.moderation.decision.lift and never resurrects irreversible redaction/key-destruction effects; modify requires both a same-batch lift of the original decision and the replacement decision matched by modify_decision_ref.

E2EE franking proof construction, report submission, and moderator-side verification roundtrip per content-moderation.md section 3.4; digest mismatch or minimal-disclosure violations downgrade or reject the proof.

Multiple active moderation decisions use the deterministic strictest fold instead of being mislabeled as split; require_review is carried by the active decision add and resolution atomically lifts every applicable review gate before current authz is re-evaluated or a stricter replacement is added.

E2EE moderation evidence packages are encrypted to the authorized moderation recipient, target only reported events, carry reporter signature evidence, and reject MLS epoch/history secrets or unrelated plaintext.
Deterministic identity migration preserves every Morph field and canonical JSON value.

Deterministic ak.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ak.transform.rename.v1 rule renames a Morph field and leaves unrelated fields untouched; the post-migration fields projection is canonical-JSON byte-equal across replays.

Deterministic ak.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ak.transform.default_backfill.v1 rule backfills a new optional field with a fixed default while preserving existing fields; idempotent and replay-deterministic.
Deterministic integer-to-number schema widening preserves the JSON numeric value and rejects unregistered widening pairs.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
Expired policy decisions and decisions bound to an older auth/policy/membership frontier MUST be rejected on replay; receivers fail closed and re-request the policy check.
Receivers recompute the RFC 8785 JCS request_canonical_digest of the presented request body; mismatch with the signed bound_to transcript MUST reject the decision.

Explicit response closed loop with runtime addressed/self eligibility and restart dedupe gates, coordinator completion policy, causal request refs, controller validation, fail-closed non-echo handling, and controller-authored durable close control.

Event-fold and local-cache recovery: rebuild from accepted private history, causal folded-frontier validation, no Account Data merge, controller control ordering/sibling resolution, terminal absorption, reassignment, action-by-response-set mapping, and projection schema state invariants.

Containment: plaintext or shared-scope occurrences of exchange binding/control schema ids or exchange_id are hard rejects/invalid; publish output, Account Data, and public/shared surfaces carry no exchange material.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Production current-v1 protected endpoints MUST reject bare Authorization: Bearer unless it is bound by DPoP, an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature, detached JWS, mTLS, or equivalent sender-constrained proof; high-security profiles additionally require RFC 9421 PoP for regular writes / sensitive reads; a PoP signature whose created/expires falls outside the replay window MUST be rejected.

DPoP htu binds scheme, authority, and path: cross-authority/scheme reuse, untrusted forwarding headers, and missing authority are rejected; only a configured trusted proxy with scrubbed headers may reconstruct the external URI.
A DPoP/RFC 9421 grant-binding session key must not reuse bytes, fingerprints, thumbprints, or key identifiers from the long-term device identity key; reuse fails closed.

High-assurance snapshot inclusion-challenge sampling verifies sufficient event_id and actor_seq_range coverage, recomputes the event-set Merkle root, rejects commitment-root mismatch, and rejects silent actor sequence gaps.
Realm-scoped actor frontiers bind realm_id and actor_id, start at actor_seq 0, retain the complete sorted sibling head set, and hash the closed realm_actor transcript deterministically.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ak.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.
Receiver rejects sender_nonce_prefix collision or nonce prefix mismatch.
Receiver rejects repeated per-device AEAD nonce counter.
Receiver rejects pure random 96-bit nonce profile for v1 encrypted attachments.
mv_register join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
counter join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.

ordered_log per-issuer prefix from issuer_seq 0 and issuer equivocation convergence: byte-identical canonical effect.op is idempotent, non-equivalent candidates for the same (cell, actor_id, issuer_seq) resolve to the greatest canonical event_digest compared as decoded octets, causal edges never change the winner, losers stay auditable, and digest collision fails closed.
fsm join: identical (from,to) sibling transitions converge idempotently; same-from different-to siblings return bottom (reject path).

A proposed Seal may include at most one mutually exclusive write to the same bottom=reject cell; apply_seal rejects a violating Seal, while unreachable Seal leaves retain ordinary bottom conflict semantics.

ordered_log issuer sub-chain seq gap yields contiguous_prefix plus pending_gap diagnostics; deterministic recompute after backfill. Equivocation winner selection belongs to ak.vector.lattice.ordered_log_join.v1.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

RSVP derives a typed composite subject from payload event_ref, nullable occurrence, and the explicitly sourced envelope actor_id; causal successors dominate while concurrent mv_register heads remain exposed independently of HLC.

Realm Link FSM: all declared initial states and transitions are accepted, tombstoned is terminal except byte-equivalent replay, undeclared transitions reject with realm_link_invalid_transition, same-basis divergent siblings return bottom, general graph cycles remain valid, and self-reference rejects with realm_link_self_reference.

minimal-metadata and audited E2EE Realms force mention_routing_hint=disabled even when policy declares recipient_registered_token; no sidecar registration, comparison, or persistence occurs and delivery falls back to blind or batch wakeup.

Account and events NDJSON stream trace conformance: catchup completion ordering, cursor-bearing frame closure, dropped-versus-resync branching, and reconnect position advancement are evaluated over complete traces rather than isolated frame schemas.

DeviceMessageEnvelope requires a sender-assigned message_id; unacknowledged byte-identical redelivery executes durable handler effects once, conflicting reuse fails with duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict, and distinct ids remain distinct logical messages.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.

Minimal-metadata author verification binds Event.actor_id and proof.verification_method to exactly one active MLS basic credential / LeafNode signature_key at the envelope epoch, rejects rollback/removal/duplicate/key-mismatch cases, and forbids principal-scoped keys/query fallback.
Audit binding is a closed control-plane FSM: active and suspended may transition as registered, revoked is terminal, and same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.
Audit session stages follow the registered request-authorize-notice-close FSM, permit explicit early close, reject skipped stages, and make close terminal.
Release recipient actor and public key must exactly match authorization and resolve to the same authorized audit actor; substitution fails closed.
Release is bounded by binding activation, first_auditable_epoch, encryption-time eligibility, sealed epoch state, and sealed_by_commit_ref.
Release requires an active binding, unexpired authorization, and accepted session head notice; suspended, revoked, expired, or wrong-stage inputs fail closed.
Same-basis close dominates release, earlier accepted releases must be frozen in close release_refs, post-close releases fail, and ordered_log ordering is deterministic.
Release material output is gated on accepted release plus a profile-valid RYW receipt, matching policy digest, and independent witnesses where attested hardware is claimed.
Byte-level RFC 9420 MLS-Exporter plus ExpandWithLabel KAT for the Arkret ak.history-v1 -> ak.content-v1 content-key chain, including domain/context/epoch negative mutations.
Canonical direct-conversation pair_key KAT over sorted stable subject DIDs and the Realm trust domain, including order-independence and unresolved-pairwise-DID rejection rules.
Direct Conversation Realm profile/discriminator bidirectional schema guard, MLS and closed-join shape, exact-two membership, no-Space policy and main-Strand invariants.
Authored active/retired binding facts and the participant-leave, Realm-terminal and main-Strand-terminal retirement boundary that forces fresh Realm, Strand and MLS identifiers.
Valid candidate filtering, causal supersession and unsigned-byte event_digest maximum selection for concurrent Direct Conversation bindings.
Actor-chain sequence and sibling buckets are Realm-scoped; cross-Realm equal sequence values are independent, while same-Realm conflicting siblings fork and cross-Realm predecessor references fail.
Byte-level reaction routing HMAC KAT covering RFC 9420 exporter derivation, NFC normalization, combining code points, emoji modifiers, and cross-label/Realm/epoch negatives.

Executable RRK durability state-transition vector: all configured recovery recipients are sealed before GC, revoked or undesignated recovery methods fail closed, and threshold authorization does not shrink the eager-seal target set.
Issuer effective-authority and freshness-unknown fail-closed checks for first-issued grants.
Effective grant validity-window intersection rejects empty windows.
Fixed delegation expiry seal prevents rolling renewal and widened downstream expiry.
Delegation cycle rejection across direct, multi-hop, revoke/redelegate and atomic batch variants.
Static depends_on_moderation_state requirement rejects missing or false declarations.
Risk-tier freshness matrix fails closed and keeps unknown low-risk pending outcomes local.
Global cross-grant decision merge prevents any allow from bypassing deny, quarantine or review.
Opaque delivery ack token, monotonic cumulative acknowledgement, binding rejection and lost escalation.
Canonical filter/query-scope cursor binding and cross-scope replay rejection.
Deterministic limited-timeline window-start state basis with safe omission on unresolved bases.
Generated boundary and injected-clock cases for Seal, device message, push, lifecycle and propagation limits.
Request-key canonical body conflict, scope binding, canonical_hash_input and 24-hour retention semantics.
SDK honors Retry-After and never clamps a long server delay into an earlier retry.
SDK pagination continues solely from has_more, independent of item count.
Canonical confusable-check test set and callable SDK utility behavior.
Transition Seal positive path recomputes old and new roots under their respective suites.
Transition Seal root, snapshot, suite, downgrade and post-transition negative matrix.
Generated decoded-cursor, selector canonical JSON, selector term, unknown-field and policy-array boundary cases.

reports/operation-schema-index.json.description: Generated DTO index for registered operations with request_schema_ref/response_schema_ref. JSON Schema files remain the canonical source; this report is a machine-readable summary for SDK/conformance tooling and prose drift review.

schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.title: Arkret Account Data Encrypted Value
schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.description: Principal-private Account Data value sealed client-side. Services validate and store this envelope but never receive the account secret or plaintext.

schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Data Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ak.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). account_data_key keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-key-registry.json. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/client-preferences.md.

account_data_key.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ak.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ak.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.
Caller-supplied opaque payload. Server stores it verbatim; canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption are the client's responsibility. Any JSON value.

schemas/account-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Self-Service Operation DTOs
schemas/account-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations: viewer, account-authentication handoff, identity-binding challenge, register, profile update, and session revocation.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Control proof for binding an already-published DID through account register. OIDC, passkey, or agent authentication alone is insufficient to establish DID control; account-first inception instead uses identity_creation_control_proof.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account-handoff-authentication-proof-v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Public, server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published DID operation, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete did_operation object.

expires_at.description: Handoff expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 1 hour; 1 hour is also the v1 default.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

identity_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into identity_creation_control_proof, adds proof_kind and verification_key_multibase, and signs that complete proof object with signature omitted. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the root-control transcript.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete request did_operation object.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the did:webvh inception operation's parameters.updateKeys[0] identity root. The verifier selects that key from did_operation and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. Signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity-creation-control-proof-v1.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Subscribe Frame
schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ak.self.account.stream.subscribe streaming channel (GET /_arkret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, presence, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ak.self.events.stream.subscribe (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ak:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

device_lists.description: Principal DID sets whose authoritative device list changed or left the caller's visibility scope on `delta` frames.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

notifications.description: Account-private notification projection deltas on `delta` frames. These are not Realm Events and are authorized by the authenticated account context rather than realm_id visibility.

agent_signer_evidence_bundle.description: Bounded signer-evidence sidecar for Agent-authored Events in this delta. Clients MUST verify each evidence item before caching or using it.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ak.self.events.query.scan for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ak.self.account.stream.subscribe` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

notification_kind.description: Closed notification type. Agent runtime approvals reuse the registered notification type `agent`.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ak:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ak.self.device_messages.query.list?after=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ak.self.device_messages.query.list?after=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

preview_only.description: Fallback path of client-sync.md §5.2: when timeline.limited=true and the server does not return realm_sync_entry.state_at_window_start, it MUST set preview_only=true. Clients then render window-start events as preview only.

members.description: Lightweight roster hint derived from effective ak.member.state, effective ak.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

members_limited.description: True when members[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

members_next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the timeline window start. NOT part of state hash, frontier, or causal graph.

collaboration_role.description: Projection-only strong Realm role, emitted only after the server validates the registered Realm profile and discriminator.

subject_id.description: Optional disclosed principal / holder DID for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ak.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ak.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ak.find.directory.query.list_handles_for_subject.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.

schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.title: Arkret Accountability Grant
schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.description: Issuer-signed endorsement used to verify Actor Profile accountable_principal_ids entries. This is the payload contract for ak.identity.accountability_grant.

issuer.description: Principal DID accepting accountability for subject. MUST equal the proof verification method controller.

accountability_scope.description: Display/governance scope only; never grants authorization.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the accountability grant is non-expiring and governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

proof.description: Detached proof by issuer over utf8('ak.accountability-grant-v1\n') || canonical_json(the object with proof omitted).

actor_kind.description: Directory / UX classification only. MUST NOT participate in authorization, reducer acceptance, capability resolution, or any wire-protocol decision: those MUST consult DID + Grant + Constraint exclusively. Implementations are free to use actor_kind for icon selection, directory filtering and presentation, but a wrong value MUST NOT widen or narrow what a principal can do. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and has no DID of its own; its identity is device_id (ak:device:<uuid>) plus a verification method under the owning principal DID. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.personal_agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

status.description: Public projection of the account lifecycle status values defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3. Implementations MAY hide or coarsen this field in projection views, but the wire enum mirrors ak.account.status.

schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Pairing and Agent Operation DTOs
schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.

agent_slug.description: Required controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug. Used only as the right-hand component of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>; not a global handle or authorization subject. Provisioning services MUST issue or update a ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is not a ak:<kind> protocol object id.

pairing_secret.description: One-time CSPRNG pairing secret carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. It is transmitted only in JSON bodies, never in URLs or logs.

device_pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style code carrying 40 CSPRNG bits, bound to a short-lived SAS/QR transcript and protected by a ten-failure lockout.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey DTO. Defined once in public-key.schema.json so device, agent and account surfaces share one definition.

agent_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent axis. Closed enum; only the controller's pause / resume / deactivate lifecycle events change it. It never encodes pairing progress: runtime key readiness is the orthogonal derived agent_runtime_state projection (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_runtime_state.description: Derived, read-only runtime key readiness axis (key-management.md §3.6.1). Services and clients MUST derive it from the same key/pairing facts and MUST NOT write it or treat it as a lifecycle transition target: no active accepted key authorization with an unexpired bootstrap handle is pending_runtime_key; no active key with the bootstrap handle expired is pairing_expired; an active key with no unconsumed replacement handle is ready; an active key with an unexpired replacement handle is replacing. Replacement handle expiry is side-effect free and returns the projection to ready.

realm_id.description: Realm that owns the capability grant cell and therefore the required ak.capability.revoke write surface.

requested_scope.description: Controller-private projection of the required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling captured at provision time, not a grant. Content actions are the maximum actions that later key scopes, Realm-scoped grants, participation or sessions may allow; an omitted action cannot be added later. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants. Receiver authority comes from a valid agent-requested-scope-disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, not this service projection.

requested_scope_digest.description: sha256 digest of the domain-separated Agent requested_scope commitment fixed in the accepted Agent DID ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service entry; the public entry does not contain the complete scope.

pairing_request_id.description: Current unconsumed, unexpired pairing handle. Its presence means pairing is open. Services MUST omit this field and its pairing_mode / pairing_code / pairing_expires_at siblings immediately after the handle is consumed or expires.

pairing_mode.description: Durable branch discriminator for the current open handle. bootstrap is valid while runtime_state is pending_runtime_key / pairing_expired; replacement is valid for any agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) and projects runtime_state replacing while open.

pairing_expires_at.description: Authoritative pairing expiry instant. This projection may preserve RFC 3339 sub-millisecond precision; consumers MUST NOT hash its raw JSON spelling. For ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1, parse this value and normalize expires_at to UTC with exactly three fractional digits (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZ), discarding sub-millisecond precision, before canonical JSON hashing.

agent_pcr_recovery_state.description: Controller-visible recovery readiness for the managed Agent Principal Control Realm. pending means no accepted controller-owned managed-PCR backup exists; ready means the current controller recovery policy and Agent PCR sealed MLS frontier are covered by the active mls_history series tail; stale means an older backup exists but no longer covers the current policy, delegation, Seal frontier, or MLS epoch. Runtime pairing commits require ready at the pre-commit frontier; the accepted key-authorization Event then advances the frontier and makes this projection stale until a post-commit backup tail is accepted.

challenge_proof.description: Structured proof of possession of new_device_pubkey. The Account Authority MUST recompute the signing transcript itself and MUST NOT settle for byte equality against a stored copy. Which transcript applies is fixed by the request shape: with device_pairing_request_id it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 rebuilt from the staged record; with challenge_transcript it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 rebuilt from those inputs plus the Account Authority own gate_audience origin. A mismatched transcript_digest, a transcript name that does not match the request shape, a verification_method other than new_device_pubkey.kid, or a failing signature MUST NOT authorize a device.

device_pairing_request_id.description: Server-mediated short-link request id. Present exactly for the short-link path. The Account Authority MUST atomically authorize only the still-pending staged record whose pairing_code and new_device_pubkey exactly match this request, and MUST verify challenge_proof against the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript rebuilt from that record (device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce, new_device_pubkey digest). A record whose proof does not verify MUST NOT authorize a device.

challenge_transcript.description: Transcript inputs for the to-device path, where there is no staged record for the Account Authority to rebuild from. Present exactly when device_pairing_request_id is absent.

account_device_enroll_request_body.description: Request to the account-authority enrollment service to mint a `service_attested` ak.device.authorize for the calling session's own device (device-lifecycle.md §5.4, key-management.md §5.0.6). Used for the bootstrap / first-device path under the managed-DID model, where no existing device can approve via device-pair.

device_public_key.description: This session's device public key as a did:key multibase string (z6Mk…) or base64.

hpke_key.description: This device’s HPKE sealing public key (multibase). Enters ak.device.authorize.payload.hpke_key verbatim and is covered by the enrollment-authority Event proof (device-lifecycle.md §5.4).

algorithms.description: Canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids the device supports. Enters ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms verbatim (device-lifecycle.md §5.2/§5.4).

actor_seq.description: Founding-device sequence. This endpoint is closed to post-bootstrap devices, so the only valid value is 1.

bootstrap_create_event_id.description: Event id of the root-signed ak.realm.create that immediately precedes the authority-signed authorize in the atomic first-device bootstrap unit. The authority copies it as the authorize Event's sole prev_refs entry.

account_device_enroll_outcome.description: The signed `service_attested` ak.device.authorize Event for the requested device. The account authority does not contact the Principal Server; the caller submits `authorized_event` verbatim to POST /_arkret/self/events.

authorized_event.description: Fully-signed ak.device.authorize Event envelope, carrying enrollment_authority_binding {kind: service_attested}.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Controller-signed private disclosure addressed to the authoritative pairing verifier. The endpoint MUST consume its presentation challenge once, match agent/controller/audience, recompute the public DID commitment digest, and use the disclosed scope for the subset check. It MUST NOT copy the disclosure into authorize_event or any durable/public history.

signing_key_binding.description: Controller-signed minimal public binding created in the same approval action. Its agent/method/raw-key/authorization id and both digests MUST match the runtime request and authorize_event exactly.

authorize_event.description: Fully-signed ak.agent.key.authorize Event envelope approved by the controller or policy engine. It MUST target the Agent Principal Control Realm, carry actor_id equal to agent_id, executed_by equal to the controller DID, authorization_ref equal to the controller delegation DID URL bound by the Agent DID Document, and a proof verification method belonging to the controller or one of its currently authorized devices. Its payload.agent_key_scope MAY be narrower than, but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of, the immutable provision requested_scope; every provision constraint remains mandatory. Required so key activation never depends on an unaudited pairing side effect. authorize_event.event_id is the pair operation idempotency identity.

agent_runtime_approval_request_body.description: Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize and submitting agent_key_pair_request_body. The service computes ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 from agent_id, pairing_request_id, verification_method, public-key digest and attestation digest. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable binding: same-binding retry is idempotent and refreshes the full request while retaining approval/notification ids; a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_controller_projec.description: Authenticated controller-safe projection of the pending runtime key request. It is deliberately not agent_runtime_approval_request_body and not agent_key_pair_request_body: pairing_code is exposed only by the sibling controller key_state field, while requested_scope_disclosure and authorize_event do not exist until the controller approves. Services MUST also omit any other runtime secret or unregistered field.

agent_human_approval_error_details.description: Closed error.details shape returned by ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant when an agent_key_proof request needs out-of-band controller approval. The enclosing ErrorEnvelope.error.code MUST be claim_required. The agent runtime MUST NOT be given CAPTCHA, OTP, browser-login, or other interactive human challenge material.

agent_runtime_approval_status_request_bo.description: Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id, pairing_code, and agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. A record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and stop polling after pairing expiry.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome.description: Controller-decision status for an agent runtime key pairing request, projected on the two orthogonal axes (key-management.md §3.6.1). While the polled pairing is still open, runtime_state is pending_runtime_key (bootstrap) or replacing (replacement) and approval_request_id echoes the pending request, if any. Once the controller has approved this exact pairing, authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding fields are present; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime, not as its own approval. Presence and digest match of those fields — never status or runtime_state alone — is the approval signal. An open bootstrap pairing whose pairing_expires_at has passed is reported with runtime_state pairing_expired; an expired replacement handle reports runtime_state ready with no authorized fields for this request, which the runtime treats as expired.

agent_provision_request_body.description: Two-phase controller-authored Agent provisioning. prepare validates prerequisites and allocates the Agent DID and Agent PCR id without publishing durable Agent state. The controller recomputes requested_scope_digest, uses the Arkret SDK to author the closed controller-signed Event pair, and returns the same allocation in commit. The service validates and admits both Events before publishing the pairing handle. Provisioning never creates an Agent profile, key authorization or Realm capability grant.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Service-allocated Principal Control Realm id for the new Agent. It is distinct from the controller PCR in provision_events.

requested_scope.description: Required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling, not a grant. Later key scopes, Realm grants, participation selections and session requests MAY narrow it but MUST NOT exceed its actions, resource selectors or mandatory constraints. An omitted action can never be added later. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants.

agent_provision_events.description: Closed, controller-signed fan-out plan authored through the Arkret SDK. Both envelopes use the authenticated controller as actor_id and its PCR as realm_id, carry ordinary Event proofs, and pass the standard Event admission pipeline. The selector source_refs binds the accountability Event id.

controller_realm_id.description: Authenticated controller PCR in which both provision Events must be authored. Present only while status is awaiting_controller_events.

requested_scope_digest.description: Digest of the complete immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID accepted inception history; only this digest, not the complete scope, is public. The client MUST recompute it from its submitted scope, returned agent_id and authenticated controller DID.

agent_renew_pairing_request_body.description: Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an agent runtime. The service issues a fresh one-time pairing_request_id + pairing_code; every previously issued pairing handle for the agent becomes permanently unresolvable. runtime_state pending_runtime_key / pairing_expired re-opens bootstrap pairing; any agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) performs runtime replacement re-pairing: lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until the new controller-signed authorization with an exact supersedes set is accepted atomically, and completion preserves the lifecycle intent (an active agent needs no resume). deactivated rejects.

agent_renew_pairing_outcome.description: Fresh pairing handle plus the current managed Agent PCR recovery projection. Unlike initial provisioning, pcr_recovery can already be ready or stale; pair commit still requires ready.

requested_scope_digest.description: Unchanged digest of the immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID binding; the complete scope remains controller-private.

agent_pairing_bootstrap.description: One-time bootstrap material handed to a personal agent runtime after provisioning. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret.

agent_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for short agent pairing handoff links. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.self.agent.pause Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service submits these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and never synthesizes an Agent-authored Event. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

Closed ak.self.agent.resume Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. Its sidecar_exposure_ack, when present, must equal the request sidecar exactly.

Closed ak.self.agent.deactivate Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service admits it only after every required key and capability revocation has been accepted. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

key_revocation_events.description: Closed ak.agent.key.revoke Events covering every currently active Agent key. Each Event is authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation; its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly. Empty is valid only when the authoritative projection has no active Agent key. Events sharing a (realm_id, actor_id) chain MUST appear in causal submission order.

capability_revocation_events.description: Closed controller-authored ak.capability.revoke Events covering every currently unrevoked grant held by the Agent, each written in the Realm that owns that grant and carrying an optional payload.reason exactly equal to the request reason. Empty is valid only when the authoritative projection has no unrevoked Agent grant. Events sharing a (realm_id, actor_id) chain MUST appear in causal submission order.

grant.description: Complete signed Realm-scoped grant. In addition to JSON Schema validation, admission MUST verify its subject/issuer/Realm bindings and that every action and resource is covered by the requested_scope disclosed in the verifier-bound private sidecar; provision constraints remain mandatory. A violation fails with agent_grant_exceeds_requested_scope.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Fresh, controller-signed private ceiling disclosure addressed to the grant admission verifier. It is transaction evidence only and MUST NOT be copied into the Realm-scoped grant or Event history.

agent_sidecar_context_ref.description: Canonical Strand-level Sidecar context identity. Track and Message coordinates are exchange/projection sub-keys and MUST NOT participate in private Strand reuse.

control_frontier.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted control refs that materialize the Sidecar and exact desired backing membership.

current_controller_device_ready.description: True only when the authenticated controller session device is the accepted genesis creator device or has completed matching Welcome and KeyPackage consume evidence.

desired_agent_ids.description: Eligible owned Agent principals in the Sidecar desired access set. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_id and is not duplicated here.

effective_agent_ids.description: Agent principals whose backing-scope membership and current MLS readiness have completed. Reducer/service MUST enforce this set is a subset of desired_agent_ids. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_id and is not duplicated in either Agent array.

agent_participation.description: Native Agent participation bits. The provision-derived ceiling maps reply to ak.message.create plus ak.reaction.add, accept_third_party_mention to ak.event.read, and act_on_behalf to ak.message.create plus applicable controller-approval/accountability constraints.

selection.description: Controller selection. Every true bit MUST be allowed by both the immutable provision-derived ceiling and the deployment/Realm/Circle/Strand governance ceiling.

ceiling.description: Effective admission ceiling after intersecting the immutable provision-derived ceiling with the deployment/Realm/Circle/Strand governance ceiling.

effective.description: Final participation after intersecting ceiling with controller selection.

schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.title: Arkret Agent Requested Scope Disclosure
schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.description: Controller-signed, verifier-bound private disclosure of a managed Agent's immutable requested_scope. This object is authorization evidence, not a grant. It MUST travel only over an authenticated confidential presentation/operation channel and MUST NOT be written to a public DID Document, durable Realm Event, public registry, pairing code, or notification. The verifier consumes request_id/challenge once, validates the short presentation window, verifies a current controller proof, recomputes requested_scope_digest against the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, and then applies the Agent ceiling subset rules. After successful one-time admission, an implementation MAY retain the object only as encrypted verifier-private evidence keyed by (agent_id, requested_scope_digest, verifier_did, audience).

request_id.description: Identifier of the signed ak.identity.presentation_request or an equivalent authenticated private challenge request. It is single-use at verifier_did.

requested_scope.description: Complete immutable Agent ceiling disclosed only to the bound verifier. It does not grant any action or resource.

requested_scope_digest.description: MUST equal sha256(canonical_json({agent_id, controller_id, kind:'ak.agent.requested_scope_commitment.v1', requested_scope})) and the digest in the accepted-at Agent DID service binding.

verifier_did.description: Exact verifier named by the presentation request. A different verifier MUST NOT accept or forward this disclosure as its own evidence.

audience.description: Exact origin, service audience, or canonical operation audience requested by verifier_did.

challenge.description: Verifier-generated unpredictable challenge. The (verifier_did, request_id, challenge) tuple is single-use; replay MUST fail closed.

expires_at.description: Presentation admission expiry. expires_at MUST be later than issued_at and expires_at - issued_at MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds. It does not change the immutable ceiling; it only bounds disclosure delivery/replay.

proofs.description: At least one current controller proof. The proof verification method MUST belong to controller_id or one of its currently authorized devices. payload_digest is sha256(canonical_json(this object with proofs omitted)); detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.agent-requested-scope-disclosure-proof-v1', payload_digest, agent_id, controller_id, verifier_did, audience, challenge, verification_method, created_at}).

schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Selector Claim
schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.description: Signed claim binding a controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug to an agent principal DID. It powers @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> compose-time resolution without making the agent carry a public handle.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID that owns the selector namespace.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped slug used as the right-hand side of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

issuer.description: DID that signs this selector claim. It is normally controller_subject; a delegated issuer MUST be authorized by controller_subject and bound in source_refs or proof evidence.

issuer_service_id.description: Service DID that served or vouched for this selector claim when distinct from issuer.

visibility.description: Disclosure boundary for selector resolution. Restricted/private claims require audience and requester policy checks before returning subject.

audience.description: Audience binding for restricted selector disclosure, such as a Realm ID, verifier domain, or service DID.
