claim_scope.description: Optional scope such as realm_id, organization_id, purpose, allowed_operations, or disclosure policy tags.

source_refs.description: Optional refs to accountability_grant, actor profile, provisioning, delegation, or revocation evidence.

schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Event Exchange Binding
schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.description: Closed typed binding that ties one Sidecar-scoped Message event to one source-routed exchange. It is legal only inside the encrypted metadata plaintext (message_metadata.sidecar_exchange_binding) of an event whose effective scope is the Sidecar backing Circle. It is the only normative way to declare an explicit user-facing response; any event without a valid binding, with an unknown role, or with a schema mismatch MUST be treated as non-echo. See zh/models/sidecar.md §7.2.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity copied verbatim from the request binding. It is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT appear in shared events, plaintext metadata, publish output, push previews, notifications, public telemetry, account-data keys, or any public/shared surface.

role.description: Closed disposition. request: the controller's private request event itself. user_facing_response: an Agent response the controller MAY echo after validation. internal: exchange-scoped Agent collaboration/tool output that MUST NOT be echoed. Consumers MUST fail closed to non-echo on any value not listed here.

request_event_id.description: Accepted Event id of the private request event of the same exchange. Event id is the only canonical reference form; Message ids MUST NOT be used here.

completes_exchange.description: Optional coordinator completion request; legal only with role=user_facing_response. It does not itself make the exchange terminal. A controller device validates the actor against coordinator_assignment_event_id and, on success, authors a durable ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event with action=close.

coordinator_assignment_event_id.description: Request Event id for the initial coordinator assignment, or the accepted reassign_coordinator control Event id. Required only when completes_exchange=true.

request_context.description: Write-once exchange identity carried only on role=request. It is the single durable source of the projection's write-once fields: any controller device rebuilding the projection copies these values verbatim, so cross-device bit-identity is anchored to the accepted request event instead of device-local state. Forbidden on response/internal roles.

completion_policy.description: Closed v1 completion policy. Only the effective coordinator may ask the controller to close the exchange.

coordinator_agent_id.description: Initial coordinator. It MUST be one of addressed_agent_ids. It MAY be omitted only when addressed_agent_ids contains exactly one item, in which case that sole item is implied.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Control
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.description: Closed plaintext encrypted inside the payload of ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. Only the Sidecar controller may author this durable private-Strand Event. It is the sole source of coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.

basis_event_ids.description: Canonical UTF-8 byte-order sorted maximal causal heads of exchange facts observed when this control was authored. The outer Event refs MUST contain role=after for every id, and the request Event must be causally covered.

response_event_ids.description: Exact canonical set of validated user-facing response Event ids causally covered by basis_event_ids. Required for every terminal action, including an empty array.

failure_reason_code.description: Required only for action=fail. close/cancel derive empty-response failure codes controller_closed_empty/controller_cancelled.

coordinator_agent_id.description: New coordinator for action=reassign_coordinator. It MUST be addressed by the request and eligible at authoring time.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Projection
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.description: Disposable controller-device-local cache for one source-routed Sidecar exchange. Every field is a deterministic fold of accepted private-Strand Events. This object is not wire truth, is not Account Data, is never merged across devices, and may always be deleted and rebuilt.

terminal_event_id.description: Controller-authored ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event that produced complete or failed.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity; it is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT be copied into shared events.

folded_frontier.description: Local cache coverage. event_ids are the canonical sorted maximal causal heads of all contributing accepted exchange facts. event_set_digest commits to the canonical sorted complete contributing Event-id set. max_hlc is display/cache metadata only and never proves causal dominance.

schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..title: Arkret Agent Sidecar View State
schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..description: Controller-private encrypted account-data plaintext for one hosted Sidecar context. It changes only private presentation and never mutates either Strand, Track, access, read state, notifications, search, or event ownership.

schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar
schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.description: Controller-owned private AI workspace bound one-to-one to (realm_id, controller_id). Agent Sidecar is a first-class protocol object, not a Circle profile or editable membership container. Its backing_circle_id is reducer-derived and system-managed solely as the private delivery/MLS scope. See spec/v1/zh/models/sidecar.md.

backing_circle_id.description: Reducer-derived system-managed private delivery/MLS scope. Raw ensure callers MUST NOT supply or mutate this field; the service-built canonical ak.sidecar.create payload MUST materialize it. Ordinary Circle APIs MUST NOT expose or manage the referenced Circle.

encryption_profile.description: Agent Sidecar is always protected by an independent MLS group; plaintext fallback is invalid.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence Operations
schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.description: Authenticated, anti-enumeration query shapes for portable Native Agent signer evidence.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence
schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.description: Portable, closed evidence used to verify a Native Agent Event signer at an accepted authorization frontier without consulting the ordinary device directory.

seal_lineage.description: Complete duplicate-free predecessor closure from the authorization Seal through the freshness observed frontier. Consumers validate every Seal id/signature and derive authorization interval/freshness ordering from graph reachability; opaque frontier strings are never compared lexically.

schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.title: Arkret Agent Signing Key Binding
schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.description: Controller-authored minimal public binding between one Native Agent signing verification method, its raw Ed25519 key, and the accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event. Private pairing, scope, PoP, attestation, and capability material MUST NOT appear in this object.

agent_key_id.description: Exact payload.key_id of the bound ak.agent.key.authorize Event; used with agent_id to derive the authoritative agent-key cell subject.

expires_at.description: Present iff the authorization itself declares expires_at. JSON null is forbidden.

key.description: Base64url without padding of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes.

schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Applet Edge Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Applet edge and bridge operations.

applet_transaction_request_body.description: Body for ak.edge.applet.command.transaction. Transport-layer requirements are mandatory but not body fields: RFC 9421 Signature/Signature-Input, Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID, Content-Digest, Idempotency-Key, received_at audit metadata, and a persisted source_signature_anchor. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 7.3.1.

source_service_id.description: Must exactly match the Source-Service-ID header and the signed source-service-id component. It identifies the source service only; each Event still requires independent actor/applet/capability signature verification.

schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Applet Ghost Actor Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. An installed Applet service / bridge submits a complete service-signed accountability Event and delegated Ghost profile Event for one external user. The Principal Server MUST re-check their applet / service / realm / namespace / capability bindings and commit the pair atomically; it MUST NOT mint either proof with a server notary key.

ghost_actor_provision_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. ghost_actor_id MUST fall inside the actor namespace declared by the applet_id registration; protocol / tenant / external_user_id identify the external principal being mirrored.

accountability_grant_event.description: Complete ak.identity.accountability_grant Event signed by the installed Applet service DID. Its nested accountability proof MUST be signed by the same service identity.

profile_event.description: Complete ak.profile.create Event for ghost_actor_id, delegated and signed by service_id. authorization_ref MUST identify the active ak.applet.ghost.provision capability grant and refs MUST bind the accountability Event.

ghost_actor_provision_outcome.description: Response for ak.self.applet.ghost.command.provision. Carries the durable event refs the Principal Server atomically accepted (or re-confirmed on an identical idempotent replay). authorization_ref is the active Applet provisioning capability grant used by the submitted pair; the accountability grant is not an authorization grant for later Ghost actions.

schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.title: Arkret Applet Install Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.install.command.preview, ak.self.applet.command.install, and ak.self.applet.command.revoke. The InstallPlan body itself is defined in applet-install-plan.schema.json.

proof.description: Required when revoke_mode includes delegated session revocation in production. The proof signs the canonical ak.gate.account.command.revoke_session transcript reconstructed from the active applet install selector.

schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet InstallPlan
schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.description: Canonical plan returned by ak.self.applet.install.command.preview and recomputed by ak.self.applet.command.install before commit. plan_digest is calculated over the canonical InstallPlan object with plan_digest omitted.

schemas/applet-package.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Package
schemas/applet-package.schema.json.description: Controller-signed package used to install an Applet. The package is a distribution object, not Realm history truth and not a grant. Principal Server / authz service derives ak.applet.registration and capability grants during ak.applet.install.

package_id.description: Distribution identifier only. Not a grant subject.

proof.description: Controller DID detached proof over the canonical package or derived registration object. proof.payload_digest MUST equal package_digest (proof over canonical package) or the derived registration object digest. Empty object is invalid.

detached_proof.description: Controller-DID detached-JWS proof shape, aligned with event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof (the generic non-Event signed-object proof). Non-Event objects bind their canonical payload via payload_digest; Event proofs MUST instead use event_digest and event_proof.

webhook_auth.description: HTTP message signature verification seal for transaction push. key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used as the app/bridge->arkret inbound source signature anchor; its DID part MUST equal service_id and it is bound to the effective registration_epoch. accepted_algs pins the acceptable RFC 9421 signature algorithms.

key_ref.description: DID URL under the Applet service_id. For app/bridge->arkret inbound transaction push, Signature-Input keyid MUST equal this value. Node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID key from Source-Service-ID, not this field.

endpoint_policy.description: Supported Applet API endpoints and their auth requirement.

limits.description: Service-side resource hints derived into the registration manifest.

ghost_policy.description: Ghost Actor support and accountability template. enabled defaults to false semantics; an explicit boolean is required.

delegation_policy.description: Delegated native-user acting request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

e2ee_policy.description: MLS join request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

widget.description: Optional Applet widget declaration. When present, it MUST validate ak.schema.applet_widget_declaration.v1.

schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.title: Arkret Applet Registration Epoch Transcript
schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.description: Closed, normalized security transcript hashed to produce an Applet registration_epoch. The hash input is the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-applet-registration-epoch-v1\n followed by the JCS bytes of this object.

schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.title: Applet Widget Declaration
schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.description: Closed declaration for an Applet UI widget origin, CSP, scoped token capability scope, and consent gate.

widget_origin.description: HTTPS origin only: scheme, host, and optional port; no path, query, or fragment.

csp.description: Content-Security-Policy that the host client MUST enforce for the widget document.

token_scope.description: Maximum capability scope for the short-lived widget token.

schemas/applet.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Protocol Object
schemas/applet.schema.json.description: Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ak.applet.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier. MUST be either a DID or the registered typed-id form ak:applet:<uuidv7>. Arbitrary opaque strings are not valid wire identifiers; bridge-specific aliases belong in namespace / external_ref fields.

service_id.description: DID of the service that hosts the applet runtime (used by registration / discovery).

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot at registration time (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.title: Arkret Audit Release Attestation
schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.description: Structured remote attestation for an audit applet release service under ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1. This is the wire form behind audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware: a verifier MUST be able to validate release-service measurement, attestation chain trust root, attestation key freshness, operator identity, Realm/Circle binding, and audit release policy digest without trusting prose declarations. The attestation binds the controlled output path for ak.audit.release; it does not add the applet to MLS and does not grant realtime plaintext access. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6.

realm_id.description: Realm this attestation evidence is valid for. Verifier MUST require realm_id to match the MLS Welcome / Event Envelope Realm being joined or audited; identical audit_policy_version_digest values across Realms do not make evidence portable.

audit_service_actor_id.description: DID of the audit release service / applet actor whose controlled output path this evidence attests. MUST match the recipient_audit_actor_id or service actor accepted by the active ak.audit.applet_binding.

service_id.description: Operating service DID hosting the audit applet or release service. MUST match the service_id in the active ak.audit.applet_binding / ak.audit.release chain.

family.description: Attestation family. 'software_test_only' is for conformance fixtures and MUST be rejected by deployments declaring attested_hardware assurance.

measurement.description: What is actually running inside the enclave / HSM / equivalent controlled output boundary. Verifiers compare this measurement to the measurement allowed by the active audit applet binding and release policy.

code_digest.description: Hash of the audit release service binary / image / policy bundle that the enclave loads. MUST be reproducible (signed by vendor build pipeline).

policy_version.description: Release service's compiled-in policy version (e.g. semantic version or git tag). MUST appear in the Realm/Circle audit binding's allowed release-service policy versions at issued_at.

report_data.description: Optional REPORTDATA-equivalent that binds the attestation to the release service public key or output-encryption key. Lowercase hex encoding of a 32–64 byte byte-string (pattern enforces an even hex length: each byte is exactly two hex characters; total 64–128 hex characters). Receivers MUST validate this binding when present.

attestation_chain.description: Ordered attestation evidence chain: leaf attestation (signed by the enclave) → intermediate (e.g. PCK certificate, AK certificate) → root (vendor attestation root certificate). Each item is base64url-encoded DER / CBOR per platform format. Verifier MUST validate signature chain and trust the root against the Realm-declared trust root list.

attestation_key.description: The attestation public key (extracted from the leaf of attestation_chain). ak.audit.release proofs and RYW receipt validation MUST be cryptographically bound to this attested output path when audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware.

verification_method.description: DID URL the receiving verifier uses to resolve attestation_key. MUST live under audit_service_actor_id's DID Document or a DID Document explicitly delegated by the active audit binding. Fragment characters are constrained to RFC 3986 unreserved + `:` for stable key ids. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

validity.description: Validity window of THIS evidence. Verifier MUST reject evidence outside the window. For evidence presented under audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1), the verifier MUST reject evidence whose window (expires_at - not_before) exceeds 90 days; Realm/service policy MAY cap it lower. Evidence with a longer window MUST be treated as an elevated-risk signal and rejected by profile policy rather than silently accepted.

revocation.description: How the verifier should check whether attestation_chain leaves / intermediates have been revoked. Required when platform supports revocation (sgx_pccs CRL, tdx PCS, etc.).

operator_did.description: DID of the controlling organization actually operating this enclave / HSM. This intentionally keeps the _did suffix because it is raw external DID material being compared against service_id and Realm policy, not a protocol actor_id/principal_id alias. MUST match what the Realm policy lists as the allowed audit operator. Distinct from service_id when the operating org is different from the technical service DID (e.g. service hosted by org A on behalf of org B).

audit_purpose.description: Why this audit applet release service may output audit material. MUST match the active binding/session purpose; mismatch → audit_purpose_mismatch.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Same definition as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.audit_policy_version_digest — fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id, trust_domain, audit_binding, release_policy, release_window_policy, activation_frontier_digest, first_auditable_epoch} at the Realm policy frontier at issued_at. Lets verifier O(1) check that the policy classification this evidence was issued under matches the current binding/session state, cannot be reused across Realms, and cannot retroactively expand eligibility for already encrypted messages. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile. See encoding.md §2 (canonical JSON) and audited-e2ee.md §6.

proofs.description: Detached signature(s) over the canonical evidence bytes (all fields except `proofs`), signed by operator-controlled keys distinct from the enclave attestation key. Two-key separation: the enclave attests its own measurement; the operator separately attests that this enclave is the one they intend to deploy.

schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Audit RYW Receipt
schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.description: Read-Your-Writes receipt issued by an Events API node, witness, or peer Principal Server confirming that a ak.audit.release or other audit envelope has reached accepted state. Required by ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 and ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 before an audit applet release service may output wrapped material or plaintext evidence (see zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6). The audit_assurance_class field MUST match the active Audit Applet Binding; mismatch fail closed.

trust_domain.description: Deployment trust domain for the Realm at the receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST require this to match the current receive context and the enclosing audit Event Realm context before using audit_policy_version_digest.

realm_operator_organization.description: DID of the Realm operator's ultimate controlling organization at this receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST derive and verify it from the Realm service/operator DID control chain; it is not a self-attested label. For federation_witness_attested, every witness controlling_organization MUST be distinct from this value and from any organization under the same ultimate controller.

kind.description: Attestation kind derived from witnesses[]. 'federation_witness_attested' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains >= 2 distinct entries (distinct issuer.did AND distinct controlling_organization AND distinct verification_method), each issuer.did is listed by Realm policy under audit.ryw_witnesses[], and no witness controlling organization equals or is ultimately controlled by realm_operator_organization. 'single_source' MUST be used iff witnesses[] contains exactly 1 entry. Any mismatch between 'kind' and the witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / Realm policy listing / operator independence MUST be rejected with audit_receipt_invalidated. The value is externally verifiable from the witness list, not a self-claim.

issuer.description: Service DID of the witness that produced this receipt.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the key the witness used to sign (e.g. did:web:...#key-1). MUST be distinct from other witnesses' verification_method values for 'federation_witness_attested' to be valid.

controlling_organization.description: DID of the organization that controls the witness. This value is not self-attested: verifiers MUST resolve issuer DID Document and confirm its controller / service ownership chain matches controlling_organization. For 'federation_witness_attested', all witnesses' controlling_organization values MUST be pairwise distinct and MUST NOT equal the audit actor's controlling organization or realm_operator_organization, including common ultimate controllers.

attested_at.description: Time at which this witness attested. Receivers MAY use the latest attested_at across witnesses as the effective receipt timestamp.

witnesses.description: Externally verifiable list of witnesses attesting that the audit_event_id+audit_event_digest reached accepted state. The 'kind' field MUST be derivable from this list per the rules in §4.1.1.

witness_attestation.description: Witness attestation block. The receipt's independence is externally verifiable from the witnesses[] list rather than self-claimed via a single enum. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1 / §4.1.1.

audit_assurance_class.description: Audit assurance class propagated from the active Audit Applet Binding. attested_hardware = ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 (TEE/HSM/enclave controlled release required). disclosed_policy = ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 (process-only disclosure, NOT cryptographically enforced). Release services MUST propagate the binding-declared value verbatim; receivers MUST fail closed when this field disagrees with the binding/policy state at the receipt's frontier.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Canonical hash of the Realm-bound audit release policy tuple from the receipt frontier. Computed as fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id: <id>, trust_domain: <trust_domain>, audit_binding: <object>, release_policy: <object>, release_window_policy: <object>, activation_frontier_digest: <hash>, first_auditable_epoch: <n>}. Lets verifiers atomically check that the receipt's claim matches the active binding/policy at this frontier without replaying events and prevents cross-Realm reuse or retroactive expansion of identical policy text. MUST match the receipt frontier's policy state and ak.audit.release.eligibility_proof; mismatch MUST fail closed (audit_receipt_invalidated). Required field — missing receipts MUST be rejected to prevent silent policy drift. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile.

recovery_reason_code.description: Optional machine-readable code, set only when this RYW receipt covers a ak.audit.accessed Event emitted via the Late Key Recovery path (see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5 and zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1). Payload value, not an error-code-registry reason_code. Used by audit projections to distinguish late-key-triggered accesses from first-access reads. When absent, the receipt covers a normal (first-access) ak.audit.accessed Event.

schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Authorization Operation DTOs
schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.description: Closed response DTOs for authorization query operations that need operation-specific list envelopes.

schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret AvailabilityReceipt
schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed holder commitment that Event bytes are available until retention_expires_at. Digest membership roots do not prove byte availability; CBA models availability independently.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical AvailabilityReceipt bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Blob Operation DTOs
schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for blob service operations whose wire shape is not the full blob metadata resource.

content.description: The binary blob content part in multipart/form-data. This field is not JCS-canonicalized as JSON; content_digest covers the bytes.

key_ref.$comment: MUST stay identical to encrypted-envelope.schema.json#/properties/key_ref and encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.1. Closed MLS group-binding object; not an opaque string.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, single ciphertext_digest
streaming chunked AEAD form (STREAM / OAE2): per-segment AEAD, per-object random nonce_prefix

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes
content hashes use content_digest with an algorithm prefix

realm_id.description: Owning Realm for authorization, asset privacy policy enforcement, retention and GC. MAY be omitted only for global / cross-Realm service blobs (e.g. avatar previews) explicitly authorized by the Blob Service deployment policy.

schemas/bottom.schema.json.title: Arkret Bottom Diagnostics
schemas/bottom.schema.json.description: Structured diagnostic for cell join values that resolve to bottom (⊥). Surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined under the current CBA query basis. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.1.

kind.description: Why the join produced bottom. 'conflict' = concurrent cas_register / fsm divergence on safety-critical cell. 'invalid_transition' = fsm op violates allowed_transitions. 'missing_dependency' = event ref to absent / failed prior event. 'unauthorized' = event issuer lacks capability for the op (verifier-side). 'notary_split' = multiple Seal leaves diverge on next-seal authority. 'schema_error' = lattice op or value violates declared cell schema.

cells.description: Cell ids participating in the bottom diagnostic. Multi-cell when a multi-cell Control Move atomically failed across linked cells.

event_ids.description: Reducer-input event ids whose effects (or precondition checks) produced this bottom. Empty allowed when the cell's bottom is structural (e.g. notary cell schema_error) and not tied to a specific event.

seal_view.description: Seal leaves and control frontier under which this bottom was observed. Diagnostics MUST pin this so the receiver can reproduce the join without ambiguity.

state_root.description: Control-plane state_root at observation time (recompute from Seal leaves). Optional when the diagnostic is emitted before state_root is computable.

heads.description: When kind=conflict and the cell's lattice exposes multiple candidate heads (mv_register, or_set with conflicting tag values), the candidate values. Implementations MUST NOT pick a winner from this array; it is for UI / audit only.

details.description: Free-form structured details specific to the diagnostic kind. Producers SHOULD use stable keys per kind (e.g. invalid_transition: from/to/expected_transitions; schema_error: schema_id/violation_path). Receivers MAY display but MUST NOT use for authorization decisions.

escalated_at.description: When the cell first crossed Realm.bottom_escalation_after_ms. Absent when within the grace window. Implementations SHOULD raise an out-of-band notification to admins / recovery governance once set.

until.description: RFC 8984 LocalDateTime interpreted in the calendar event timezone; no UTC offset or Z suffix is allowed.

schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.title: Arkret Call Recording Artifact
schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.description: Canonical metadata for a call recording artifact after it has entered the Arkret blob pipeline. It binds the blob, recording start event, MLS exporter recording key context, retention policy and deletion audit surface without introducing a ak:recording or ak:artifact storage key.

content_digest.description: Digest published by the Arkret blob pipeline for the stored recording object.

ciphertext_digest.description: Digest of encrypted recording bytes. This MUST match encryption.ciphertext_digest and the referenced encrypted blob metadata.

produced_by.description: Media service DID or recorder service DID that produced the encrypted recording bytes.

recording_initiator_capability_ref.description: Capability grant reference proving the recording was initiated by an actor holding ak.call.record.

deletion_audit.description: Present only after a delete attempt is scheduled, completed, or blocked. The referenced erasure receipt remains the durable audit proof.

call_recording_retention.description: Retention contract for a recording or transcript capture artifact. retention_expires_at is the earliest deletion time; deletion_trigger declares the only accepted purge cause; audit_lock blocks all purge paths until an audit-grade release is accepted; consent_confirmed records the required second client-side capture confirmation.

retention_expires_at.description: Earliest time the artifact MAY be purged. Absent = governed by retention_policy_id. MUST NOT be in the past at write time.

audit_lock.description: When true the artifact is under audit / legal hold; purge MUST be rejected with legal_hold_active until the lock is released by an audit-grade action.

consent_confirmed.description: Records that the second client-side confirmation required before recording or transcript capture was obtained.

trigger_event_id.description: Durable event that caused this delete attempt, when the trigger is event-backed.

erasure_receipt_ref.description: ak.audit.erasure_receipt event, ak.schema.erasure_receipt.v1 object, or digest proving the deletion outcome.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

capability_action_registry_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical capability-action-registry.json snapshot used to expand aggregate_admin actions. Required by the reducer whenever actions[] contains an action whose registry row has event_mapping_kind=aggregate_admin; optional and audit-only otherwise. Unknown or unavailable snapshots fail closed with capability_registry_basis_unavailable.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Delegation control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='delegation_control' and max_delegation_depth (see capabilities.md §10). Top-level delegable is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no delegation_control constraint the grant is not delegable (equivalent to max_delegation_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

not_before.description: Top-level grant validity start. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_not_before = max(not_before, every temporal.not_before present).

expires_at.description: Top-level grant validity end. Authorization evaluates this together with temporal constraints: effective_expires_at = min(expires_at, every temporal.expires_at present). Delegated grants MUST not extend beyond the parent's effective_expires_at.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

proofs.description: Detached grant proofs sign canonical_json({context:'ak.capability-grant-proof-v1', payload_digest, issuer, subject, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag, not a wire field. payload_digest is the canonical hash of the grant body with proofs removed.

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/cell) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.

schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Circle administration operations (ak.self.circle.*). Each operation builds a canonical ak.circle.* Operation and routes it through the standard local accept pipeline; the durable Circle object model is circle.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

circle_view.description: Circle projection row returned by create/get/lifecycle operations. Field set mirrors circle.schema.json; reducer-managed fields (mls_group_ref, state, members, created_at) are read-only outputs.

profile_ref.description: Create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it; profile-specific Circles expose it so clients can apply mandatory filtering.

mls_group_ref.description: Reducer-derived MLS group reference; present only when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'.

member_count.description: Exact count of active Circle members. Present only when the caller is an active Circle member; directory-only previews MUST omit it and use the privacy-bucketed preview contract instead.

viewer_membership.description: The caller's own Circle membership state when one exists.

members.description: Active Circle member DIDs (strict subset of parent Realm.members). Empty after tombstone.

circle_create_request_body.description: Actor-supplied fields for ak.circle.create. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT appear.

membership.description: Target canonical ak.circle.member.state membership value. Defaults to join. Joining another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member; knock requires join_rule=request.

note.description: Reducer-emitted reason code on Ignored / Rejected, or unsupported-feature note while MLS scope rotation is not wired end-to-end.

circle_lifecycle_request_body.description: Optional body for ak.self.circle.command.archive / ak.self.circle.command.restore / ak.self.circle.command.tombstone. The target circle is taken from the path.

schemas/circle.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle
schemas/circle.schema.json.description: Circle — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, and delivery/query/projection boundary. It may be plaintext delivery-only or MLS-backed depending on encryption_profile and parent Realm policy floor. It does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. Circle is NOT a principal Group; principal-set capability narrowing belongs on Group / capability constraint / resource selector. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

profile_ref.description: Optional create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it. Profile-specific creation paths MUST persist their registered profile id. Agent Sidecar is a separate ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object and MUST NOT be represented by this field.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_count. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

join_rule.description: How an actor becomes a Circle member. 'public' lets any active parent-Realm member self-join; it does not make the Circle globally discoverable. 'knock' requires the application/approval flow. 'invite' requires Circle admin add or invite.

history_visibility.description: Circle's own history visibility. Effective visibility MUST NOT be wider than the parent Realm's policy floor. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6.

content_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local content encryption floor. When omitted, the Circle inherits the parent Realm's content_encryption_floor. Effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, this field). May only tighten, never widen, the parent Realm floor, and the effective floor is a one-way ratchet: once e2ee_required has been accepted it MUST NOT be lowered back to allow_plaintext (reducer rejects with content_encryption_floor_downgrade). e2ee_required is only meaningful when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'; a Circle with encryption_profile='none' MUST keep allow_plaintext. See zh/models/circle.md §7.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local metadata encryption floor (binary, symmetric with content_encryption_floor: allow_plaintext | e2ee_required). When omitted, the Circle inherits parent Realm's metadata_encryption_floor. May only tighten, never widen, parent Realm floor; the effective floor is a one-way ratchet (reducer rejects a lowering write with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade).

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped agent participation ceiling for this Circle: { native_agent: { reply, accept_third_party_mention, act_on_behalf } }. When omitted, inherits the parent Realm ceiling. Each bit MAY only tighten, never widen, the parent ceiling (reducer rejects a widening write with agent_participation_ceiling_widen); it is further tightened by any inner Strand ceiling. The legacy flat three-bit shape is invalid v1 wire. See zh/models/circle.md field table.

encryption_profile.description: Circle content encryption profile. create-locked. 'none' means plaintext delivery/query/projection isolation only and is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor allows plaintext. 'mls_rfc9420' means the Circle owns an independent MLS group and MUST NOT derive its keys from the Realm-default MLS group.

mls_group_ref.description: Reducer-derived reference to the independent MLS group bound to (realm_id, circle_id). Present only when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'. Populated by ak.circle.create reducer; not actor-supplied on wire.

state.description: Circle lifecycle state. v1 defines active, archived, and tombstoned only; Circle has no independent freeze or destroy state because parent Realm freeze/destroy applies at the Realm boundary.

short_name.description: Human-facing short name. Unique per (realm_id, short_name) case-insensitive — reducer-enforced. Prefix SC- is reserved for reducer-managed Agent Sidecar backing Circles; ordinary Circle create/update MUST reject it with reserved_circle_short_name.

color_token.description: Color token from the spec-controlled palette. Clients MUST map token -> theme color (light/dark/high-contrast) consistently across devices; clients MUST NOT reassign tokens.

schemas/common-ids.schema.json.title: Arkret Common ID and Reference Definitions
schemas/common-ids.schema.json.description: Shared ID and reference pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.

schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Consent Cell Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for holder-private consent cells. Only holders/controllers receive consent_cell_view; peer request submission returns an opaque outcome and never exposes cell state.

active_grant_dots.description: Currently-active grant dots (not yet observed/revoked, within validity window).

consent_update_request_body.description: Body for grant / revoke. The holder is taken from the path; the authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

consent_request_request_body.description: Body for opaque contact/consent request submission. peer_did defaults to the authenticated actor and MUST equal it. Holder existence is deliberately not a precondition visible to the caller.

consent_request_outcome.description: Constant anti-enumeration response. Missing holder, denial, rate-limit drop and quarantine acceptance all return this exact shape; no cell id, state, dots, timestamps or expiry are exposed.

schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Contact and Direct Conversation Operation DTOs
schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for contact lifecycle operations and direct conversation resolver.

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

invite_consent_grant_ref.description: Optional. Event ref of the peer-issued ak.consent.grant (scope invite or any) granting the holder the right to send Realm/Strand invites to this peer. Present only when granted_to_me includes invite or any. Used by the holder as consent_grant introduction evidence to invite this contact into a Realm without a locator URL.

peer_service_id.description: Optional. Principal Server service DID hosting the peer, when known (e.g. learned from a cross-Principal-Server contact delivery). Lets the holder address responses/invites to the peer's home server. Omitted for same-Principal-Server contacts.

message.description: Optional free-text greeting carried into contact_requested_payload.message. NFC-normalized per canonical encoding rules.

recipient_service_id.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When target is hosted on a different Principal Server, the requester MUST supply the target home service DID so the issuer-side server federates the signed ak.contact.requested fact via ak.peer.contacts.command.submit. Omit for same-server requests.

introduction_evidence.description: Optional evidence explaining how the requester found the target. Required by the issuer-side Principal Server when it federates a first-contact request to another Principal Server; if omitted, the server MUST derive compliant evidence or treat the request as explicit_address.

requester_service_id.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When the original requester is hosted on a different Principal Server, the responder supplies the requester home service DID so the accept / reject fact is federated back via ak.peer.contacts.command.submit. Omit for same-server responses.

full_peer_revoke.description: When true, UI/admin explicitly requested revocation beyond contact-managed grant dots.

block_peer.description: When true, additionally add the peer DID to the holder invite_receive_policy.denied_subjects, so future invite delivery from this peer is dropped and disclosed opaquely. Models a hard block ("拉黑") on top of contact tombstone.

peer_service_id.description: Optional cross-Principal-Server addressing (see contact-and-direct-conversation.md §4.1). When contact (the peer) is hosted on a different Principal Server, the holder supplies the peer home service DID so the issuer-side server federates the signed ak.contact.tombstoned fact via ak.peer.contacts.command.submit. Omit for same-server tombstones; when absent the issuer falls back to the peer recorded peer_service_id on the stored contact row.

peer_claim_request.description: Requester-signed peer KeyPackage claim returned from the preceding remote_keypackage_claim authoring step. It is accepted only for create=true and must exactly match the reserved draft.

claim_authorization_draft.description: Immutable peer claim request and explicit service/trust-domain transport binding reserved by the source service. The participant signs the canonical authorization transcript and resubmits draft.request plus requester_authorization as peer_claim_request.

materialization_draft.description: Immutable client-side materialization plan issued only after a KeyPackage claim is final. The participant submits realm_event, founding_grant_event, and peer_member_event as the atomic ordinary-Realm bootstrap unit, then uses the founding grant's ak.capability.grant authority to submit main_strand_grant_event before main_strand_event. The participant authors real MLS genesis/add-commit/Welcome objects from claimed_keypackage, then submits the remaining post-bootstrap Realm Events before binding_event in the participant PCR. No service may synthesize participant Event proofs or MLS ciphertext.

unsigned_direct_materialization_event_ba.description: Shared envelope shape of every unsigned draft Event in a direct_conversation_materialization plan. proofs MUST be empty: the service issues an authoring draft and never signs on behalf of the participant. Each draft slot narrows this base to exactly one kind via its own role-closed definition; the six slots are NOT interchangeable.

unsigned_direct_realm_create_event.description: Bootstrap unit event 1. payload.object MUST be the Direct Conversation Realm object (ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1) whose id equals this envelope realm_id and whose created_by equals actor_id.

unsigned_direct_founding_grant_event.description: Bootstrap unit event 2: the creator founding ak.capability.grant required by models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5. It MUST immediately follow realm_event in the same atomic batch. The nested grant is delivered in authoring state with grant.proofs empty; the participant device generates the issuer-attestation proof per authz/capabilities.md section 3.0.1. No service may synthesize it.

unsigned_direct_peer_member_event.description: Bootstrap unit event 3: the peer member join written by the creator under the founding grant. It is the bootstrap initial member carve-out of governance/join-policy.md section 4, not a third-party member_add, and it is exempt from seal_basis per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 5.

unsigned_direct_main_strand_grant_event.description: Post-bootstrap least-authority grant authorizing only ak.strand.create for the creator in this Direct Conversation Realm. The nested grant is returned unsigned and MUST receive a participant device issuer-attestation before the outer Event is signed.

unsigned_direct_main_strand_event.description: Post-bootstrap main Strand create. Submitted after the MLS genesis/add-commit/Welcome objects authored from claimed_keypackage.

unsigned_direct_binding_event.description: Final binding event submitted in the participant PCR after the Realm side is complete.

schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.title: Arkret Poll Content Block
schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.description: Canonical content-block schema for ak.content.poll and ak.content.poll.response.

poll_answer.description: One visible answer option. answer.id values MUST be unique within a poll; reducers and conformance vectors enforce that cross-item constraint.

poll_body.description: Poll configuration. max_selections is validated against responses by reducers because JSON Schema cannot compare a response to its referenced poll message.

schemas/cross-signing-publish.schema.jso.title: Arkret Cross-Signing Publish
schemas/cross-signing-publish.schema.jso.description: Payload content for ak.cross_signing.publish (schema_id ak.schema.cross_signing_publish.v1). Publishes the (PSK -> {SSK, USK}) binding to the principal control stream. Each subordinate key MUST carry a binding signature produced by PSK over a canonical signing input that includes trust_domain — see device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. MUST match the receiver's current trust_domain and enters the PSK binding transcript so a publish from deployment A cannot be replayed into deployment B.

generation.description: Monotonically increasing publish generation. Each ak.cross_signing.reset MUST increment by 1. Receivers MUST reject publishes whose generation is <= the currently accepted generation.

expected_previous_generation.description: CAS precondition for the current accepted cross-signing generation. Initial publish uses 0. Reducers MUST accept only when this equals the current accepted generation and generation == expected_previous_generation + 1.

kid.description: Verification method identifier within the principal's DID document or key log.

alg.description: JOSE-style algorithm identifier; MUST be present in the protocol algorithm registry.

verification_method.description: PSK kid that signed this subordinate key's canonical signing input.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over the canonical 'ak.cross-signing-bind-v1\n' + canonical_json input, including trust_domain. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

schemas/cross-signing-reset.schema.json.title: Arkret Cross-Signing Reset
schemas/cross-signing-reset.schema.json.description: Payload content for ak.cross_signing.reset (schema_id ak.schema.cross_signing_reset.v1). High-risk operation that retires the current (SSK, USK) generation and requires one of four kinds of proof — see device-lifecycle.md §14. A successor ak.cross_signing.publish MUST follow within 24h.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Enters every proof's canonical transcript so the same proof bytes cannot be replayed from deployment A into deployment B (different trust_domain → different transcript → signature verification fails as invalid_signature). Receivers MUST check this matches their own trust_domain before doing any signature work, returning cross_domain_replay_rejected otherwise. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 and zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.6.

reset_event_id.description: Typed event_id of the Event Envelope carrying this reset payload. MUST equal the enclosing Event.event_id. Binding it into proof transcript prevents wrapping the same proof bytes into a different Event shell. Mismatch MUST be rejected as reset_event_id_mismatch.

previous_generation.description: The generation being retired; MUST equal the currently accepted publish generation.

new_generation.description: Generation that the successor ak.cross_signing.publish will use; MUST equal previous_generation + 1.

revoked_device_ids.description: Devices known compromised or lost. Reducer atomically revokes them and requires MLS leaf removal/rekey. Required for compromise and device_loss resets.

did_url.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Fragment characters constrained to RFC 3986 unreserved + `:` for stable key ids. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The schema only encodes wire shape; key-class verification is normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4. `verification_method` MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method (zh/identity/key-management.md §3.2 — e.g. `did:webvh:...#ak_principal_signing_v1` or the DID method's equivalent control key), and MUST NOT be the self_signing_key or user_signing_key being retired by this reset.

verification_method.description: Principal-grade control-key verification method. MUST NOT reference the SSK/USK being reset (§14.4 rule (a)).

recovery_unlock_proof.description: Recovery-key unlock proof. The cryptographic strength comes entirely from `signature` — possession of the recovery private key is proven by verifying `signature` over the §14.1 canonical input under the public key bound to `recovery_secret_ref` in the recovery session's snapshotted accepted recovery_policy. A DID Document-only recovery key is not authoritative. `unlock_commitment` is a wire-integrity / debug binding only: it is a deterministic public hash that the receiver re-computes from material already in the event. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) recovery_secret_ref MUST resolve to a recovery_keys[] entry that was authoritative at issued_at; (b) signature MUST verify against that entry's public key; (c) unlock_commitment MUST equal SHA-256(utf8('ak.cross-signing-reset-unlock-binding-v1\n') || recovery_secret_ref || unlock_binding_input_bytes), where unlock_binding_input_bytes is the §14.1 canonical input with proof_body excluding both signature fields and unlock_commitment. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(c) fails.

recovery_session_id.description: Recovery session id from the §15 device recovery state machine (step 2). Carried inside the recovery_unlock proof body so it enters the §14.1 canonical transcript via proof_body, giving the proof a self-contained freshness binding that does not depend on external recovery state. Receivers MUST reject a recovery_unlock reset whose recovery_session_id does not match an active recovery session for principal_id at issued_at. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 / §15.

recovery_secret_ref.description: Stable verification_method identifier of a recovery_keys[] signing entry inside the recovery session's snapshotted accepted recovery_policy (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-proof-1`). MUST match an entry that was authoritative, unexpired and unrevoked at issued_at; a DID Document-only key or recovery share id is invalid.

unlock_commitment.description: Deterministic wire-integrity hash bound to (recovery_secret_ref, reset content). Receiver-computable from public material; does NOT prove possession of the recovery secret — `signature` does. See §14.4 rule (c) for the exact derivation and the self-reference exclusion.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Cryptographic and quorum verification are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) every signature MUST verify against the public key of an authorized, non-revoked device in the principal's current device set at issued_at, over the §14.1 canonical input; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid, deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the current `recovery_policy.device_quorum.k` (or equivalent published quorum policy) at issued_at — a smaller threshold supplied by the issuer MUST be rejected as `failed_precondition` reason=`cross_signing_reset_quorum_below_policy`. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(d) fails.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently published recovery_policy device-quorum k (recovery_policy.device_quorum.k); receivers MUST cross-check (see description rule (d)).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; reducer-side verification requires deduplicated valid signatures count >= threshold per description rule (c).

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by principal_signing, recovery_unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_id. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the reset payload and reject cross-domain attestations as cross_signing_reset_recovery_service_attestation_domain_mismatch.

schemas/cursor.schema.json.title: Arkret Cursor
schemas/cursor.schema.json.description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'after', 'before', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Arkret-Wait-For'). Wire form is always ak:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §8 / §8.3.1): v1 core uses the stateful opaque-handle form only — body is {v, purpose, issued_at, expires_at, h} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) tuple. Server-side handle lookup IS the integrity check; there is no inline transcript binding to verify on the client side. Servers MUST reject unknown / expired / cross-binding handles with cursor_integrity_invalid.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'after' on /account/subscribe, 'before' / 'after' on ak.self.events.query.scan and ak.peer.events.query.scan (including its service-to-service federation pull form GET /_arkret/peer/events?before=<cursor>), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Arkret-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). The handle binding (resolved server-side) carries positions for 'stream' or target for 'barrier'; the wire body does not.

issued_at.description: Cursor issuance instant in the canonical Arkret UTC millisecond profile.

expires_at.description: Cursor expiration instant. MUST be in the future when issued. TTL upper bounds (expires_at - issued_at): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days).

h.description: Server-side opaque handle. The issuing server MUST bind this handle to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) and MUST be able to revoke it. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding); minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically (base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet). Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. Handle lookup IS the integrity check — there is no MAC or signature to verify inline. This is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. Servers SHOULD keep the handle → binding map durable across process restarts (see client-sync.md §12.1): a memory-only table is still integrity-correct (unknown handles fail closed) but turns every restart into a fleet-wide forced full resync. For production-grade deployment profiles (small_team / organization / high_security_organization / sovereign_deployment / sovereign_enclave / isolated_sovereign_network) this durability plus TTL GC is a MUST per client-sync.md §12.1; only personal_node keeps it at SHOULD.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore. In v1 core there is no `_mac` / `_sig` integrity field — handle lookup IS the integrity check — so the underscore namespace is private to the issuing server. `_mac` and `_sig` themselves are explicitly excluded by the top-level `not` clause: a cursor body carrying either MUST be rejected (encoding.md §8.3).

schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.title: Arkret Delivery Binding Stale Error Body
schemas/delivery-binding-stale.schema.js.description: Canonical error body for the delivery_binding_stale federation signal. A receiver that has accepted a member delivery-binding rebind handover returns this when a sender still delivers under the pre-handover binding. Carries new_recipient_service_id, handover_frontier, and a verifiable handover_proof binding the accepted ak.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move. High-risk redirect: senders MUST cross-verify handover_frontier via a non-destination witness and validate handover_proof (reachability, seal-frontier finalization, allowed_recipient_services membership, trust-domain guard) before following. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.1 and registry/error-code-registry.json (delivery_binding_stale / delivery_binding_handover_proof_invalid).

new_recipient_service_id.description: Target Principal Server service DID after rebind. MUST be within the current effective allowed_recipient_services / delivery binding policy allow set.

handover_frontier.description: Handover frontier F that triggered the rebind. MUST equal handover_proof.frontier.

handover_proof.description: Verifiable proof binding the accepted ak.member.state{membership=join} rebind Move that produced the new binding.

actor_id.description: Rebind target principal; MUST equal target_principal_id.

witness.description: Event digest / state witness / inclusion proof of the rebind Move. Sender MUST verify reachability in the Realm Event graph and policy, and that the Move is seal-frontier finalized.

message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id).

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. Pair with sender_device_id for cross-signing binding.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

device_proof.description: Optional per-device transport proof block. Schema-open extension point keyed by device-lifecycle.md §5.2 cross-signing binding (typical sub-fields: cross_signing_binding, sender_device_key_fingerprint, signature_over_content_digest). MUST NOT replace MLS authentication of the enclosing envelope; included only when an additional out-of-band per-device transport binding is required (e.g. SAS verification, dehydrated-device proofs). Receivers MUST treat unknown sub-fields as opaque and MUST NOT trust device_proof in isolation.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. SHOULD be the device hpke_key or the ephemeral key already established by the bound SAS verification transcript.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {message_id, kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

realm_key_request_content.description: ak.realm_key.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §13.2). A read-eligible receiver asks a concrete key source to evaluate policy and, if authorized, deliver historical history_secret material via durable ak.realm_key.share or an equivalent policy-authorized recovery path. Carries no key material itself.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: Recipient device HPKE public key (KeyPackage init key or equivalent) the key source MUST verify as an authorized device key for recipient_principal_id before sealing history_secret.

requested_source_kind.description: Source class this request targets. key_backup is intentionally excluded because it is retrieved via ak.self.keys.backups.command.unlock.

target_source_ref.description: Concrete source this request is routed to: a device_id for own_device / verified_member_device, or a service DID for archive_node / recovery_service. Service-targeted reuse of this to-device kind is valid only when ServiceDescribe exposes a concrete recipient_device_id / queue target for the service DID; otherwise the service MUST expose a dedicated operation.

target_principal_id.description: Principal that owns target_source_ref (the to-device queue is addressed by (principal, device_id)). Carried so the relay routes directly without scanning Realm members to reverse-lookup the device's principal.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the requested key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}.

policy_digest.description: Optional requester-observed policy digest hint. The key source MUST recompute the effective policy from accepted history before sharing.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional requester-observed membership frontier hint. The key source MUST recompute recipient eligibility from accepted history before sharing.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style device-pairing code bound into a same-principal authorization transcript. It is short-lived, one-time, and locked after ten failed submissions.

new_device_pubkey.description: Canonical PublicKey for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. kid MUST be the requesting ak:device:<uuidv7> id and the key material MUST be carried in key. The legacy {kid, alg, public_key} spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected. The object is later consumed verbatim by ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

challenge_proof.description: Fresh requesting-device proof of possession over the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 transcript, which commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. The receiving authorized device MUST recompute the transcript from the values it displays to the user and verify the signature before treating the requesting device as pairable; it is later submitted verbatim to ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.

schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). These endpoints are unauthenticated: staging mints an account-less pending record, and resolve/status exchange the short handle for pairing material without binding or granting anything until an authenticated device authorizes the pairing.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the challenge proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

device_pairing_to_device_challenge_trans.description: Transcript inputs the authorizing device forwards for the to-device pairing path, where no server-staged record exists. The Account Authority rebuilds the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 signing input from these values plus its own gate_audience origin and the digest of the submitted new_device_pubkey; it MUST NOT accept a client-supplied gate_audience, because substituting its own origin is exactly what blocks cross-Account-Authority replay. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2.

transaction_id.description: Verification transaction id of the ak.key.verification.request that carried this pairing challenge.

expires_at.description: Expiry the proof committed to. The Account Authority MUST reject an elapsed expires_at before it verifies the signature.

device_pairing_challenge_proof.description: Proof of possession of the staged new_device_pubkey, bound to the server-minted pairing challenge. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1\n") || canonical_json({client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2. The proof can only be generated after staging returns, because it commits to server-minted values that do not exist at stage time.

transcript.description: Names the exact signing transcript. ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 is the server-mediated short-link path and commits to {client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}. ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 is the to-device verification path and commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. A verifier MUST select the member set from this discriminator and MUST NOT accept a proof whose transcript name does not match the path it is verifying.

verification_method.description: MUST equal new_device_pubkey.kid. The proof is verified with the staged new_device_pubkey and with no other key.

transcript_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical challenge transcript bytes. The verifier recomputes it from its own staged record and rejects a mismatch before checking the signature.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts pending_authorization, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the challenge proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Result of staging a device-pairing short-link record. It returns the full server-minted challenge material the new device needs to build the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 proof. pairing_code is a short human-carryable secret; both device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code are the query credential for the resolve/status endpoints and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query string.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Pairing material handed to an already-authorized device after resolving a device-pairing short link. It carries the server-minted challenge material so the authorized device can recompute the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript and verify the proof it received out of band from the new device. It does NOT carry the proof itself: the staging surface is unauthenticated and never sees it. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret; the authorized device still drives ak.gate.account.command.pair_device to complete authorization.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still open, state is pending_authorization. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

schemas/did-continuity-proof.schema.json.title: Arkret DID Continuity Proof
schemas/did-continuity-proof.schema.json.description: Payload profile for ak.did.proof continuity transitions, including cross-method did:web -> did:webvh upgrades.

trust_domain.description: Receive-context trust domain covered by every signature_chain payload_digest. Verifier MUST reject a proof whose value differs from current_receive_context.trust_domain.

audience.description: Optional list of intended verifier scopes (e.g. Realm IDs, registry service DIDs, or trust-domain identifiers) that this continuity proof is bound to. When present, verifiers outside the listed audiences MUST reject the proof to prevent cross-protocol / cross-Realm replay of an account migration claim. When absent, the proof is broadcast-style and verifiers fall back to checking signature_chain + transfer_proof only. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §4.2.

principal_id.description: DID of the principal that produced this signature-chain link. The signing key is named by verification_method; this is the responsibility subject.
