verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Fragment is REQUIRED. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

payload_digest.description: Hash of utf8('ak.did-continuity-proof-v1\n') || canonical_json(proof object, including trust_domain and audience, with signature_chain[].payload_digest and signature_chain[].signature omitted).

seq.description: Monotonic DID method log sequence for this DID. seq=0 is the inception entry and MUST NOT carry prev_event_digest; every seq>0 entry MUST carry prev_event_digest equal to the previous accepted entry's head_event_digest.

operation.description: Normalized operation kind. The DID method-specific raw operation object is carried in operation_body; this field is the reducer/verifier discriminator.

prev_event_digest.description: Hash of the previous accepted key-log entry. Required for seq>0 and forbidden for seq=0.

head_event_digest.description: Self digest of this entry: canonical_digest of the entry with `proofs` and `head_event_digest` removed (canonical JSON per encoding.md §2, wire hash form per §3.1). The next accepted entry's prev_event_digest and identity receipts both reference this value. Normative byte-level definition: zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.1.3.

operation_body.description: DID method-specific raw operation object. This is not a generic JSON Patch; validation dispatches by DID method and operation kind.

proofs.description: Controller proofs over this entry. payload_digest = canonical_digest(entry without `proofs`); the detached proof signs the canonical binding object {context:'ak.did-key-log-entry-proof-v1',payload_digest,did,seq,verification_method,created_at,domain?,audience?} defined in zh/identity/identity-did.md §4.4 and proof-context-registry.json. verification_method MUST be a controller key authorized for this operation at the previous accepted entry's state; the registry host MUST NOT substitute its own key.

schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Directory Operation DTOs
schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, agent selector lookup, and push webhook registration operations.

verified_badge.description: Public organization verification badge suitable for directory preview rendering.

member_count.description: Public exact organization member count when the organization directory policy permits exact counts.

realms.description: Public Realm ids linked to this organization when the organization directory policy permits Realm fan-out preview.

realm_count.description: Count of public Realm ids linked to this organization.

directory_resolve_handle_request_body.description: Resolve a canonical handle. For restricted handle claims, requester / proofs / claim_presentations / audience / realm_id are authorization inputs; services MUST use indistinguishable denial for anonymous or unauthorized restricted, revoked, rate-limited, and not-found cases.

controller_handle.description: Canonical controller handle string without the @ sigil.

controller_subject.description: Controller principal DID resolved from controller_handle and verified against the selector claim.

subject.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

directory_list_handles_for_subject_reque.description: List currently visible handle claims for a subject. The service MUST apply the same visibility, audience, requester proof, rate-limit, and indistinguishable-denial rules as resolve_handle; absence of a returned handle is not proof the subject has none.

psi_ristretto255_element.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 32-byte RFC 9497 ristretto255 element. Decoders MUST additionally reject non-canonical group encodings and the identity element.

psi_voprf_proof.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 64-byte RFC 9497 batched DLEQ proof (two 32-byte scalars).

psi_derived_prefix_16.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the v1 fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix.

psi_response_padding.description: ASCII SP padding. The origin serializes the complete response with RFC 8785 JCS as UTF-8, omits Content-Encoding and applies no content coding, and chooses this value so the HTTP entity body Content-Length exactly equals the phase bucket declared by ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

psi_batch_id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7 typed batch id correlating the blind and match rounds of one logical PSI query. It is unique within the authenticated device credential and is bound to canonical request digests for replay-safe quota charging.

psi_blind_request_body.description: Round 1 of the §6.2 two-round OPRF set-membership PSI: the client submits blinded connection identifiers. PSI window quota is enforced here; denial is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard ErrorEnvelope, never a 200 outcome.

ciphersuite.description: Exact RFC 9497 ciphersuite identifier. The ak.private_contact_discovery.v1 profile fixes the separate RFC protocol mode to modeVOPRF (0x01).

blinded_elements.description: Client-padded batch. Cardinality MUST equal ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.batch_item_count; real and dummy elements are indistinguishable to the provider.

psi_match_request_body.description: Round 2 of the §6.2 two-round PSI: the client submits one fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix for every element of the admitted blind batch, preserving cardinality and order. An admitted batch_id MUST NOT be quota-denied at this phase.

derived_prefixes.description: Each entry is the fixed 16-byte prefix of the corresponding unblinded VOPRF output digest. Cardinality and order MUST equal the admitted blind request.

directory_private_contact_discovery_requ.description: Two-round OPRF set-membership PSI request (zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §6.2/§6.3); the phase field discriminates the round.

invite_consent_handoff_stub.description: Minimal invite/consent handoff stub allowed beside PSI match bits. It declares state or next-step guidance only; it MUST NOT carry a contact request token, reachability proof, profile, membership, or read grant.

state_digest.description: If present, MUST be salted per requester/session or replaced by an audience-bound opaque token per consent-model.md §6.2.

psi_blind_outcome.description: Round 1 success outcome: VOPRF evaluations over the fixed-size submitted batch plus one RFC 9497 batched proof. evaluated_elements MUST be same-length and same-order as the request's blinded_elements.

evaluation_proofs.description: Exactly one RFC 9497 batched VOPRF DLEQ proof covering the entire fixed-size evaluated_elements array. The client verifies it with the public key for this key_epoch from ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

derived_prefix_bytes.description: Fixed byte length of every round-2 derived_prefixes entry in the v1 profile.

psi_match_outcome.description: Round 2 success outcome: fixed-cardinality hit bitmap (dummy-padded to the provider-enforced batch_item_count). Per-target conditions (nonexistent, undiscoverable, per-target policy-denied, OPRF mismatch) are encoded as unmatched bits and MUST NOT surface as distinct fields, codes, or timing (§6.4 Class A).

handoff_stubs.description: Optional minimal invite/consent handoff stubs. If present, MUST have the same cardinality as hit_bitmap, with dummy stubs (e.g. state="unknown") at unmatched positions so the field shape does not reveal hits.

directory_private_contact_discovery_outc.description: Two-round PSI success outcomes, discriminated by phase. PSI quota denial is NOT an outcome shape: it is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard ErrorEnvelope at the blind phase, padded to the success-path size bucket and delay class (§6.4 Class B).

trigger.description: Expiry anchor trigger. on_first_read / on_last_read are driven by private read cursor or policy-allowed receipt inputs through anonymous aggregate trigger contributions; expiry metadata MUST NOT expose reader identity.

grace_ms.description: Additional local projection / key-drop grace. Does not extend the Realm policy maximum lifetime.

read_trigger_window_ms.description: Maximum wait window for on_last_read aggregate contributions. If omitted, implementations MUST use max_ttl_ms. This window is metadata-only and MUST NOT expose reader identity or unread reader count.

schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.title: Arkret Draft Sync Account Data
schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.description: Encrypted account-data plaintext shape for ak.profile.draft_sync.v1.

aad_visibility_event_id.description: Normative discriminator for event id visibility in aad. hidden forbids aad.event_id and aad.event_ref_digest; routing_digest requires aad.event_ref_digest and forbids aad.event_id; opaque_id requires aad.event_id and forbids aad.event_ref_digest.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification. See encryption-and-audit.md §4. Ratchet tree material MUST NOT be carried in the per-message envelope; group state changes strand through ak.mls.genesis / Welcome / Commit events.

key_ref.description: MLS group binding hints. Closed object: privacy-sensitive AAD must not be smuggled through here. Forbidden in v1: ratchet_tree, leaf_node, group_info (these MUST NOT be replicated per-message).

schemas/ephemeral-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Ephemeral Broadcast Envelope
schemas/ephemeral-envelope.schema.json.description: Wire shape for broadcast ephemeral signals — ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, ak.call.signal. These signals have wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json: they MUST NOT carry CBA reducer fields, MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root or actor_seq, MUST NOT enter reducer state, and MUST NOT be submitted via ak.events.submit. All broadcast ephemeral signals require a device_id and detached proof so receivers can verify actor source authenticity without trusting relay attribution. They are carried on dedicated ephemeral channels (sync subscribe live stream, presence/typing fanout, call signaling channel) and are dropped at TTL. Point-to-point to-device signals (ak.key.verification.*) use device-message.schema.json instead — they have a sender+recipient pair and do not match this broadcast shape. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §2.3 (wire-scope reject rule) and zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5 (ephemeral channel transport).

kind.description: Ephemeral signal kind. MUST be one of the four broadcast ephemeral kinds; ak.key.verification.* point-to-point strands MUST use device-message.schema.json instead.

realm_id.description: Realm whose ephemeral channel carries this signal. Authorization to broadcast a signal on a Realm channel is governed by the same membership / capability rules as the corresponding durable kinds.

actor_id.description: Signaling actor. MUST be a member of the Realm (ak.member.state cell join != ban/leave/remove at receive time) for the broadcast to be admitted by other clients; receivers drop signals from non-members without surfacing them.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for all broadcast ephemeral signals; proof.verification_method fragment MUST equal this full device_id.

sent_at.description: Wall-clock send time. Diagnostic only — ephemeral signals do not participate in HLC ordering.

expires_at.description: Server / client MUST drop the signal at or after this time. Per-kind soft caps (recommended): presence ≤ 60s, typing ≤ 15s, receipt.read ≤ 30s, call.signal ≤ 30s. Signals with expires_at > sent_at + 5 minutes MUST be dropped by receivers (`invalid_param`).

payload.description: Kind-specific signal payload. Schema per kind is defined by the producing module (e.g. zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md for ak.call.signal, zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md §3.5 for ak.typing, zh/discovery/read-receipts.md for ak.receipt.read). Payload MUST NOT carry mutable governance state — that belongs in a durable event.

proof.description: Detached-JWS proof over the canonical ephemeral envelope, structurally isomorphic to the durable Event proof ($defs/event_proof in event-envelope.schema.json / models/event-and-patch.md §3). Required for every broadcast ephemeral kind (ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, ak.call.signal) so receivers can verify origin without trusting relay attribution. Signing input is the canonical proof binding object {context:'ak.ephemeral-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}; event_digest is canonical_digest of the envelope with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS). verification_method MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ak:device:<uuidv7>` id, and its controller DID MUST equal envelope actor_id. See crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5.

call_id.description: Typed call/session identifier (ak:call:<uuidv7>) scoped to the Realm. Unified with ice-config-response and media-operations so cross-channel join cross-checks key on the same form.

seq.description: Monotonic per-(realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id) sequence. Receivers MUST reject replay or rollback.

data.description: Signal-type-specific payload body (invite/answer/candidate/mute_state/...). Optional because some signals (e.g. ack) carry no body. moderation is closed by the conditional below; other signal types retain their profile-specific shape.

strand_id.description: Strand whose timeline the actor is typing into. Fanout MUST be clipped to the Strand effective scope per zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md §3.5.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key the actor is typing into. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message timelines are restricted to the discussion track, so when present this MUST be 'discussion'; when omitted receivers MUST resolve it to 'discussion'. Kept explicit so future profiles that register additional writable timelines can disambiguate typing targets without changing the envelope shape.

typing.description: true = actor started or continues typing; false = actor stopped typing and receivers SHOULD clear the indicator immediately.

ttl_ms.description: Client-side auto-clear hint in milliseconds. The envelope expires_at remains the authoritative drop deadline; per-kind soft cap for typing is 15s.

ephemeral_proof.description: Detached-JWS proof for a broadcast ephemeral envelope. Structurally isomorphic to event-envelope.schema.json #/$defs/event_proof: same kind / alg / verification_method / event_digest / created_at / jws shape, so a single EdDSA detached-JWS verifier serves both durable Event proofs and ephemeral signal proofs. The binding object carries context='ak.ephemeral-proof-v1'. The only difference is which canonical bytes feed event_digest (here: the ephemeral envelope with `proof` removed).

kind.description: detached_jws = device signature over the canonical proof binding object canonical_json({context:'ak.ephemeral-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). event_digest is the canonical ephemeral-envelope hash with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS).

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing device key. MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ak:device:<uuidv7>` id and equals envelope.device_id; verifier MUST strip the fragment for controller comparison and MUST compare that controller DID bit-identically to the envelope actor_id, then resolve the verify key from the device directory (keys/query device_signing_key, keys-operations.schema.json). Same form as event_proof.verification_method.

alg.description: Default EdDSA. Same enum as event_proof.alg for a shared verifier.

event_digest.description: canonical_digest(envelope without `proof`) per RFC 8785 JCS, isomorphic to event_proof.event_digest (which excludes proofs + unsigned).

schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Erasure Receipt
schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed attestation that an issuer completed, partially completed, or blocked a hard-erasure request within a declared storage boundary. It proves the issuer's deletion action and retained verification stub, not disappearance of independent third-party copies.

scope.description: Boundary in which deletion was attempted. This MUST be narrow enough for an auditor to tell which service/storage class made the claim.

retained_stub_digest.description: Hash of the retained verification stub after erasure: hash(canonical_json(retained_stub)). The stub must be sufficient to verify event id/digest, proof event_digest, redaction authorization, seal inclusion, target id, legal-hold state, and receipt linkage without retaining erased plaintext.

retained_stub.description: Optional in-band verification stub. When omitted, the issuer MUST expose the same canonical stub via its erasure receipt endpoint; retained_stub_digest still binds the exact bytes.

fanout_status.description: Cross-Principal-Server erasure receipt fanout aggregate status tracked by the issuing server (models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.2). 'pending' = peers still within erasure_propagation_window_ms and not all acknowledged; 'complete' = every peer that ever held this Realm's content returned a receipt; 'incomplete' = at least one peer failed to acknowledge within erasure_propagation_window_ms. The issuing server MUST surface 'incomplete' to audit/UI and MUST NOT silently swallow it. Absent on receipts that do not drive fanout tracking.

peer_receipts.description: Per-peer fanout acknowledgement records maintained by the issuing server: one entry per peer Principal Server that ever held this Realm's content. Each entry records that peer's acknowledgement status and time, backing the aggregate fanout_status.

status.description: 'pending' = awaiting this peer's feedback receipt; 'acknowledged' = peer returned a receipt (regardless of its outcome); 'failed' = peer reported a non-completed feedback outcome (partially_completed / blocked_by_legal_hold); 'timed_out' = no feedback within erasure_propagation_window_ms.

receipt_id.description: The peer's own feedback receipt id, when received.

event_digest.description: Digest of the original Event envelope or durable object metadata, when the erased subject was event-backed.

retained_digests.description: Event digest / object payload digests retained for signature verification. MUST NOT be a bare digest of erased low-entropy plaintext.

schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.title: Arkret Erasure Verification Stub
schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.description: Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_digest. It preserves event graph, proof, seal, redaction, legal-hold and receipt linkage evidence without retaining erased plaintext.

events.description: Canonical set projection of covered Event canonical digests. Bare event IDs are forbidden because they do not bind Event content. Items MUST be strictly increasing by the UTF-8 bytes of canonical_json(item); producers sort and deduplicate before signing, and receivers reject a non-canonical wire array before digest verification.

proofs.description: Detached receipt proofs sign canonical_json({context:'ak.receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest: receipt_digest, issuer, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag, not a wire field.

allOf.$comment: A device re-anchor receipt is a canonical set containing exactly one reanchor and one replacement authorize item. The issuer compares scope.reanchor_digest with the item whose kind is ak.device.reanchor and scope.replacement_authorize_digest with the item whose kind is ak.device.authorize; array position has no domain meaning.

registry_head.description: Digest of the accepted-at identity registry head snapshot.

reanchor_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.device.reanchor.

replacement_authorize_digest.description: MUST equal event_digest of the unique events[] item whose kind is ak.device.authorize.

schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Event Envelope
schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.description:
Single canonical wire object for **durable Event Envelope** — i.e. events with wire_scope=durable_event OR wire_scope=actor_private_event in event-kind-registry.json. Reducer-input events (reducer_input=true) are CBA events: DataEvents carry top-level effects / seal_ref / auth_context; Control Moves carry effects / seal_basis and optional preconditions. Non-reducer events (read cursor, batch receipts, range completeness, audit RYW, etc.) omit effects / seal_ref / seal_basis. Causal refs use prev_refs (actor chain), causal_refs[] and refs[] (semantic refs with role: authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...). proof.event_digest is the hash of canonical producer event bytes after removing proofs, unsigned, and reducer-stamped top-level fields (currently effective_scope and actor_kind); detached_jws signs the canonical proof binding object that includes fixed context='ak.event-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, and domain/audience where present. hlc IS included in canonical producer event bytes (integrity-protected) but is semantically advisory — see encoding.md §6-§7.

**Wire-scope boundary (normative)**: ephemeral_event kinds (ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, ak.call.signal) MUST NOT appear with this schema — they use the dedicated ephemeral-envelope.schema.json carried on the ephemeral channel (and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state). Likewise ak.key.verification.* and ak.realm_key.request use device-message.schema.json on the point-to-point to-device channel. ak.self.events.command.submit MUST schema_violation any event whose kind has wire_scope=ephemeral_event in the registry — see operations-sync.md §2.3 (wire-scope reject rule).

kind.description: Standard ak.* effect kinds MUST appear in artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json. State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvents use effects + seal_ref + auth_context; Control Moves use effects + seal_basis and Seal finality; per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic.

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope for this accepted Event. scope_circle_id=null materializes as {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle-scoped objects materialize as {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. Actor-supplied submit payloads MUST NOT carry this field. This value is excluded from producer proof.event_digest, but enters accepted envelope storage, Seal/sub-seal observational commitments when present, and in MLS-backed scopes E2EE AAD and MLS governance binding input.

actor_id.description: Principal whose Realm/cell state the Event mutates and to whom the durable fact is attributed. When executed_by is absent, the proof signer maps to actor_id. When executed_by is present, actor_id remains the principal of record while the actual executor and proof signer map to executed_by.

executed_by.description: Optional actual executor DID for a delegated write. This covers both an agent/applet/service acting for a controller actor and a controller acting under explicit managed-principal delegation to write an Agent principal's control state. actor_id is always the principal of record; executed_by is the principal that issued and signed the wire write. When present, MUST appear together with authorization_ref. Applet delegated writes also MUST carry applet_id. Enters canonical event bytes, event digest, and E2EE AAD. Receivers MUST verify the proof's verification_method maps to executed_by (not actor_id) and MUST NOT synthesize an actor_id signature.

authorization_ref.description: Optional. Required when executed_by is present. Prefer a materialized ak:grant:* id; an event id is allowed only when it points to the accepted grant/delegation event that produced the effective authorization; a DID-document delegation URL (did_delegation_ref) is allowed when the delegation is expressed in the principal DID document (for example ArkretDeviceEnrollmentAuthority or the managed-agent principal-control delegation). Reducer MUST validate the referenced grant/delegation covers the event kind and target resource and is within its effective validity window; for did_delegation_ref the designation is resolved against the actor_id principal DID document at the event's accepted-at.

applet_id.description: Optional signed Applet provenance. Required by ak.profile.applet_* when the Event is introduced by an Applet, Ghost Actor, bridge, or delegated applet path. Enters canonical event bytes and therefore is covered by proof.event_digest. When present, authorization_ref MUST also be present and MUST bind this applet_id and registration_epoch per zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 11.

external_ref.description: Optional signed external provenance reference for Applet / bridge-originated Events. It is covered by event_digest and MUST NOT be carried only in unsigned when used for loop prevention, audit, or external-message idempotency. Must not contain unauthorized external plaintext.

actor_kind.description: Reducer-stamped projection of the actor_id Actor Profile's actor_kind at write time (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/models/actor.md). Lets audit/forensic/offline readers classify the event without resolving Actor Profile. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and never appears as actor_id; device actions are attributed to the owning user/org principal DID. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (schema_violation reason=actor_kind_reducer_managed); reducer stamps it during accept. Immutable once written and excluded from producer proof.event_digest.

hlc.description: Advisory hybrid logical clock. INCLUDED in canonical bytes for signing and event digest (so it is integrity-protected and cannot be rewritten by relays), but semantically advisory: used only as a deterministic tiebreaker for timeline display when two events are causally unreachable. MUST NOT influence authorization, lattice join, Control Move precondition comparison, or Seal finality. See encoding.md §7 and event-auth-state-resolution.md §3 rule 1.

prev_refs.description: Actor-chain causal predecessors (envelope-level). For semantic refs (authorized_by, after, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...), use refs[].

refs.description: Semantic refs with role. did_recovery_anchor is reserved exclusively for ak.device.reanchor and is enforced bidirectionally below; all other common roles remain open extension tokens.

causal_refs.description: DataEvent semantic causal predecessors by event_digest. These refs express business causality only; they are not global completeness proofs.

preconditions.description: Control Move only. Pre-state predicates that must hold under the seal_basis governance view; if any fails, the entire event fails (no partial application of effects). DataEvents MUST NOT carry preconditions.

effects.description: Reducer-input only. Atomic cell writes. DataEvents may only target data plane cells; Control Moves may only target control plane cells. MUST contain at least one effect when present.

seal_ref.description: DataEvent only. Accepted control-plane Seal id used as the authorization basis. Receivers verify identity/key/capability validity at this seal and apply revocation freshness rules.

conflict_keys_digest.description: Optional diagnostic digest: hash over the canonical sorted list of cell ids derived from effects[]. Producer and verifier each derive the cell set from effects[] under their schema version; a mismatch surfaces schema-derivation divergence early. This field is NOT a security boundary: verifiers MUST derive conflict domains from effects[] regardless of its presence.

auth_context.description: DataEvent only. Pins the signing DID/key/capability epoch used to verify authorization at seal_ref.

seal_basis.description: Control Move only. Signed governance basis for preconditions/effects. control_event_set_root covers only control-plane event digests; state_root covers only control-plane cells.

unsigned.description: Local / transport-only metadata (server-derived hints, redaction reason, age). NOT covered by signature or event digest.

proofs.description: Detached signatures over the canonical proof binding object. proof.event_digest is computed from canonical producer event bytes excluding proofs, unsigned, and reducer-stamped top-level fields (currently effective_scope and actor_kind); hlc is included in that hash as advisory signed metadata. The actor / device / service signature lives here. Seal signatures live on the Seal object, not on the event.

requirements.description: Schema/reducer/feature/critical-extension requirements declared by this event. All sub-fields enter the canonical event bytes and the proof event_digest. Receivers MUST fail closed on any unknown critical entry.

schema.description: Schema profile ids this event depends on.

reducer.description: Reducer profile id this event depends on.

features.description: Features this event requires; receiver MUST fail closed if any is unknown.

critical_extensions.description: Critical extension declarations; each entry MUST have id, extension_scope, fail_closed=true.

allOf.$comment: Signed Applet provenance invariants. external_ref is only meaningful when bound to a signed applet_id, and Applet-originated writes must cite the accepted authorization/delegation grant.

Known active non-reducer event kinds (wire_scope=actor_private_event OR wire_scope=durable_event with reducer_input=false) MUST NOT carry CBA reducer fields: preconditions/effects/seal_ref/auth_context/seal_basis. ephemeral_event kinds are forbidden here entirely — see the next allOf branch.

Wire-scope boundary (normative, T02). Kinds with wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json MUST NOT appear in the durable Event Envelope. They use ephemeral-envelope.schema.json (broadcast: presence/typing/receipt/call.signal) or device-message.schema.json (point-to-point to-device: ak.key.verification.*, ak.secret.*). ak.self.events.command.submit MUST schema_violation on any wire bytes matching this enum; reducer/state path MUST NOT advance Seal coverage or actor_seq for these kinds.

Known active reducer-input event kinds MUST carry effects and exactly one CBA basis shape: DataEvent (seal_ref + auth_context, no preconditions/seal_basis), Control Move (seal_basis, no seal_ref/auth_context), the ak.realm.create genesis bootstrap shape, OR a Realm bootstrap follow-up shape (same submit batch after create; batch context is enforced by admission, not JSON Schema). Unknown extension kinds must declare their own critical extension requirements and are not matched by this branch.

oneOf.$comment: ak.device.authorize may be the second item of the exact PCR bootstrap or device re-anchor atomic unit. JSON Schema permits the no-basis shape; batch admission MUST reject it anywhere else.

allOf.$comment: Conflict-recovery event detection: any precondition with op=head_in implies conflict recovery semantics. When triggered, refs[] MUST contain BOTH a state_witness and an inclusion_proof (event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1). Schema-level enforcement; reducer-level verify re-checks.
MUST contain at least one state_witness ref
MUST contain at least one inclusion_proof ref
ak.device.reanchor is the only event allowed to carry did_recovery_anchor, and it must carry exactly one critical ref whose id has did:webvh versionId shape.
Count the reserved role independent of critical so one critical plus one non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

Any Event carrying did_inception is confined to the closed self-principal PCR-genesis shape and carries exactly one critical ref. A delegated Agent PCR create intentionally carries no did_inception; batch/reducer admission distinguishes self-principal genesis from delegated Agent genesis by comparing actor_id, executed_by, authorization_ref, PCR binding and DID subject, which JSON Schema cannot express.
Count the reserved role independently so a critical ref plus a non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

A principal_control Realm create without did_inception is syntactically reserved for delegated managed-principal genesis. Requiring the delegation pair prevents a self-principal caller from falling through to ordinary realm.create capability admission; the delegated_pcr_genesis verifier performs the actor/DID/service/realm comparisons that JSON Schema cannot express.

Reject these top-level field names. The Event Envelope root is closed (additionalProperties=false); extension data belongs in payload or requirements.critical_extensions. The root field names type / auth_refs / target_ref / operation_id are dropped and MUST NOT appear at the root; use kind / refs[role=authorized_by] / payload.* fields / SDK-internal id instead (see operations-sync.md §5).

anyOf.$comment: auth_refs is dropped; it MUST NOT appear at the root, use refs[role=authorized_by]

external_ref.description: Signed external provenance. Extension profiles define exact field vocabulary; common fields include protocol, network_id, instance_id, user_id, location_id, event_id, external_id, and url. Implementations MUST preserve all fields in canonical bytes and MUST NOT use unsigned.external_ref for security decisions.

canonical_event_timestamp.description: Canonical Event Envelope/proof timestamp. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits; whole-second shorthand, finer fractions, and numeric offsets are forbidden.

profile_ref.description: Profile that defines this extension's semantics when schema_ref is not the exact governing profile.

parameters.description: Closed extension-specific parameter bag. Unknown top-level fields are forbidden; extension-defined data belongs here and is interpreted only after id/schema_ref support is sealed.

material_digest.description: Optional digest of out-of-band extension material when parameters would be too large for the event envelope.

did_delegation_ref.description: DID URL of a delegation entry in the principal DID document that designates the executed_by principal as authorized for the action (e.g. a ArkretDeviceEnrollmentAuthority service entry id, or a capabilityDelegation verification method id). Used as authorization_ref when the delegation lives in the DID document rather than in an on-stream grant/event. Resolved against the principal DID document at the event's accepted-at (point-in-time), so enrollment-authority key rotation does not invalidate prior authorizations.

kind.description: add/remove → or_set; set → mv_register/cas_register; transition → fsm; inc/dec → counter; append → ordered_log.

issuer_seq.description: Required only for kind=append. Zero-based sequence scoped to (effect.cell, envelope.actor_id); see event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

role.description: Common roles include authorized_by, attestation, parent_event, after, audit_pair, recovery_capability, state_witness, inclusion_proof, did_inception, and did_recovery_anchor. did_recovery_anchor is reserved to ak.device.reanchor by kind dispatch.

proof.description: Optional inline proof material. Used for inclusion_proof role: carries the Merkle audit path defined by event-auth-state-resolution.md §6.2.1 / §6.2.2 that proves a leaf belongs to a witness state_root. May be omitted when id alone is a content-addressed reference to a separately stored proof object.

kind.description: detached_jws = actor / device / service signature over canonical proof binding object: canonical_json({context:'ak.event-proof-v1', event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). context is a fixed signing-context domain tag, not an Event envelope field. event_digest is the canonical producer event hash excluding proofs, unsigned, and reducer-stamped top-level fields (currently effective_scope and actor_kind); hlc IS covered by that hash as advisory signed metadata. Ordering authority signatures are carried by Seal.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the Event-signing key. For principal device proofs the fragment MUST be the full device_id (`ak:device:<uuidv7>`), so receivers can resolve `(actor_id, device_id)` through the device directory. Generic verification strips fragment/query only for controller comparison and compares that controller DID bit-identically to actor_id or executed_by. The sole exception is an Event whose selected admission variant is did_root_anchor: its closed verifier MUST instead require verification_method to equal an active controller-proof verification method from the one critical did_inception/did_recovery_anchor entry and verify the controller proof/update authority against that referenced did:webvh history; a root did:key controller is not rewritten to the principal actor_id. This exception cannot apply to any other Event.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for handle-claim proofs. Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it required.

proof.description: Generic detached-JWS proof shape reused by non-Event schemas (snapshot signature, snapshot witness attestations, identity receipts, handle claims, etc.). MUST NOT be used as the shape of Event Envelope `proofs[]` — Event proofs reference $defs/event_proof and bind canonical Event bytes via `event_digest`. Non-Event signed objects MUST define an object-family signing-context constant and include it in the canonical proof binding object with payload_digest; the context constant is not a wire field in this generic shape. drift detection: `payload_digest#event_proof` in forbidden-wire-fields.json is the hard-reject mirror of this rule. New non-Event signed objects MAY $ref this shape; new signed Event-shaped objects MUST instead $ref event_proof.

kind.description: Generic detached JWS proof over a canonical non-Event payload binding object that includes an object-family context constant.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key for this non-Event detached proof. Same pattern as $defs/event_proof.verification_method; semantics are decoupled from Event proof (see $defs/event_proof for the Event-only shape).

payload_digest.description: Generic non-Event detached-proof hash. This $defs/proof shape is reused by non-Event schemas; Event.properties.proofs references $defs/event_proof and MUST use event_digest instead.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for non-Event proofs. handle-claim.schema.json requires binding_state=verified claims to carry at least one proofs[] entry with proof_purpose=holder_acceptance; without this optional field that requirement was unsatisfiable under additionalProperties:false. Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it load-bearing.

schemas/event-payload.schema.json.title: Arkret Standard Event Payloads
schemas/event-payload.schema.json.description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ak.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

member_delivery_binding.description: Per-Realm binding of a member to a concrete delivery target service. Authoritative source for Realm-scoped event / sync / to-device / push / key-package delivery; sender MUST NOT consult the actor's DID Document service entry as an alternative resolution path when this binding is present. Pairwise / unlinkability use-cases are orthogonal — see identity-did.md and pairwise DID guidance.

recipient_service_id.description: service DID of the recipient Principal Server for this member in this Realm.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows principal_server. Notary / shared Sync Service are addressed by Realm-level sync_endpoints, not by member-level delivery_binding.

binding_scope.description: v1 only allows realm-scoped bindings. Organization-wide or DID-global bindings are out of v1 scope; they would be expressed by Realm policy + organization registry instead.

binding_source.description: How the binding was determined at join time. 'explicit' = user / admin chose; 'did_document_default' = resolved from invitee DID Document (only allowed when Realm policy enables fallback); other values are policy-driven.

delivery_modes.description: Explicit allow-list of delivery modes for this binding. Empty / absent is NOT permitted; implementations declaring a 'full' member SHOULD list all five values.

service_endpoint.description: Optional cached HTTPS endpoint of recipient_service_id at resolved_at. Diagnostic / fast-path hint only; sender MUST re-resolve via DID Document before federation transactions and SHOULD verify endpoint matches the service DID's current binding.

did_document_digest.description: Canonical hash of invitee's DID Document at resolved_at. Required when binding_source = did_document_default.

resolved_at.description: Wall-clock time at which the binding was resolved. Always required so that downstream verifiers can decide whether the resolved state is still acceptable under their freshness policy.

service_acceptance_ref.description: Reference to the recipient service's prior service_acceptance / endorsement Event. Required when binding_source = explicit, invite, or organization_policy; reducer MUST verify the referenced Event is signed by recipient_service_id and its scope covers this Realm. Producers MUST NOT fabricate this ref for realm bootstrap; bootstrap without real service evidence must use another binding_source with its own evidence or remain unroutable.

holder_proof_ref.description: Reference to the member's DID proof (challenge-response) that bound the DID to recipient_service_id at the auth/account layer. Required when the member did not submit the join Control Move directly from a session at recipient_service_id.

policy_event_ref.description: Reference to the Realm / Join / Organization policy revision that authorised this binding. Required when binding_source ∈ {join_policy, organization_policy, realm_policy}.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. After this timestamp the binding is no longer usable for delivery; senders MUST quarantine pending events and the member MUST submit a rebind Move (same-state join self-transition) carrying a fresh binding. Sender behaviour is fail-closed: MUST NOT fall through to DID Document on expiry.

delivery_binding_policy_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.delivery_binding_policy. Closed object so that misspelled fields are rejected with schema_violation. The enclosing Event envelope carries realm_id. See zh/governance/member-delivery-binding.md §4.
delivery_binding_policy_payload.description: Realm-level constraints on member delivery_binding acceptance: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, and who may sign rebind. allowed_recipient_services is fail-closed: empty array [] = reject any recipient service; use the explicit sentinel ["*"] to mean unrestricted. minProperties: 1 so an empty {} payload is schema_violation (semantically equivalent to never writing the event).

realm_id.description: Optional echo of the Realm this policy governs; authoritative scope is the enclosing envelope realm_id.

allowed_binding_sources.description: Subset of binding_source values allowed to appear in an accepted binding. Default (when this policy event is absent) is ["did_document_default"] for personal / public Realms; organization Realms MUST narrow it explicitly.

did_document_default_allowed.description: Whether binding_source=did_document_default is permitted. Defaults to false. Organization / compliance Realms MUST keep it false.

oneOf.description: Closed allow-list of recipient_service_id values. Empty array [] = reject any recipient service (fail-closed): the reducer MUST reject routable joins (delivery_binding_policy_mismatch) when the recipient service is neither on this list, nor covered by the ["*"] sentinel, nor endorsed via required_endorsers. The empty array MUST NOT be interpreted as 'unrestricted'. Non-empty required_endorsers remains mandatory even when the service is listed here.

The explicit unrestricted sentinel ["*"]. Lifts ONLY the recipient-service allow-list dimension; it does NOT exempt required_endorsers or other §2 acceptance criteria. The unrestricted meaning MUST be declared explicitly via this sentinel and never inferred from an empty array.

allowed_recipient_services.description: Either an array of recipient service DIDs (possibly empty = fail-closed reject) or exactly the sentinel ["*"] for unrestricted. Defaults to [] (reject / fail-closed) when this field is omitted. See zh/governance/member-delivery-binding.md §2 / §4.

required_endorsers.description: When this array is non-empty, the recipient_service_id's service_acceptance_ref MUST be endorsed by one of these governance DIDs, regardless of allowed_recipient_services or the ["*"] sentinel. Empty array = no mandatory endorsement requirement.

unroutable_membership_allowed.description: Whether delivery_status="unroutable" members are permitted. Defaults to false.

rebind_authorization.description: Legal signer / endorser set for rebind Control Moves. Defaults to member_and_admin. See §6.

expires_after_seconds.description: Maximum validity of any binding in this Realm; unset/null = no expiry.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ak:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

track_name.description: Strand track key for Message payloads. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field name `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`. The discriminator is `kind`, the composite child array is `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes` (see schemas/message.schema.json and forbidden-wire-fields.json `blocks/content_block_composite`).

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

keypackage_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped MLS KeyPackage reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

device_cross_signing_binding.description: SSK signature binding a ak.device.authorize payload's device_public_key, hpke_key and algorithms to the principal's accepted cross-signing generation. Canonical signing input is defined in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5.2.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the self-signing key that signed the device trust binding.

device_enrollment_authority_binding.description: Delegated-authority binding for a ak.device.authorize event admitted as service_attested: device_public_key, hpke_key and algorithms are attested by an enrollment authority designated in the principal DID document. Both the external-authority B model and the principal-owned A-model genesis use this shape; identity model is determined by whether authority_did equals principal_id, not by the binding name. Identity root keys MUST NOT sign this event.

authority_did.description: DID of the enrollment authority that attested this device, designated by the principal DID document. MUST equal the envelope executed_by.

authorization_ref.description: Reference to the delegation evidence designating authority_did as an enrollment authority for this principal (DID-document service delegation, materialized grant, or the accepted delegation event). MUST match the envelope authorization_ref.

authority_verification_method_snapshot.description: Inline snapshot of the enrollment authority's signing verification method as it existed at issuance time. REQUIRED when the enrollment authority DID has no history-resolution method (e.g. did:web) so that historical re-verification depends only on event-carried evidence, not on online resolution of the authority's current DID document. Receivers MUST verify proofs[] with this snapshot's public key. A ak.device.authorize issued by a no-history-resolution-method authority that omits this snapshot (or authority_controller_proof) MUST be rejected with reason device_enrollment_authority_snapshot_missing. See zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.6 step4 and zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.2.

method_id.description: Verification method id of the snapshotted key within the enrollment authority DID document at issuance time.

public_key_multibase.description: Multibase-encoded public key of the snapshotted verification method. Exactly one of public_key_multibase / public_key_jwk MUST be present.

public_key_jwk.description: JWK form of the snapshotted verification method public key. Exactly one of public_key_multibase / public_key_jwk MUST be present.

alg.description: Signature algorithm of the snapshotted verification method.

authority_controller_proof.description: Controller proof linking authority_verification_method_snapshot to the enrollment authority DID's controller set at issuance time, signed by the authority DID's then-current controller key over 'this verification method belongs to this DID and is authorized to sign device authorizations'. REQUIRED alongside authority_verification_method_snapshot when the enrollment authority DID has no history-resolution method. See zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.6 step4.

controller_method_id.description: Verification method id of the controller key (within the enrollment authority DID document) that produced this proof.

signature.description: Controller signature binding the snapshotted verification method to the authority DID and its device-authorization-signing authority.

signed_at.description: Issuance time of the controller proof.

patch_path.description: Arkret field patch path. Segments are snake_case identifiers, optional stable-key selectors (such as profile-declared named-collection arrays of the form `<field>[<key>=<value>]`), or backtick-quoted literals; numeric array indexes are not part of ak.patch.v1. v1 standard schemas no longer use stable-key selectors — Strand tracks is now a map keyed by track name, so paths like `tracks.discussion.profile` are plain object segments.

patch_value.description: A plain value is shorthand for {"$op":"set","value":...}. Objects containing $op MUST be patch_operation objects.

not.$comment: Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; `type` is a banned field name.

object_snapshot.description: Embedded object snapshot inside an Event payload. Object kind is derived from the typed-id prefix on `id`; there is no separate `type` field.

generic_standard_payload.description: Generic fallback shape used only inside Event Envelope kind dispatch and tooling diagnostics. It rejects the `type` field but does not close kind-specific fields; validators MUST NOT accept a standard Event solely because its payload validates against this definition.

not.$comment: Standard ak.* event payloads use kind (envelope) + payload schema discriminators. `type` is a banned field name here to keep schema validation aligned with reducer behavior.

notary_fault_equivocation_payload.description: Notary equivocation evidence: two Seals signed by signer_id that violate the slot rule (same (realm_id, notary_seq) with different canonical bytes, or notary_seq=k+1 not descending from the same signer's notary_seq=k). Admission is verification-only: the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1.

notary_fault_censorship_payload.description: Notary censorship evidence: a signed control-plane receipt whose event digest is provably absent from the obliged Seal's control_event_set_root and that received neither signed-reject nor defer. Does NOT automatically disqualify the notary; adds an audit fault record. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2.

receipt.description: The signed control-plane receipt issued under receipt_sla_ms (event_digest, received_at, receipt_seq, issuer, signature).

seal_ref.description: The Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the receipted Control Move.

non_membership_proof.description: Sorted-neighbor non-membership proof for the receipted event digest against seal_ref's control_event_set_root.

missing_rejection_or_defer_proof.description: Optional structured evidence that no signed-reject / defer covering the receipt exists in the obliged window.

realm_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Realm object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance. Batch-level validation MUST also require this create to be immediately followed by the closed-form creator self-grant defined by zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5; create plus founding grant is one atomic bootstrap unit, and a missing or widened founding grant rejects the whole unit.

realm_notary_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.notary. The enclosing Control Move MUST CAS the current ak.component.notary.v1 head and the current notary authority MUST finalize the containing Seal.

realm_digest_suite_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.digest_suite_transition under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. The containing Transition Seal commits the pre-transition governance view with previous_state_root and the post-transition view with state_root.

realm_organization_payload.description: Organization-side endorsement or revocation for a Realm relationship. Reducer validation MUST require realm_id to match the top-level Event.realm_id, organization_id to resolve to an Organization principal, the Realm-side writer to hold ak.realm.admin, and authorization to verify against the organization DID control state or a delegated service whose purpose covers this relationship and control_scopes.

statement_id.description: Stable id of this organization statement. It is audit identity, not the reducer cell subject; the reducer cell subject is (organization_id, relationship).

realm_id.description: Realm the organization statement is bound to. MUST equal the enclosing Event.realm_id.

organization_id.description: Organization principal DID that endorses, governs, sponsors, certifies, or revokes the Realm relationship.

relationship.description: Relationship being asserted or revoked for this organization and Realm.

control_scopes.description: Machine-readable scopes covered by the organization's consent. A scope here is an endorsement boundary only; actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy, notary, capability, or service-binding event.

expires_at.description: Administrative review/renewal hint only. It does not auto-transition account status; a later explicit ak.account.status event is required and remains subject to supersedes and terminal rules.

realm_frontier_digest.description: Optional digest of the Realm control frontier the organization evaluated when issuing this statement.

organization_policy_ref.description: Optional DID-document delegation URL, policy object, governance decision, or attestation reference used to evaluate the statement.

authorization.description: Organization-side authorization proof. This is independent of the Realm-side ak.realm.admin authorization required to write the event into Realm history.

issuer.description: Organization DID or delegated service DID that issued this statement.

delegation_ref.description: Required when issuer_role is governance_service or account_authority. It MUST resolve to a live organization DID delegation whose purpose covers ak.realm.organization and the requested relationship/control_scopes.

executed_by.description: Optional human administrator or service principal that initiated the organization-side decision. This does not become the organization principal.

proof.description: Signature, threshold transcript, or governance-service attestation over the canonical organization statement binding statement_id, realm_id, organization_id, relationship, status, control_scopes, issued_at, validity window, and statement replacement/revocation fields.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

strand_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Strand object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

circle_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Circle object schema for wire validation. Reducer validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match top-level created_at, then enforce parent Realm encryption floor. When payload.object.encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420', the reducer derives the independent MLS group binding for (realm_id, circle_id). payload.object.mls_group_ref is reducer-derived and MUST NOT be actor supplied.

sidecar_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Agent Sidecar object schema. It is emitted only by the atomic ak.self.agent.sidecar.command.ensure aggregate after the reducer/service derives and creates backing_circle_id; raw ensure callers never construct or submit this Event directly. The reducer MUST enforce one non-tombstoned Sidecar per (realm_id, controller_id), controller equality with the authenticated principal, exact same-batch backing Circle binding, and effective_scope=circle with circle_id equal to backing_circle_id.

agent_sidecar_exchange_control_payload.description: Outer payload for ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. The service-visible strand_id routes the Event inside the Sidecar backing Circle; encrypted_payload plaintext MUST validate as agent-sidecar-exchange-control.schema.json. Admission MUST require that the effective scope is the matching Sidecar backing Circle and actor_id is that Sidecar's controller.

morph_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Morph object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

object_stage_set_payload.description: Shared base shape for ak.<kind>.stage.set events. Each concrete stage_set payload class (strand_stage_set_payload / morph_stage_set_payload) extends this base by pinning the object-id field (strand_id / morph_id) and is referenced from event-envelope.schema.json conditional routing. The stage enum is the protocol-level 8-value set defined in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.2; profile MUST NOT extend or override the enum. Reducer hard invariants are listed in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 (terminal state freeze, non-active reject, reducer-derived stage_changed_at, same-value no-op, single-source via this event). The payload intentionally does NOT carry a reason / note / explanation field: this event log is the audit source (actor_id + created_at), and human-readable explanation belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. expected_stage compiles to a cell head_eq precondition and provides optimistic concurrency; omission is equivalent to no CAS.

expected_stage.description: Optional CAS precondition: when present, reducer compiles it to a cell head_eq comparison against the cell's current value. Mismatch yields failed_precondition reason=stage_cas_mismatch. Same semantics as ak.strand.watch.set's expected_value.

not.$comment: Reason / note / explanation fields are intentionally rejected. Stage transitions audit through the event log; human-readable rationale belongs in a Message on the discussion track that references this event.

strand_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.stage.set. Mutates Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see object_stage_set_payload description and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §3.2.

not.$comment: Mirror of object_stage_set_payload guard. Reason-style fields are forbidden; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message.

morph_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.stage.set. Mutates Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see object_stage_set_payload description and zh/models/morph.md §2.

not.$comment: Mirror of object_stage_set_payload guard.

morph_schema_migrate_payload.description: Migration of a Morph's schema_refs[] under the schema-evolution policy (zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3). Distinct from ak.morph.update — schema_refs[] changes MUST go through this event so the migration is auditable, capability-gated, and carries an explicit compatibility class. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds the ak.morph.schema_migrate capability (or the Realm-declared equivalent) at the event's frontier; missing capability yields capability_denied. Reducer MUST reject compatibility_class ∈ {breaking, transformation} unless the Realm declares ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (yielding morph_schema_refs_transformation_unsupported otherwise). Reducer MUST verify from_schema_refs[] matches the Morph's current schema_refs[] at apply time (yielding failed_precondition otherwise). The event's own requirements.schema[] MUST include the union of from_schema_refs[] and to_schema_refs[] so readers can resolve both versions during overlap. Each transformation_rules[] entry SHOULD describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.); the rule object shape is governed by the Realm-declared ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 profile.

from_schema_refs.description: Expected current schema_refs[] of the Morph at apply time. Reducer MUST set-equal-compare against the Morph's state and reject mismatches as failed_precondition (semantic: optimistic concurrency on schema_refs).

to_schema_refs.description: Desired schema_refs[] after migration. MUST be a registered set of schema profile ids resolvable at apply time.

compatibility_class.description: additive: to_schema_refs[] only adds optional fields / lookup-compatible profile refs; no historical event needs reinterpretation. breaking: to_schema_refs[] removes or tightens fields; future events follow new schema but historical events keep validating under from_schema_refs[]. transformation: a per-event data transform is needed to map old payload shape to new (requires explicit transformation rules). Core reducers MUST accept additive only; breaking and transformation require the ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 opt-in Realm profile.

transformation_rules.description: Required when compatibility_class='transformation'. Each entry MUST describe a deterministic, replay-safe per-field mapping (rename, type widening, default backfill, etc.). The rule object shape is governed by ak.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1 (see profile description in conformance-profiles.json).

migration_evidence.description: Optional seal / witness evidence justifying the migration (e.g., governance proposal id, audit trail seal). The event's authorization_ref carries the formal capability gate; migration_evidence is for human reviewers.

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the profile cell subject is payload.object.id.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone.

body.description: Caller-supplied opaque account-data value. Any JSON value.

account_blocklist_payload.description: Payload for ak.account.blocklist. Holder-private personal blocklist state; it never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

object_patch_payload.description: Generic patch payload for object families that do not define a narrower id-specific payload. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; object_ref and target-less patch forms from earlier drafts are not canonical.

morph_update_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.update. Patches ordinary Morph fields on the Morph identified by target_ref. morph_kind is create-locked by ak.morph.create and MUST NOT appear in patch; stage and stage_changed_at are single-sourced by ak.morph.stage.set.

profile_realm_override_payload.description: Realm-scoped actor profile override payload for ak.profile.realm_override. target_ref is the Actor Profile being overridden; target_realm_id is the Realm where the override applies.

strand_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.update. Patches ordinary Strand fields on the Strand identified by target_ref.

circle_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.circle.update. Patch path MUST NOT contain realm_id, encryption_profile, mls_group_ref, state, state_changed_at, created_by, or created_at; reducer enforces the path-level lock and semantic policy floor checks.

space_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.space.update. Patches Space metadata (title, rank, kind-specific fields) on the Space identified by space_id. Per operations-sync.md §7.3 / §9.3 and realm-and-space.md §3.3, ak.space.update only mutates the Space's own metadata; it MUST NOT PATCH top-level state (archive/restore go through ak.space.archive / ak.space.restore) and MUST NOT move Strands (ak.strand.move / ak.strand.reorder). Reducer rejects update on a non-active Space (reason=space_not_active) — see conformance-vectors.md §6.7.

object_lifecycle_payload.description: Generic lifecycle payload for Strand / Circle / Morph archive-restore-tombstone style events. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; target_state may describe the intended lifecycle result but cannot replace the target object reference.

circle_member_state_payload.description: Payload for ak.circle.member.state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (Realm), scoped to a Circle; reducer MUST verify actor_id is a `join` member of the parent Realm before any transition to `join`, MUST gate `knock` on Circle join_rule=knock, and MUST reject self-unban/self-unremove paths.

circle_seal_commit_payload.description: Reducer-derived payload for ak.circle.seal_commit. Commits an opaque Circle sub-seal head digest into the parent Realm Seal stream at the profile-defined cadence.

restricted_policy_digest.description: Required when value=restricted. Digest of the effective ak.realm.history_sharing_policy value that defines restricted history visibility.

default_key_share.description: Baseline key-share rule before restricted_rules are evaluated. event_time_visibility still requires T0 history visibility, current safety policy, and receiver device checks.

allowed_receiver_states.description: Closed baseline key-share receiver-state allow-list. This is intentionally narrower than restricted_rules[].receiver_classes: preview_token_holder is a read/preview class, not a key-share state, and MUST never be inferred here or receive history key material solely from a preview token.

receiver_classes.description: Read-eligibility classes for this restricted rule. This axis intentionally includes preview_token_holder, unlike value.allowed_receiver_states. A preview token may authorize a bounded stub/projection but never satisfies the independent key-share receiver-state gate.

account_id.description: Opaque service-account identifier. It is the ak.component.account.status.v1 cell subject; accounts bound to the same principal_id are evaluated independently.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable account status diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes (for example deactivation_federation_incomplete).

supersedes_status_event_id.description: Event id of the ak.account.status event being superseded. Required by zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3 rule 2 when lowering severity (e.g. back to active after appeal). MUST NOT be used to downgrade erasure_pending (reason_code erasure_pending_is_terminal).

realm_set_default_strand_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.set_default_strand. Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. Reducer projects strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify strand_id references a projected, non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm; a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. The Strand projection is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage. expected_default_strand_id, when present, compiles to a cell head_eq precondition for optimistic concurrency (CAS); omission is no CAS.

expected_default_strand_id.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard. When present, the reducer accepts the write only if the Realm's current default_strand_id equals this value (null asserts no default is currently set). Mismatch MUST be rejected (failed_precondition).

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.archive and ak.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

membership_state.description: Canonical membership state enum shared by ak.member.state (Realm) and ak.circle.member.state (Circle). Single source of truth: Realm and Circle membership use the identical value set; they MUST NOT diverge. `knock` denotes a pending join request (Realm Join Policy / Circle join_rule=knock); see governance/join-policy.md §9 and models/circle.md §9.1.

gate_proofs.description: Join-policy gate proofs evaluated by governance/join-policy.md before accepting membership=join. maxItems aligns with the gates 1..16 bound in join_policy_payload; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

member_identity_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.member.identity.update. Append-only replacement event for one Realm-scoped member display/subject projection segment. Service-visible metadata names the segment and the prior events it replaces; the segment body is plaintext or the original encrypted envelope and MUST contain the complete data for that segment. Handle lifecycle is excluded from this event and is governed by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims.

segment.description: v1 core defines a single full MemberIdentity segment. Narrower segments require a future schema/profile revision that extends this enum or defines a new payload schema; v1 receivers MUST reject unknown segment values.

replaces.description: Prior ak.member.identity.update events in the same (realm_id, actor_id, segment) that this event supersedes for current profile projection. Referenced events remain immutable history.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the replaced event's full payload.identity_payload carrier wrapper ({member_identity: ...} or {encrypted_payload: ...}). Prevents replacing a different payload under a reused or confused event id.

identity_payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the exact identity_payload carrier object. It is a cache invalidation key, not a substitute for signature or MLS verification.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard for the current effective set of this (realm_id, actor_id, segment). When present, it MUST equal the writer-observed effective-set digest before applying this event: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON {realm_id, actor_id, segment, effective_events:[{event_id, segment, payload_digest}]}, with effective_events sorted by (segment,event_id). It is not the identity_payload_digest and not a roster member_display_state_digest.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service may receive. Human-readable purposes do not replace this field.

join_policy_payload.$comment: Value-shape schema for the realm.join_policy.v1 cell (written as a sub-component of ak.realm.policy_components). Structural validation is JSON Schema; property-level gate_id uniqueness within gates[] cannot be expressed in pure JSON Schema 2020-12, so it is enforced by (a) reducer rejection with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id and (b) tools/lint_artifacts.py check_join_policy_gate_id_uniqueness over fixtures and Markdown examples. uniqueItems below catches whole-object duplicates as a baseline. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3 / §3.1.

application_ttl.description: Join application pending lifetime as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT168H.

cooldown_after_reject.description: Minimum interval before the same actor may reapply after rejection, as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. PT72H.

read_receipt_policy_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.read_receipt_policy. Closed object so typos in receipt_compliance_opt_in or its sub-fields cause schema_violation. The enclosing Event carries realm_id; payload does not duplicate it. minProperties=1 rejects an empty no-op policy. Compliance exceptions exist only as sub-fields of receipt_compliance_opt_in; absent object / absent sub-field / false all mean not opted in. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.1.

receipt_compliance_opt_in.description: Structured compliance opt-in object replacing the three former parallel boolean escape switches. Absent object means nothing is opted in. Each sub-field defaults to false; absent / false / misspelled sub-fields all mean NOT opted in, so the reducer MUST treat them as reject (fail-closed). forced_public_world_readable_receipts is a SECOND gate on top of public_receipts_on_world_readable (the former being true does not relieve the latter). Closed object (additionalProperties=false) so unrecognized sub-fields are rejected with schema_violation at wire-parse time. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.1.

child_privacy_tightening_against_require.description: Privacy-floor escape switch. When the parent policy sets disclosure='required' and this is true, a child Realm MAY tighten disclosure to 'optional' or 'disabled'; otherwise the reducer rejects with read_receipt_compliance_floor_violated.

public_receipts_on_world_readable.description: Opt-in for the visibility='public' + history_visibility='world_readable' combination. When false the reducer MUST reject that combination (read_receipt_visibility_combination_invalid); when true it admits the combination with a warning diagnostic.

forced_public_world_readable_receipts.description: Second opt-in for disclosure='required' + visibility='public' + history_visibility='world_readable'. The reducer MUST reject the forced public world-readable combination (read_receipt_forced_public_world_readable_forbidden) unless this is true in addition to public_receipts_on_world_readable=true.

message_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.create. If content/encrypted_content contains an audience_mention AST node (for example @all or @here), reducer admission and notification dispatch MUST additionally enforce ak.message.mention.broadcast plus the audience policy / max_recipient / rate-limit rules in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered.

allOf.$comment: ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. Reducer initializes revision_root := id on create; only ak.message.revise events may set it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `revision_root/message_create_payload`.

mention_sidecar_digest.description: Optional E2EE mention-routing sidecar tags for push-notification fallback. Tags are opaque keyed-HMAC routing tokens produced by the sender client only when Realm policy enables recipient_registered_token routing; services compare them to recipient-registered opaque tokens and MUST NOT derive MLS exporter secrets.

reply_to.description: Optional creation convenience: the message this one replies to. The reducer records it as the message's reply linkage (lifting it onto the message content) and surfaces it as a replies_to relation in the message projection; it does not require a separate canonical ak.relation event. The materialized Message object itself carries no reply_to scalar. See strand-and-message.md §9.1.

agent_context.description: Auditable authorization context required when a native Agent authors the message.

expiry.description: Optional disappearing-message expiry contract for ak.profile.disappearing.v1. Expiry is projection / retention semantics and MUST NOT be treated as redaction.

message_revise_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.revise. Revisions that introduce new direct mentions MAY generate mention notifications only when the implementation can compare against the previous accepted visible revision. Revisions that introduce an audience_mention AST node (including @all / @here mappings) MUST satisfy the same ak.message.mention.broadcast and policy gates as create.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the target Strand. Optional on revise/redact: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message identified by message_id / target_ref / revision_of. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.
