Active track_name of the redacted message's parent Strand. Optional: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

trigger.description: Expiry anchor trigger. on_first_read / on_last_read are driven by private read cursor or policy-allowed receipt inputs through anonymous aggregate trigger contributions; expiry metadata MUST NOT expose reader identity.

grace_ms.description: Additional local projection / key-drop grace. Does not extend the Realm policy maximum lifetime.

read_trigger_window_ms.description: Maximum wait window for on_last_read aggregate contributions. If omitted, implementations MUST use max_ttl_ms. This window is metadata-only and MUST NOT expose reader identity or unread reader count.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Strand id; encoded as a ak:strand: typed id.

comment.description: RSVP comment. MUST be an encrypted_payload unless Realm policy explicitly permits a plaintext-visible RSVP comment (calendar-event.md §5).

oneOf.description: Plaintext RSVP comment; only permitted when Realm policy lists the receiving service as plaintext-visible.

reaction_payload.description: Reducer input for ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove. OR-Set membership is keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key); a remove tombstones every prior add from the same actor with the same key in the causal past. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8 for the authoritative Reaction model (target scope, OR-Set, authz, anti-abuse) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the plaintext-vs-encrypted policy.

key.description: Reaction key. Plaintext realms SHOULD use a single Unicode emoji cluster or registered short tag. End-to-end-encrypted realms with `aad_visibility != opaque_id` MUST carry the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag here (`HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("arkret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji))`), naturally bound to the current MLS group + epoch via the exporter secret; see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the authoritative construction. This lets OR-Set dedup, rate-limit and reducer convergence keep working without revealing the chosen emoji; the canonical emoji travels in `encrypted_payload`.

annotation.description: Optional free-form annotation (e.g. issue triage label). MUST be omitted when `encrypted_payload` is present; in E2EE realms the annotation MUST instead be carried inside `encrypted_payload`.

encrypted_payload.description: Encrypted carrier for the canonical reaction key and any annotation in E2EE realms. The decrypted plaintext JSON MUST validate as #/$defs/reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext. When present, outer plaintext `key` MUST be the routing tag and `annotation` MUST be omitted; service-side OR-Set convergence still uses the outer routing key.

reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext.description: Plaintext JSON encrypted into reaction_payload.encrypted_payload.ciphertext for ak.reaction.add / ak.reaction.remove in E2EE realms. The outer reaction_payload.key remains required and carries the service-visible routing tag; this plaintext carries the real reaction key and optional user content.

key.description: Canonical reaction key after client-side normalization: a single NFC Unicode emoji cluster or profile-registered short tag. This is the real reaction key, not the outer HMAC routing tag.

annotation.description: Optional user-visible annotation associated with the reaction.

remove_add_event_ids.description: Optional client-side convergence accelerator for ak.reaction.remove: add event ids that this remove intends to tombstone. MUST be omitted on ak.reaction.add. Service-side reducers still rely on the outer event actor_id, target_ref, key, and causal frontier.

agent_key_scope.description: Agent scope object with two uses. In POST /_arkret/self/agents requested_scope it is the required immutable global Agent ceiling; in ak.agent.key.authorize it is a per-key ceiling that MAY be narrower but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of the provision ceiling. It is never a capability grant. actions may contain service operation ids and content action tokens; an omitted action can never be restored by a key, Realm grant, participation selection or session. resources constrain the service surface and may optionally narrow later content resources, but never authorize content by themselves. Provisioning and pairing do not materialize capability grants from this object; effective authority is the intersection of provision ceiling, key ceiling, independent Realm-scoped grants, participation, session request, membership and policy.

actions.description: Literal action ceiling. Every downstream key scope, grant or session action MUST appear here; action families, prefixes and subsumption do not widen it.

resources.description: Selector ceiling, not authorization. Each downstream selector must be covered by a parent selector. operation/service parents cover the same kind and matching explicit field and cannot carry content fields. The content-kind vocabulary is the ResourceSelector vocabulary except '*'; kind=realm covers every Realm-local content kind in the matching Realm and other content kinds cover only the same kind. Omitted parent realm_id is a cross-Realm ceiling wildcard and omitted exact ref is a same-kind/same-Realm wildcard. With no content selector, later Realm grants still choose concrete resources and no content wildcard is granted.

constraints.description: Global mandatory constraints. Every effective key/grant/session evaluation MUST retain and AND these constraints; downstream scopes may add stricter constraints but MUST NOT omit or relax provision constraints.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key. Durable grant/approval/proposal/policy evidence carries ref so it can be replayed at the event frontier; the short-lived pairing_request branch instead binds pairing_request_id, request_canonical_digest, and approved_by and MUST omit ref.

pairing_request_id.description: Optional profile-local, short-lived pairing artifact id. Required by the agent-key pairing acceptance flow and MUST equal the pairing_request_id in the accepted request; it is not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, approval evidence, and both the service-surface and content-capability ceilings that later agent_key_proof sessions must narrow from.

public_key_digest.description: Digest of the public key material behind verification_method. Native Agent authorization always commits this value; receivers compare it with the disclosed raw Ed25519 key.

signing_key_binding_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical ak.schema.agent_signing_key_binding.v1 object. This commitment makes the controller-authorized Event and the minimal public disclosure inseparable; a service MUST NOT substitute another disclosure.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the key authorization is non-expiring and governed solely by revocation (ak.agent.key.revoke / lifecycle cascade).

supersedes.description: Exact set of every active Agent-key authorization dot observed immediately before this controller-signed authorization is accepted during runtime re-pairing. Each entry binds both the key id and the authorization Event that introduced the active dot. The array MUST be omitted only for first pairing, when the authoritative active set is empty. Every replacement MUST set-equal the complete pre-accept active authorization set, including an old dot with the same key_id as the new authorization; a stale, partial, extra, or implicit map overwrite fails closed. Acceptance atomically removes these dots with reason superseded_by_repairing and adds this authorize dot, so no server-forged ak.agent.key.revoke Event is required.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. When expires_at is absent, authorization lifetime is governed by the canonical revocation chain and lifecycle cascade; this field may identify the freshness source used for that check.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time. v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_digest.description: Optional digest of verifiable attestation material when kind is not self_asserted.

attestation_ref.description: Optional external verifiable attestation reference (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.).

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.revoke. The or_set cell subject is (agent_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is covered by an accepted Seal. The authoring basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the payload carries no frontier field.

agent_sidecar_exposure_ack.description: Controller acknowledgement of Agent Sidecar objects that entered the Agent's derived exposure set while the Agent was paused. This acknowledgement changes desired access only; effective access still requires backing-scope and MLS reconciliation.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.pause. The status cell is keyed by agent_id and moves from active to paused. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the reducer accepts the transition only under the accepted current control frontier.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.resume. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, accountability grant, and any sidecar exposure acknowledgement against the accepted current control frontier before returning the agent to active.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.deactivate. Revocation fan-out and future agent-session rejection are judged at the accepted Seal covering this Move (or its successors); the authoring basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis. The payload carries no frontier field.

previous_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent at deactivation time. Runtime key readiness is the orthogonal derived runtime_state projection and never appears here (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.draft.propose. Actor-private proposal that may materialize into controller-owned encrypted draft account data after policy checks.

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_approve. Controller approval binds the draft/action request, target, approved payload digest, expiry, and single-use nonce.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates a draft/action request without shared Realm side effects.

consent_grant_payload.description: Holder-private consent grant. The actor (consenter) is the holder; payload.peer is the counterparty whose contact is consented to. Wire-equivalent to a Move whose effect is add(tag,value) on the cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (or_set lattice); ak.consent.revoke writes a remove on the same cell. Lives in the holder's Principal Control Realm (or holder-private actor stream); MUST NOT be written to a shared Collaboration Realm. Realm role taxonomy: zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7.

consent_id.description: Stable identifier; used as the cell_subject of the consent cell. ak.consent.revoke MUST reference the same consent_id.

peer.description: Counterparty DID (or pairwise DID) that this consent applies to.

consent_scope.description: What kind of contact is consented to. 'invite' = peer may send Realm / Strand invites; 'direct_message' = peer may initiate 1:1 message; 'voice_call' / 'video_call' = peer may initiate WebRTC call; 'presence' = peer may observe presence; 'any' = full consent across all consent scopes.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

consent_revoke_payload.description: Revoke a previously granted consent. Wire-equivalent to a Control Move whose effect is remove(tag) on the consent cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (the same cell written by ak.consent.grant). Payload observed_dots MUST match the Control Move effect's observed_dots so schema validation and audit can see exactly what was removed.

consent_id.description: MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked.

observed_dots.description: Exact add dots being removed. A full revoke, including consent_scope=any cascade, MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive; implicit cascade without dot enumeration is invalid.

direct_conversation_authorization_basis.description: Canonical authorization basis for creating a Direct Conversation. accepted_contact references the accepted contact facts; managed_agent_controller references the accepted managed-Agent provisioning/controller/runtime-key facts that bind the peer Agent to the requester controller.

contact_requested_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is the requester; target is the holder being asked to accept. This fact lives in the requester's Principal Control Realm and may be mirrored by the target as the original signed envelope.

request_id.description: SHOULD equal the enclosing ak.contact.requested event_id.

requester_consent_refs.description: Consent grant event refs written by requester for every requested scope.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Optional digest of the private contact request introduction_evidence carried by PeerContactDeliveryRequest. Raw evidence is not written into the contact fact log.

contact_accepted_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact accept fact. Issuer is the original request target; requester is the peer whose request was accepted. Accepting writes target-controlled consent grants and references them here.

contact_rejected_payload.description: Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is the original request target. Rejecting does not grant or revoke consent by itself.

contact_tombstoned_payload.description: Principal-scoped holder tombstone for one contact relation view. Issuer is the holder ending their side of the contact. Default revocation scope is contact-managed active consent dots only.

direct_conversation_bound_payload.description: Principal-scoped signed binding from an unordered participant pair to the canonical DM Realm and main Strand. Issuer MUST be one of the participants; the original signed envelope may be mirrored by the other participant.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key: sha256(JCS({participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain})) where p0/p1 are canonical stable subject DIDs sorted by unsigned UTF-8 byte order. Receivers MUST recompute it exactly as contact-and-direct-conversation.md §7 defines; handles and unresolved pairwise DIDs are forbidden inputs.

member_event_refs.description: Membership event refs proving both participants are active members of the DM Realm.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group bound to this DM Realm candidate.

mls_genesis_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.mls.genesis Event for mls_group_id in realm scope.

mls_commit_event_ref.description: Accepted epoch-0 Add Commit Event that admits the peer KeyPackage.

mls_welcome_event_ref.description: Accepted Welcome Event paired with mls_commit_event_ref.

binding_state.description: Authored fact state. duplicate and non_canonical are derived projection states selected by the canonical candidate reducer and are never authored on wire.

invitee.description: Directed invite subject DID. On ak.invite.create it selects the directed branch and carries the conditional ak.component.member.state.v1 leave -> invite effect. On ak.invite.cancel / ak.invite.revoke targeting a directed DID invite it is REQUIRED and MUST equal the invitee recorded on the target invite cell; the same Control Move then carries the atomic invite -> leave member.state effect. 3PID placeholder invites carry no invitee and MUST NOT produce a member.state effect.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. payload.invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

expires_at.description: Invite expiry timestamp. Directed v1 invite creates MUST carry it; reducers MUST NOT infer indefinite validity.

subject_id.description: Subject DID being bound by a ak.invite.claim payload. For claim payloads this MUST match binding_proof.subject_id and the DID verification method used by subject_proof.

token_commitment.description: Reducer-matched salted commitment for the pending ak.invite.third_party record. Raw invite tokens, URL fragments, SMS codes, or plaintext 3PID values MUST NOT appear on wire.

claim_nonce.description: One-time nonce scoped to (invite_id, token_commitment). Reducers MUST reject nonce replay while preserving non-enumerable external responses.

binding_proof.description: Verification-service proof for ak.invite.claim. Reducers verify signature over the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript against the invite's verification_public_key and current Realm verification_service_id allowlist before accepting a claimed transition.

verification_service_id.description: Verification service DID. Realm reducers MUST re-check this DID against the current effective Realm allowlist and any service DID pinned by the original invite.

verification_method.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0; matches the strict form used by $defs/verification_method elsewhere in this schema.

subject_id.description: DID being bound by the verification service. MUST equal the payload top-level subject_id.

realm_id.description: Realm bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the Event envelope realm_id.

claim_nonce.description: Nonce bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the payload top-level claim_nonce.

expires_at.description: Proof expiration. Reducers MUST reject expired proofs and MUST also enforce the invite cell expires_at.

signature.description: Signature over utf8("ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json({audience, binding_proof: unsigned_binding_proof, claim_nonce, invite_digest, invite_id, realm_id, subject_id, token_commitment, verification_service_id}); unsigned_binding_proof is this object without signature.

subject_proof.description: Subject DID proof over ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript. The transcript digest binds subject_id, invite_id, realm_id, token_commitment, claim_nonce, audience, verification_service_id, and binding_proof_digest of the complete signed binding_proof object.

verification_method.description: Current verification method of subject_id.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the canonical ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript.

hpke_key.description: Device HPKE public key used for secret/key envelope sealing. MUST be covered by cross_signing_binding (§5.2) or enrollment-authority Event proof (§5.4); services MUST NOT substitute this value in projection.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids supported by this device. Enters device trust binding transcript together with device_public_key and hpke_key.

device_signature.description: Device possession proof for ak.device.authorize. When present, it MUST be an Ed25519/EdDSA detached signature by the private key corresponding to device_public_key over the ak.device-authorize-possession-v1 canonical input defined in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5.2. It MUST NOT be signed by the grant-binding (DPoP) key / session_public_key / cnf.jkt key. Recovery-strand device authorization requires this field.

recovery_session_id.description: Present when this authorization was produced by a device recovery strand (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15). Binds the event to the recovery_session_id used by the proof transcript, backup-decrypt proofs, and the recovery_receipt, so an auditor reading only the control stream can correlate authorization to receipt. Omitted for ordinary pairing-based authorizations. Not part of the cross_signing_binding signing input (§5.2).

device_reanchor_payload.description: Closed payload for the B-model DID-root recovery anchor. Fields are ordered identity, DID generation, accepted pre-fence basis, then the exact replacement authorization binding. Generation projection fields are reducer-managed and MUST NOT be added here.

did_version_id.description: Verified did:webvh entry versionId. Its numeric prefix defines the re-anchor conflict slot.

device_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.device.revoke. The revocation's control-plane authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis (covered by the canonical event bytes and proofs); its effective cutoff is the accepted Seal covering this Move. The payload carries no frontier field.

key_backup_active_series_payload.description: Payload for ak.key_backup.active_series. The standalone ak.schema.key_backup_active_series.v1 schema carries the authoritative signed active-series record shape.

cross_signing_publish_payload.description: Payload for ak.cross_signing.publish. Schema ak.schema.cross_signing_publish.v1 (cross-signing-publish.schema.json) carries the authoritative shape; this payload entry mirrors the required-field set so the kind-specific payload class is wired into event-payload.schema.json dispatch. See device-lifecycle.md §5.1.

cross_signing_reset_payload.description: Payload for ak.cross_signing.reset. Schema ak.schema.cross_signing_reset.v1 (cross-signing-reset.schema.json) carries the authoritative shape; this payload entry mirrors the required-field set so the kind-specific payload class is wired into event-payload.schema.json dispatch. See device-lifecycle.md §14.1.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the claimed MLS KeyPackage bytes. MUST equal the referenced ak.mls.keypackage.payload.keypackage_digest and claim_ref.keypackage_digest.

claim_ref.description: KeyPackage claim binding used by the receiver before decrypting the Welcome. claim_id, keypackage_ref, and keypackage_digest must match the top-level fields; capabilities_digest is sha256(JCS(claimed_capabilities)) from the single-use claim response. Exactly one trust binding is present: ssk_generation for cross-signing devices, device_authorize_event_id for service-attested enrollment-authority devices, or agent_key_authorize_event_id for an independently authorized Native Agent runtime.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event for the claimed Native Agent runtime key.

claim_envelope.description: Detached requester signature binding the claimed KeyPackage to this Welcome, Realm, claim nonce, and Welcome digest before decrypting the Welcome. Exactly one requester signing binding is present: ssk_generation for requester SSK signatures, or requester_device_id for service-attested requester device signatures.

peer_claim_receipt.description: Required when the KeyPackage was claimed through the peer claim protocol. The receiving destination Principal Server validates this signed receipt against its durable claim ledger before accepting the Welcome.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the MLS KeyPackage bytes identified by keypackage_ref.

share_kind.description: Discriminator for the key-share target. member_device seals history_secret material to a concrete authorized recipient device. realm_recovery_key seals the same material to a durability_policy RecoveryRecipient RRK verification method (crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10.8).

recipient_principal_id.description: For member_device shares, the member principal receiving the history key. For realm_recovery_key shares, the durability_policy.recovery_recipients[].principal_id that published the RRK verification method.

recipient_device_id.description: Required only for share_kind=member_device. The concrete authorized recipient device whose HPKE public key receives the sealed history_secret material.

recipient_verification_method.description: Required only for share_kind=realm_recovery_key. DID URL of the RRK HPKE public key, equal to durability_policy.recovery_recipients[].verification_method and designated by an active ArkretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry in recipient_principal_id's DID Document.

recovery_recipient_id.description: Required only for share_kind=realm_recovery_key. Stable durability_policy.recovery_recipients[].recipient_id covered by this RRK seal.

source_authorization_ref.description: Accepted policy/grant/source-authorisation Control Move proving that sender_device_id may deliver this share_kind and key_scope to the named recipient at the Event CBA basis. It is covered by sender_device_signature and MUST be independently verified before installing history_secret material.

sender_device_signature.description: Detached device signature over the canonical share transcript fixed by crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md 13. The transcript carries context "ak.realm-key-share-sender-proof-v1" and binds share_kind, sender_device_id, source_authorization_ref, recipient_principal_id, the selected variant target fields (recipient_device_id OR recipient_verification_method + recovery_recipient_id), key_scope, exactly one of ciphertext / encrypted_key_ref, aad_digest?, expires_at? and created_at. Unselected branch fields, the unselected material field and absent optional fields MUST be omitted from the transcript and MUST NOT be written as null.

share_kind.description: Discriminator shared with realm_key_share_payload so both kinds derive the same ak.component.realm_key.delivery.v1 cell subject. v1 registers member_device only: durable realm_recovery_key withheld semantics are not defined (crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md 2.10.8 handles RRK seal failure through fail-closed error paths).

source_authorization_ref.description: Accepted policy/grant/source-authorisation Control Move proving that sender_device_id may decide delivery for this recipient, target and key_scope at the Event CBA basis. A withheld carries subject-level terminal semantics, so receivers MUST verify it and reject the Event with late_recovery_share_not_authorized when it is missing or does not cover the decision.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. Implementations MUST NOT infer key scope from strand_id or track.

policy_digest.description: Hash of the effective Realm/Circle policy root that is the basis of this delivery decision. For ak.realm_key.share it is the root authorising the historical key delivery. For ak.realm_key.withheld it is the root the source actually evaluated when refusing delivery; it pins the refusal basis and does NOT assert that the share was ever authorised. The source MUST resolve a single effective root on the Event CBA/T0 basis and MUST NOT emit a durable withheld with a zero value, the receiver-current root or an implementation placeholder.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional hash of the membership frontier evaluated for history visibility and recipient membership.

control_frontier.description: Sorted accepted control refs that materialize the Sidecar and exact desired backing membership. Semantic validation requires UTF-8 byte-lexicographic order and equality with the current server-derived Sidecar MLS context.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm identifier. MUST equal effective_scope.realm_id.

circle_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='circle'. MUST equal effective_scope.circle_id.

effective_scope.description: Tagged MLS governance scope. Realm-default groups use {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle groups use {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. This field, not Strand id or track, determines key and membership scope.

sidecar_binding.description: Required by semantic admission when effective_scope is the reducer-managed backing Circle of an Agent Sidecar; forbidden for all other MLS scopes.

binding_profile.description: Explicit profile that defines how this governance binding is interpreted. Full E2EE uses ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1; the only v1 downgrade profile is ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing, unsupported, inconsistent with the Realm profile declaration, or used to imply a downgrade without the matching policy/profile declaration.

reducer_profile.description: Reducer profile identifier used to interpret membership_frontier, policy_root, capability_root, and covered_seals_cell semantics. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing or does not match the reducer profile negotiated for the Realm/federation peer.

mls_governance_binding.$comment: Schema requires the tagged scope and circle_id presence rules. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare realm_id == effective_scope.realm_id and, for circle scope, circle_id == effective_scope.circle_id; JSON Schema cannot express cross-field equality for these string values.

mls_genesis_payload.$comment: Schema requires both effective_scope and governance_binding. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare effective_scope with governance_binding.effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express deep cross-field equality.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the MLS group created at epoch 0. MUST match governance_binding.effective_scope.

base_epoch.description: Expected previous MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.previous_epoch.

next_epoch.description: Committed next MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.next_epoch.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / authorized registry-authz service; a self-signed registration alone MUST NOT write to a Realm (reason=applet_registration_unauthorized). registration MUST be signed by the controller DID (proof per models/event-and-patch.md §3).

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier: a DID or the typed-id form ak:applet:<uuidv7>.

service_id.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_id.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used as the app/bridge->arkret inbound source signature anchor and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID from Source-Service-ID instead.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

proof.description: Controller-DID detached signature over the canonical registration object (excluding proof). An empty proof object MUST be rejected as schema_violation; required proof fields per models/event-and-patch.md §3.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ak.mimi.room_binding. Writes the ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json cell_subject). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of a Arkret Realm/Strand discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ak.policy.manage, ak.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the MLS Governance Binding covered_seals_cell precondition.

mimi_room_uri.description: MIMI room URI. Cell subject for ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

binding_scope.description: Arkret Realm + Strand scope this MIMI room projects. strand_id MUST point at an accepted Strand with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Strand's discussion track.

hub_provider.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

policy_root.description: Digest of the Arkret policy component projection bound to this MIMI room binding.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes; migrating stops new writes until a verified migration proof returns the binding to accepted or revoked.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision. A sealed moderation decision that writes an or_set add effect onto the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell whose subject is target_ref (the moderated target_event_id / target_object_id canonical string). See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §2.6 / §8.1. Multiple active adds are a normal joinable OR-Set value and fold deterministically by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review > none; they are not moderation_control_split merely because more than one entry exists. This sealed payload accepts only hard_deny / quarantine / require_review. Runtime allow and soft_deny remain out-of-band Policy Server outcomes and MUST NOT be persisted as ak.moderation.decision adds. The optional action carries the finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family. The actor MUST independently hold ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage; refs[role=authorized_by] SHOULD reference the Policy Server signed decision for audit (not a capability source).

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell subject.

decision.description: Sealed moderation-state decision verb (content-moderation.md §2.6 / §8.1). Lower snake_case. allow and soft_deny are out-of-band runtime outcomes and are intentionally excluded.

issuer.description: Actor or service DID issuing the sealed moderation decision. Reducers use it as part of the or_set add tag and appeal separation-of-duties check.

request_canonical_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the moderated request or event preview bound to the Policy Server decision. Part of the moderation_state or_set add tag.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

policy_decision_ref.description: Reference to the Policy Server signed decision used as risk evidence. Audit / replay only; not a capability source.

modify_decision_ref.description: Set when this decision is the new decision emitted atomically by an appeal verdict=modify (content-moderation.md §5.5.2); reducer verifies it matches the same-batch appeal event id.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision.lift. Writes an or_set remove effect on the same ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell, removing the tag previously added by the decision identified by decision_ref. See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2 (appeal verdict=overturn MUST pair a lift whose target equals decision_ref in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction).

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell the lift mutates. Same cell subject as the original ak.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ak.moderation.decision Event whose sealed tag is being removed.

audit_applet_binding_payload.description: Payload for ak.audit.applet_binding. Writes the control-plane FSM cell ak.component.audit.binding.v1 keyed by binding_id. Initial status is active; legal transitions are active->suspended, suspended->active, active->revoked, and suspended->revoked; revoked is terminal. The binding is non-retroactive and does not make the applet an MLS member or realtime sync recipient. Messages encrypted before activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch are never eligible for this binding's ak.audit.release.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ak.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_kinds.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_session_payload.description: Shared payload class for ak.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The session_state field is the target state of the control-plane FSM cell ak.component.audit.session.v1 keyed by session_id. Initial state is request; legal main-path transitions are request->authorize->notice->close, with request->close and authorize->close allowed for aborted sessions. Close is terminal; same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.

approved_recipient_audit_actor_id.description: Audit subject approved to receive release material. Required on ak.audit.session.authorize; ak.audit.release.recipient_audit_actor_id MUST match it byte-for-byte.

approved_recipient_public_key_ref.description: Audit release recipient key approved by ak.audit.session.authorize. MUST resolve to approved_recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key; ak.audit.release.recipient_public_key_ref MUST match it byte-for-byte.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ak.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It appends to the control-plane ordered log ak.component.audit.release.v1 keyed by session_id only while the accepted session FSM head is notice. Same-basis close dominates and rejects the release. The payload records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

recipient_public_key_ref.description: Release material encryption target. MUST equal the authorize payload's approved_recipient_public_key_ref and resolve to recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ak.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ak.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_identity, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ak.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ak.realm.media_service.service_id.

call_participant.description: A single participant value added by ak.call.state.payload.roster_delta. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

call_state_payload.description: Typed delta payload for ak.call.state. Every present field maps to one or two explicit registered cell effects; omitted axes produce no effect.

result.description: Typed recording outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent recording result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

artifact.description: Canonical artifact metadata for recording_transition.to=ready. It binds the Arkret blob, recording exporter context, retention policy and deletion audit surface.

failure_message.description: Human-readable diagnostic for recording_state=failed. It MUST NOT contain recording plaintext or backend direct URLs.

result.description: Typed transcription outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent transcript result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

call_summary_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.summary (durable end-of-call summary). Written once after a call reaches a terminal `state`; carries duration, peak participant count, and capture status so clients can render a durable call record without replaying ephemeral signaling. See crypto-media/call-state.md §7. started_at/ended_at/duration_ms are nullable: non-active terminal states (missed/cancelled/failed) MUST set them null per call-state.md §7.

final_state.description: The terminal call lifecycle state this summary closes over. MUST be one of the call_state_payload terminal states.

peak_participant_count.description: Highest concurrent participant count observed during the call.

distinct_participant_count.description: Number of distinct (actor_id, device_id) participants that joined at any point.

recording_state.description: Final recording_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state for the durable record. Absent = the call was not recorded.

transcript_state.description: Final transcript_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state. Absent = the call was not transcribed.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. REQUIRED: it selects the target capture cell family (ak.component.call.recording.v1 vs ak.component.call.transcript.v1) in the registered cell contract, so it MUST NOT be inferred from a missing-field default.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

result.description: Initial immutable capture evidence. The start-event reference MUST equal this Event's event_id; retention.consent_confirmed=true closes the pre-capture consent gate before the FSM enters a capturing state.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the cas_register cell value as 'list_space_id' on the cell at ak:cell:ak.component.strand.position.v1:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ak.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch cell. The new cell value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event whose payload access_kind=watch_set_others identifies writer / target / cell / before-after heads. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the cell (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Compiles to cas_register head_eq precondition. Whole-value compare against the cell pre-state: either null (assert no prior record) or { level, level_public? } matching the prior cell value exactly. When omitted, reducers MUST treat it as head_eq null: only the initial write may pass; an existing cell MUST fail_precondition. Omission MUST NOT disable CAS or imply last-write-wins.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a cell does not carry a public-level setting).

schemas/federated-device-signing-key-evi.title: Arkret Federated Device Signing Key Evidence
schemas/federated-device-signing-key-evi.description: Portable device-key authorization evidence. The original accepted service-attested ak.device.authorize Event cryptographically binds the key to the principal's DID-designated enrollment authority; the authenticated source Principal Server attests only that the authorization is current and active. Transport-only: this object never enters another Event digest, Realm reducer, Seal, or timeline.

verification_method.description: MUST equal actor_id + '#' + device_id.

device_signing_key.description: Ed25519 device signing public key. The multibase suffix MUST equal device_authorize_event.payload.device_public_key.

authorization_accepted_at.description: Source authority's server-sealed acceptance time for device_authorize_event. The destination uses this time for historical DID/enrollment-authority resolution; it MUST be no earlier than the Event created_at and no later than the source service attestation time.

device_authorize_event.description: Original accepted ak.device.authorize Event. It MUST target actor_id/device_id, carry enrollment_authority_binding.kind=service_attested, bind device_signing_key, and have portable proofs with no service-specific domain or audience. The destination independently verifies its proof against the DID-designated enrollment authority.

schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.title: Arkret File Transfer Account Data
schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.description: Plaintext shape that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.file_transfer.v1 account-data values.

content_digest.description: Digest of the stored blob bytes. For encrypted file transfer this is the ciphertext digest and MUST NOT be a plaintext file hash.

blob_size_bytes.description: Size of the stored blob bytes, usually ciphertext plus AEAD overhead.

media_type.description: Original file media type. This field lives inside encrypted account data; encrypted blob metadata SHOULD use application/octet-stream.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: Original file byte length before client-side encryption.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming chunked AEAD form: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

content_key.description: Fresh per-transfer content key carried only inside encrypted account-data plaintext.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file file-transfer key message: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming file-transfer key message: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

enc.description: HPKE KEM encapsulated key for the recipient device.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.title: Arkret Grant Constraint
schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, kind_restriction, scope_limitation, delegation_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_kind.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with constraint_subkind); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with constraint_subkind). Use the optional 'constraint_subkind' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_kind has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

constraint_subkind.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_kind. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}. Per constraint-schema.md §2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent constraint_subkind: it is the claim_based constraint_subkind=claim sub-case expressed via claim issuer = device cross-signing key. Implementations MAY require constraint_subkind for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ak.message.revise.own', 'ak.message.redact.own']). Action mismatch is neutral in the effect fold: satisfied for effect=allow and not matched for deny/quarantine/require_review.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ak.circle.manage / ak.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits applet interop-session operations to the listed applet-defined session correlation ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ak.self.blob.command.presign grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_labels.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_delegation_depth.description: Maximum remaining delegation hops. Bounded by the canonical delegation chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md §3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ak.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

max_operations.description: Maximum number of distinct accepted idempotency identities in one UTC epoch-aligned fixed period. Enforcement is a linearizable check-and-reserve at one logical quota authority shared by every node in the enforcing service; per-node duplicated budgets and overshoot are forbidden.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration. For quota constraints, a stricter conditional schema permits only a non-zero fixed-length week/day/hour/minute/second duration; year/month durations are forbidden so every authority derives the same UTC epoch-aligned window id.

burst.description: Optional token-bucket capacity at the same logical quota authority, capped by max_operations and refilled at max_operations/period. It never increases the fixed-window total budget.

constraint_scope.description: Closed v1 quota counting scope. Unknown values are schema violations and MUST fail closed. Quota counters are actor-bound; the enum selects the additional slicing dimension: actor only, actor+space, actor+realm, or actor across all nodes/regions of the enforcing service's global quota domain. global is not an implicit federation-wide counter. Every node in the service domain MUST share one logical linearizable quota authority.

required_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject DID MUST match the actor DID.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Values mirror Realm/Circle encryption_profile. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the Realm's current encryption_profile (see constraint-schema.md §12).

plaintext_fallback_allowed.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext when the encryption floor cannot be met. See constraint-schema.md §12.

audit_trail_required.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md §12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see policy-server.md §7.1 and capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ak.strand.update / ak.message.create / org membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-constraint_subkind form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a constraint_subkind (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_kind":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no constraint_subkind passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no constraint_subkind is the valid ordinary time-window form.
Rate quotas need an explicit counting scope; otherwise SDKs cannot derive a stable counter key.
quota constraint_subkind=rate is a complete hard-quota tuple; partial rate constraints are invalid.
burst is a modifier of a complete rate quota and cannot stand alone.
Cumulative resource quotas need an explicit counting scope; single-operation fields such as blob_max_bytes do not.
Cumulative resource-count quotas need an explicit counting scope.
Quota periods must have a fixed duration so all nodes derive the same UTC epoch-aligned window. Calendar years/months and zero/empty durations are not valid quota periods.
An edit window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=edit_window requires the edit duration field.
A redact window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=redact_window requires the redact duration field.
redact_after_window_allowed modifies message_edit_window and is invalid without it.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators / contract-registry consumers disambiguate this claim from other DID-bearing envelopes.

handle_aliases.description: Interop aliases such as RFC 7565 acct:. Aliases are never canonical; verifiers MUST normalize to handle before cache lookup, proof comparison, or delivery_binding construction.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID for a user/principal handle. This is the stable DID the handle resolves to; it is not a Realm actor_id, server-local account_id, administrative identifier, service DID, or generic resource id.

issuer.description: DID of the handle authority. Bare hostnames are discovery inputs, never proof issuers.

issuer_service_id.description: Service DID that signed, served, or vouched for this handle claim when distinct from issuer.

claim_kind.description: Protocol-level kind of holder/principal handle claim. v1 intentionally does not allow the earlier draft service_handle value: service-readable names or resource labels need their own service/resource schema, while organization-assigned user/principal handles use organization_handle.

visibility.description: Default disclosure boundary for this handle claim.

audience.description: Audience binding for the claim. For handle claims used to build a Realm delivery_binding, audience is the target Realm ID, the inviting service DID, or another verifier domain the proofs explicitly bind to. Verifier MUST reject claims whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_scope.description: Optional claim_scope such as organization_id, realm_id, purpose, or allowed operations.

member_delivery_binding.description: Single source for the Principal Server service DID and delivery parameters this handle claim offers to the membership builder. Top-level delivery shortcuts are forbidden; use member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_id, member_delivery_binding.service_acceptance_ref, and member_delivery_binding.policy_event_ref.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.title: Arkret Media ICE Config Result
schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ak.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

actor_id.description: Actor that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

issued_at_bucket.description: Coarse UTC bucket start used for TURN pseudonym derivation. MUST equal floor(issued_at / bucket_seconds) * bucket_seconds. Bound into the signature so TURN usernames cannot be correlated across buckets by rewriting metadata.

bucket_seconds.description: TURN pseudonym bucket size in seconds. v1 fixes the default and interoperable value at 300s; clients SHOULD refresh before crossing the next bucket.

expires_at.description: Convenience field equal to issued_at + ttl_seconds. MUST match within signature validation.

turn_required.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response is a soft failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

kid.description: Verification method id, typically <media_service_id>#<key-id>. Bare DID is accepted (resolves to the controller's current key); DID URLs with key fragment are RECOMMENDED. The optional `#<key-id>` fragment is allowed (charset aligned with the token-exchange service_signature.kid pattern).

alg.description: Signature algorithm. Values MUST be active proof_alg entries in signature-alg-registry.json. Default v1 deployments use EdDSA; stronger or deployment-specific profiles MAY require another registered algorithm while preserving the exact signing input defined in webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.

signature_input.description: Domain-separation label prepended to the ICE config signing bytes. v1 fixes this to ak.media.ice_config.v1 and it MUST NOT be reused for participant binding signatures.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the RFC 8785 canonical ICE config response object with the top-level signature field removed. This is the canonical payload covered after the signature_input label and 0x00 separator.

sig.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.title: Arkret Minimal-Metadata Identity Link
schemas/identity-link.schema.json.description: Encrypted application-message or MLS private-extension payload that binds a Realm-scoped pairwise DID to the real principal DID for ak.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1. The binding is scoped to both realm_id and trust_domain so the same pairwise mapping cannot be replayed across deployments. This object is never written to public Realm history unless a separate disclosure policy explicitly permits it.

pairwise_did.description: Realm-scoped pairwise DID used in Event.actor_id and MLS leaf credential. The v1 boundary is the Realm, not a Matrix-style Room.

principal_id.description: Real principal DID that controls or has disclosed the pairwise DID.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain. Receiver MUST require this value to match the current Realm / service trust_domain before accepting a pairwise DID -> principal DID mapping.

strand_id.description: Optional application-message context marker for the Strand carrying the identity link. It does not create independent membership or key scope; key scope is determined by effective_scope.

track_name.description: Optional display-track context marker for application routing. Track names do not create independent membership, policy, or MLS key scope.

mls_group_id.description: Optional MLS group identifier (base64url RFC 9420 GroupID) for diagnostic / cross-implementation correlation. NOT used by the reducer for authorization — authoritative MLS group state lives in ak.mls.genesis / ak.mls.commit events. Provided here so audit projections can quickly correlate an identity-link with its MLS group without replaying the full epoch chain.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a key controlled by principal_id or by a disclosure proof accepted by Realm policy. Fragment is REQUIRED (this is a DID URL, not a bare DID). DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical input bytes: utf8('ak.identity-link-v1\n') || canonical_json(identity-link object with proof.signature omitted). The signed object includes trust_domain.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

signature.description: Registry detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.identity-receipt-proof-v1', payload_digest, registry_service_id, did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid assertion method controlled by registry_service_id. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.title: Arkret InclusionList
schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.description: FOCIL-style control-plane inclusion list. A non-proposer notary signer lists pending Control Move digests that passed its local verification; the next Seal MUST include, signed-reject, or prove batch pre-state verification failure for every listed digest, otherwise receivers MUST reject that Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3). single_did notary profiles cannot provide this mechanism. The list is an accountability object, not a Seal: it never advances governance state by itself.

signer_id.description: Notary signer issuing the list. MUST be an eligible non-proposer signer of the Realm's multi-signer notary profile at issue time.

list_seq.description: Per-signer monotonic inclusion-list sequence. Two different canonical lists from the same signer with the same (realm_id, list_seq) constitute equivocation evidence under the section 7.1 slot rule.

event_digests.description: Canonical ascending list of pending Control Move event digests that passed the issuer's local verification and hold a valid receipt.

expiry_seal_count.description: Number of subsequent Seals within which the obligation must be discharged. Default deployment value is 1 (the next Seal).

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical InclusionList bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.title: Arkret Invite Delivery Request
schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.description: Private service-to-service request used by an inviter-side Principal Server to deliver a Realm invite to the invitee-side Principal Server. The request carries an explicit invite address and introduction evidence; raw locator tokens are never written into durable Realm events.

invite_event.description: The ak.invite.create EventEnvelope or equivalent accepted event view being delivered.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

recipient_service_id.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.
v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of the invitee-issued ak.consent.grant (scope invite or any) that authorizes the inviter to send Realm/Strand invites. High-trust evidence: it is material the invitee actively issued to the inviter, equivalent in trust to a locator_ref.

consent_id.description: Optional consent cell id locating the holder consent cell, to speed up receiver verification of the active grant dot.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the inviter used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to invite_address.subject_id. The receiver MUST verify binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

member_delivery_binding_candidate.description: Optional builder evidence returned by a Directory or trusted issuer for intent=invite. When present, verifiers MUST check subject_id, handle, recipient_service_id, audience, issuer_service_id, expiry and proofs against this delivery.

resolved_by.description: Optional Directory or issuer service DID that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST be reported as deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Only a receiver policy disclosure level of outcome may add disclosed_outcome, and only with delivered|blocked.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, closed to delivered|blocked. Present ONLY when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer; omitted (opaque) otherwise. delivered: the invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST NOT be disclosed: it reveals holder-private consent state (identity/consent-model.md 6.1.1) and MUST be reported as status='deferred' with no disclosed_outcome, in the same response and timing equivalence class as rate-limit silent drop, timeout drop, holder-not-found and holder policy deny.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.title: Arkret Invite and Contact Receive Policy
schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.description: Subject-private policy used by a Principal Server to decide which invite delivery or first-contact request introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log or the public contact fact log.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private invite receive policy this object configures. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

holder_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

handle_claim_behavior.description: Default behavior for handle_claim evidence. Omitted means quarantine. A subject MAY set notify to allow verified handle-based requests to reach the holder, but the effective value is capped by receive_policy_constraints.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for invite/contact delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Optional subject-private allowlist for canonical handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty or omitted means no subject-level domain restriction; deployment constraints may still restrict the effective set.

denied_handle_domains.description: Subject-private denylist for canonical handle domains. Matches are rejected before allowed_handle_domains is evaluated.
