trusted_handle_issuers.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of handle claim issuers accepted for handle_claim evidence.

trusted_directory_services.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of Directory service DIDs accepted as resolved_by for handle_claim evidence.

denied_subjects.description: Per-subject block list (peer principal DIDs). Invite delivery whose inviter is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy, to avoid leaking the block via a side channel.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite/contact delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked) to the requester, by introduction trust tier. Holder quarantine is never disclosable at any tier: it maps to status=deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, discovery_trust=opaque, low_trust=opaque.

domain_name.description: Canonical IDNA A-label domain. Subdomains are not implied; list each accepted domain explicitly.

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered|blocked result is disclosed to the inviter. Neither level ever discloses holder quarantine.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

discovery_trust.description: Disclosure level for public or restricted discovery evidence: handle_claim. Default opaque.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_principal_server, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound applied to subject-private receive policies. The effective receive policy is the intersection of the subject policy and these constraints; constraints can only make a subject less reachable, never more reachable.

applies_to.description: Surfaces governed by this constraint object. Omitted means both invite_delivery and contact_request.

deployment_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Maximum set of introduction evidence kinds this deployment permits. Omitted means no deployment-level kind cap.

handle_claim_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for handle_claim evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

explicit_address_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for explicit_address evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Deployment-level allowlist for handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty means no handle domain is accepted.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

token_commitment.description: Salted commitment to a high-entropy invite token. Required for offline_token mode.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

schemas/join-policy-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Candidate Join Policy Operation DTOs
schemas/join-policy-operations.schema.js.description: Closed profile-private DTOs for ak.profile.candidate.join_policy.v1. These objects are carried only by the registered join-application HTTP operations; candidate_kind is never an Event.kind and none of these receipts enter shared Realm history.

server_protected_body.description: Private record for a non-E2EE Realm. The service MUST encrypt this object at rest and authorize every read; it is never copied to shared Realm history or ordinary sync.

reviewer_envelope_body.description: Opaque E2EE application body encrypted to eligible reviewer devices. The server validates recipient capability/device bindings but cannot inspect plaintext answers.

application_receipt.description: Applicant-signed application receipt. application_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with application_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

review_receipt.description: Reviewer-signed decision receipt. review_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with review_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-review-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

cancel_receipt.description: Applicant-signed cancellation receipt. cancel_receipt_digest is sha256:JCS of this object with cancel_receipt_digest and proof omitted. proof signs the ak.join-application-cancel-receipt-proof-v1 transcript.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..title: Arkret Key Backup Active Series Record
schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..description: Signed principal-control record selecting the canonical backup series for one (actor_id, backup_kind). This closes the rollback gap when multiple series exist after compromise rotation or migration. Receivers MUST verify this record before choosing a series from list results.

series_pointer_version.description: Strictly monotonic per (actor_id, backup_kind). The first record is 1 and every successor is previous+1; receivers reject rollback, gaps and same-version forks.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

frontier_ref.description: Principal control stream frontier under which active_series_id was selected, bound to exactly one A/B identity-model generation.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(record without auth_data.signature).

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ak.cross_signing.publish.generation used to authorize this active-series selection.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize event anchoring the B-model device that signed this active-series selection.

schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.title: Arkret Key Backup Plaintext Keybag
schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.description: Canonical plaintext carried inside ak.schema.key_backup.v1 ciphertext after AEAD/HPKE open. The public envelope contents[] is only an index; this keybag is the import truth source.

secret_b64u.description: base64url(no padding) encoded secret bytes. The item_kind and metadata define how receivers import the bytes.

managed_principal_binding.description: Required for controller-custodied Native Personal Agent PCR MLS material and MUST byte-for-byte match the corresponding public contents[] binding and AEAD AAD canonical binding set.

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.title: Arkret Key Backup Unlock Proof
schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.description: Proof presented before a recovery strand downloads or unlocks a key-backup envelope. It binds a backup read/decrypt action to one recovery_session_id, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and the proof transcript accepted by the recovery session.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that moved the session to verified.

challenge.description: Optional echo of the recovery-session challenge; when present it MUST match the session snapshot.

verification_method.description: DID URL for either the accepted requesting device key after authorization, or the recovery-session proof key before did_recovery unlock.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(unlock proof without auth_data.signature).

mixed_secret_storage.description: True only for the personal_node exception where one encrypted backup envelope contains both identity-signing material and E2EE / MLS history material. Non-personal deployment profiles MUST reject this flag. When true and recipient_method=passphrase_kdf, the stricter Argon2id floor below applies.

series_id.description: Stable identifier for one immutable chain of backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during compromise rotation or migration; active series selection is outside this envelope and MUST come from the signed active-series record in identity/key-management.md §7.6. Receivers use (actor_id, backup_kind, series_id) to detect server-side rollback / withholding within the selected series.

series_seq.description: 0-based, strictly monotonically increasing sequence number within (actor_id, series_id). Genesis envelope of a series MUST set 0. Receivers MUST reject envelopes whose sequence does not strictly exceed the previously accepted sequence in the same series.

supersedes.description: backup_id of the immediate predecessor in the same series_id. MUST be absent for series_seq=0; MUST be present, non-null, and reference an existing predecessor for series_seq>0.

supersedes_digest.description: Required when supersedes is non-null. Hash of the canonical_json of the predecessor envelope (excluding auth_data.signature). Receivers MUST recompute and reject mismatches as `series_chain_broken`.

frontier_ref.description: Optional reference to the principal control stream frontier at envelope creation time. Exactly one model generation is bound: ssk_generation for A-model cross-signing or device_generation_ref for B-model enrollment authority.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Required for backup_kind=did_recovery and optional as a signed recovery-strand hint for other backup classes. Binds the backup envelope to the active recovery policy version under which it was produced. Receivers MUST compare this tuple to the currently accepted recovery policy before using a did_recovery envelope; when present on other classes, mismatch fails as recovery_policy_mismatch but the field does not replace active-series, frontier, Realm/MLS authorization, or device-state checks. This is intentionally separate from frontier_ref and ssk_generation: it binds the recovery authorization surface, not only the device trust generation or control-stream position.

recipient_key_ref.description: For recipient_method=recovery_public_key, this MUST resolve to a non-revoked recovery_key_agreements[].key_agreement_ref in the envelope's referenced accepted recovery policy, and the selected hpke_suite MUST appear in that entry's hpke_suites. DID Document-only key agreements are not an authorization source. A recovery_keys[].verification_method is a signing-key ref and MUST be rejected here.

hpke_suite.description: Registered active HPKE suite (KEM x KDF x AEAD per RFC 9180) selector; the value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Applies only to recipient_method=recovery_public_key. When absent it denotes the default-MUST row ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1. aead.name MUST equal the selected suite's AEAD. An unregistered or inactive suite MUST be rejected (unsupported_hpke_suite). Absent / ignored for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key).

aead_profile.description: Optional AEAD profile id that binds algorithm version, nonce length, tag length, key length, and AAD construction. Receivers that do not support the profile MUST fail closed instead of inferring semantics from name alone.

nonce.description: base64url AEAD nonce. Required for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key). For recipient_method=passphrase_kdf this MUST equal HMAC-SHA256(HKDF(derived_key, info='arkret-key-backup-aead-nonce-v1'), canonical_json({backup_id, actor_id, device_id, backup_kind, backup_version, created_at, aead.name, aead.aead_profile?, aead.nonce_salt}))[0:N_AEAD]; receivers recompute and reject mismatches. Absent for recovery_public_key (HPKE derives its nonce internally).

nonce_salt.description: Producer-generated base64url random salt (at least 128 bits before encoding) included in the passphrase_kdf nonce derivation transcript. Required when recipient_method=passphrase_kdf; not secret, signed as envelope metadata, and prevents nonce reuse from duplicate business metadata tuples.

enc.description: base64url HPKE KEM encapsulated key. Required for recipient_method=recovery_public_key; the KEM/KDF/AEAD are pinned by encryption.hpke_suite (default ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1) per artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Absent for the symmetric methods.

domain_separation.description: Signed key-backup domain separation transcript. Binds HKDF info and AEAD/HPKE AAD to the envelope fields used by key-management.md §7.1 / §7.5 so implementations do not infer subdomain semantics from ciphertext or local state.

device_id.description: The envelope's device_id bound into the AEAD AAD. The top-level device_id is optional, so an envelope sealed without an originating device MUST bind null here rather than omitting the key or substituting an empty string: the AAD transcript keeps a fixed field set so sealer and opener reconstruct it byte-identically (key-management.md §7.2). See the secret_storage_no_device KAT case in fixtures/key-backup-hardening-fixture.json.

managed_principal_bindings.description: Canonical sorted set of every distinct managed_principal_binding carried by contents[] and by the decrypted plaintext keybag. Required when any managed Agent PCR item is present; otherwise it MUST be absent. This binds managed-principal custody to the AEAD/HPKE ciphertext and prevents cross-Agent or cross-PCR transplant.

recipient_method.description: SEC-04: the envelope's encryption.recipient_method bound into the AEAD AAD so a ciphertext can never be cross-opened under the wrong recipient interpretation. Sealer and opener reconstruct it byte-identically from the stored envelope; receivers MUST fail closed on a method/AAD mismatch.

recipient_key_ref.description: SEC-04: the envelope's encryption.recipient_key_ref (recipient key / verification method) bound into the AEAD AAD so the recipient identity is part of the authenticated context.

managed_principal_binding.description: Required only for controller-custodied Native Personal Agent PCR MLS material. The outer backup actor remains the controller; this binding does not change backup ownership.

secret_version.description: Monotonic version of the backed-up secret (e.g. mls_account_secret). Used by clients for deterministic preferred-backup selection and anti-rollback ordering (key-management.md §9.1). Present on versioned secret items; absent on share-style items such as recovery_key_share.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the device signing key.

signature_algorithm.description: Raw signature algorithm name; MUST be a value generated from an active signature-alg-registry row (Ed25519 / ES256 / ML-DSA-65). EdDSA is the proof_alg label, not a raw signature_algorithm value. ML-DSA-65 is gated behind the PQ migration profile.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over canonical_json(envelope without auth_data.signature).

signed_fields.description: Names of envelope fields covered by the signature; MUST include backup_id, actor_id, backup_kind, backup_version, series_id, series_seq, encryption, domain_separation, contents, ciphertext_digest, and when present supersedes, supersedes_digest, frontier_ref, and recovery_policy_ref.

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ak.cross_signing.publish.generation of the self-signing key generation that authorized the device signing this backup. Exactly one of auth_data.ssk_generation and auth_data.device_authorize_event_id identifies the device trust root.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize event id anchoring the service_attested/enrollment-authority device signing this backup. Exactly one of auth_data.ssk_generation and auth_data.device_authorize_event_id identifies the device trust root.

then.description: A controller-owned mls_history envelope carrying managed Agent PCR material MUST be recoverable by the controller recovery public key, bind the controller policy and both controller/Agent PCR frontiers, use the managed_agent_pcr domain, and contain a current mls_group_state item. Semantic validation requires the AAD binding set to equal the distinct bindings in public contents and decrypted plaintext.

mls_history backups MUST use secret_storage_key or recovery_public_key (key-management.md §7.5.2 / §7.5.3 and device-lifecycle.md §12); passphrase_kdf, threshold_recovery, hardware_wrapped_key, and the removed device_snapshot_secret are rejected. Every recovery_public_key envelope, including mls_history, MUST carry a signed recovery_policy_ref.

allOf.description: Every recovery_public_key envelope is bound to one accepted recovery-policy version. The recipient_key_ref resolves only within that policy's recovery_key_agreements array, and recovery_policy_ref is signed even when backup_kind is secret_storage or mls_history.

then.description: did_recovery backups MUST use recovery_public_key (key-management.md §5.0.1 recovery-material gate), MUST carry recovery_policy_ref matching the active recovery policy, and MUST cover that field in auth_data.signed_fields. passphrase_kdf and secret_storage_key are forbidden for did_recovery; threshold_recovery and hardware_wrapped_key are recovery policy / proof-layer factors, not key-backup recipient methods.

managed_frontier_ref.description: Accepted and sealed Agent Principal Control Realm frontier covered by a controller-owned managed-PCR backup item.

managed_principal_binding.description: Binds controller-custodied MLS recovery material to one managed Native Personal Agent and its Principal Control Realm. controller_id MUST equal the outer backup actor_id; authorization_ref is resolved from the Agent DID history at envelope created_at and MUST authorize principal_control_realm_recovery.

schemas/key-transparency.schema.json.title: Arkret Key Transparency Evidence
schemas/key-transparency.schema.json.description: Canonical Arkret-specific evidence for ak.profile.key_transparency.v1 and high-security/sovereign log-backed witness requirements. This wire object is not an implementation of IETF KEYTRANS and MUST NOT be advertised as such; interop with draft-ietf-keytrans-protocol-05 requires a separately registered adapter/profile.

schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret MLS KeyPackage Operation DTOs
schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request and response DTOs for self and peer MLS KeyPackage upload, claim, claim-status query, consume, and revoke operations. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

object_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

key_package.description: Base64url encoding of the canonical MLS KeyPackage bytes.

cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

device_signature.description: Optional defense-in-depth entry signature over the upload entry transcript registered by device-lifecycle.md section 9.0. It never replaces the required request-level batch signature.

last_resort.description: When true, this entry is a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10). It remains published across claims and never enters the single-use claimed or consumed states; rotation, expiry, or explicit revocation transitions it to revoked with a registered revocation_reason. This application-layer flag is covered by the upload entry's device_signature. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event that binds a Native Agent runtime verification method to this KeyPackage. This branch is mutually exclusive with ssk_generation and device_authorize_event_id.

last_resort.description: When true, this claim record returns a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10) because the single-use pool was empty. The package may be reused within the same intended_realm_id and is not transitioned to consumed; the holder MUST rotate it and trigger group updates on next online. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

device_signature.description: Required authoritative batch signature over the typed upload request with the top-level signature and all entry signatures omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.upload.create domain. Ordinary devices and Native Agent runtimes share the same transcript.

requester_authorization.description: Detached authorization by the requesting participant. The signature transcript, verification-method ownership, freshness, and exact request binding are normative in device-lifecycle.md section 9.2.

peer_key_packages_claim_unsigned_request.description: Server-prepared immutable peer claim request fields before requester_authorization is attached. claim_request_id carries at least 128 bits of entropy and equals the Idempotency-Key value on the peer command.

peer_key_packages_claim_authorization_dr.description: Complete server-reserved object shown to the participant before signing. The signature transcript binds both the immutable request fields and the explicit service/trust-domain transport destination; the client MUST NOT infer transport_binding from local configuration.

requester_signing_key_evidence.description: Transport-only portable authorization evidence appended by the authenticated source Principal Server for the requester_device_id model. It is excluded from the participant authorization transcript. The peer command receiver requires it unless the same accepted device authorization is already present in a locally verified requester projection.

request.description: The exact participant-authorized unsigned request fields. Together with request_digest, this lets the destination bind a later Welcome and Direct Conversation binding to the durable claim without trusting source-service assertions.

peer_keypackage_claim_receipt.description: Destination-service-signed durable receipt. source_service_id and request are covered by the receipt signature; request_digest additionally binds the complete transport command, including participant authorization and portable signer evidence.

peer_key_packages_claim_outcome.description: Privacy-preserving peer success response. It intentionally omits inventory counts and per-device failure information.

signature.description: Signature over the typed consume request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.consume domain.
Signature over the typed revoke request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.revoke domain.

schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Device Key Operation DTOs
schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.keys.{upload,query,claim} and ak.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ak.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key (device-lifecycle.md §5.2 / §5.4). This is the verify key receivers resolve via verification_method `{actor}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full ak:device:<uuidv7> id, to check ak.call.signal / ephemeral envelope and durable Event proofs.

device_status.description: Usable directory status of the (principal_id, device_id) pair at query time. active requires an accepted, non-revoked authorization and, for B-model principals, device_generation_status=active plus authorized_generation_ref=current_device_generation_ref. revoked means ak.device.revoke is in effect. Servers MUST omit usable key material for revoked, unverified, fenced, or conflicted devices.

device_generation_state.description: Reducer-managed B-model generation state. Omitted for A-model principals, which use SSK generation instead.

query_device_record.description: Per-(principal_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_outcome. The directory facet is populated only for currently usable devices. For B-model principals the server MUST compare authorized_generation_ref with the sibling principal device_generations state and omit device_signing_key, hpke_key and prekey claims when the generation is fenced or conflicted.

hpke_key.description: The device HPKE public key used for secret / key envelope sealing, echoed verbatim from the authoritative ak.device.authorize.payload.hpke_key (device-lifecycle.md §5.2/§5.4). MUST only be returned for verified, non-revoked devices; services MUST NOT substitute this value in projection.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the §5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize event id anchoring the current device-set projection. For service_attested / enrollment-authority devices this pairs with enrollment_authority_binding and identifies the accepted authorization event whose payload.device_public_key is exposed as device_signing_key.

authorized_generation_ref.description: Reducer-managed B-model DID generation that authorized this device. Producers MUST NOT self-report it. A B-model device is usable only when this equals the principal current_device_generation_ref and device_generation_status is active. Omitted for A-model SSK devices.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

cross_signing.description: Tier-2: {principal_id} -> that principal's current accepted-generation ak.cross_signing.publish payload (device-lifecycle.md §5.1). Lets receivers anchor the SSK to the DID control set before trusting cross_signing_binding. See device-lifecycle.md §8.3.

device_generations.description: Current B-model generation fence by principal. Omitted for A-model principals. If a principal is conflicted, or a device record's authorized_generation_ref differs from current_device_generation_ref, the corresponding device record MUST expose no usable signing/HPKE/prekey material and keys_claim MUST not return a claim for it.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.unlock. The unlock proof MUST validate as ak.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1 and MUST be verified against the recovery session, caller, requesting device key, active-series record, and target envelope before the full ciphertext is returned (key-management.md §7.7.1 / §7.8). The path backup_id and proof.backup_id MUST match.

cross_signing_binding.description:
Tier-2 A-model device trust binding echoed from ak.device.authorize.payload.cross_signing_binding (device-lifecycle.md §5.2). The accepted-generation SSK signs `"ak.device-trust-bind-v1
" + canonical_json({principal_id, device_id, device_public_key, hpke_key, algorithms, ssk_generation})`. B-model devices instead use enrollment_authority_binding plus authorized_generation_ref.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the self-signing key (SSK) that produced the binding signature, e.g. did:webvh:...#ak_self_signing_v1.

ssk_generation.description: cross_signing.publish generation under which the SSK signed this device binding; compared to the principal's accepted generation per device-lifecycle.md §5.2.1.

schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.title: Arkret Directory Subject Handle List
schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.description: Result body for ak.find.directory.query.list_handles_for_subject. It lists currently visible handle claims for a disclosed holder/principal subject DID in the caller's context. Every claim in claims[] MUST have claim.subject byte-for-byte equal to this response subject.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID used as the reverse lookup key. This is not a Realm actor_id.

claims.description: Current context-visible signed handle claims. Each item MUST have subject equal to the top-level subject; mismatches MUST be dropped or fail the response closed.

primary_handle.description: Optional canonical primary handle selected from claims[] by identity-handles.md section 3.2.1 for the same context/as_of. The @ mention sigil is not part of this field.

as_of.description: As-of timestamp used to build the visible claim set and primary handle selection.

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

thumbnails.description: Bound thumbnail / preview descriptors. Producers SHOULD prefer this over preview_blob_ref for private or E2EE media.

schemas/media-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Realtime Media Operation DTOs
schemas/media-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request DTOs for realtime media service operations. ak.self.media.query.ice_config responses use ice-config-response.schema.json.

schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.title: Arkret Member Delivery Binding Candidate
schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.description: Builder-side candidate object that ferries Handle resolution output (intent=member_add | invite) or a trusted-issuer-signed equivalent into the Realm member_add / invite pipeline. Produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after the reducer independently re-validates against Join Policy. See identity-handles.md §3.7.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the addressee. Materialised as payload.actor_id / cell subject in ak.member.state{membership=join}.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. acct: aliases and @ mention spelling are rejected here.

handle_aliases.description: Optional interop aliases (RFC 7565 acct:). Never used for cache keys, signature transcripts, or delivery_binding materialisation.

binding_source.description: MUST NOT be did_document_default — handle-resolved candidates and DID Document fallback are independent materialisation paths.

issuer_service_id.description: Service DID that signed the candidate (Directory service DID, Principal Server service DID, or Organization service DID).

audience.description: Target Realm ID or inviting service DID. Verifier MUST reject candidates whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp marking when the issuer signed the candidate. Required: paired with expires_at to give verifiers a replay-protection window and to detect retro-dated candidates. issued_at MUST be <= expires_at.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Expired candidates MUST NOT enter the builder.

source_refs.description: Event references at the issuer / Directory / Organization that back this candidate; clients SHOULD re-verify against the truth source.

proofs.description: At least one proof binding handle, subject_id, member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_id, audience, issuer_service_id, issued_at, expires_at and (when present) claim_digest. issued_at MUST be inside the signed transcript so an MITM cannot widen the replay-protection window by rewriting it; verifiers MUST reject proofs whose canonical transcript omits issued_at.

claim_digest.description: sha256 digest over JCS(semantic_projection(upstream handle claim)) per zh/identity/identity-handles.md ?3.2.1; it is not a digest over the whole upstream handle claim object.

intent.description: Builder entry point. Advisory for audit / telemetry; reducer behaviour does not branch on this field.

schemas/member-identity.schema.json.title: Arkret Member Identity
schemas/member-identity.schema.json.description: Realm-scoped, actor-scoped full member_identity segment. It is carried by ak.member.identity.update in plaintext or inside encrypted-envelope.schema.json. Replacement events that name segment=member_identity MUST carry this complete object. This object discloses subject_id and display_profile for Realm UI projection; handle lifecycle is intentionally excluded and is governed only by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims. Mention / reply / quote / actor attribution MUST use subject_id (the principal DID), never a handle string.

actor_id.description: Effective member actor DID in this Realm. MAY be a Realm-scoped pairwise DID.

subject_id.description: Principal DID or disclosed holder DID represented by actor_id for display purposes. Authorization and audit continue to use the Event actor and member state.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of this MemberIdentity object with the top-level proof field excluded. The signature MUST cover the same canonical bytes.

schemas/message.schema.json.title: Arkret Message

anyOf.$comment: forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content
forbidden track key; canonical name is track_name
forbidden Message extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata

track_name.description: Strand track key for this Message. v1 Message objects are restricted to the Strand discussion track. Profiles that need another timeline kind MUST register a separate object/event profile instead of overloading Message.track_name.

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope of this Message, materialized from the scope_circle_id effective at create time (models/circle.md §6.1-§6.2). kind='realm' for Realm-default scope; kind='circle' when the message's Strand was Circle-scoped at write time. Immutable: a later Strand scope rebind MUST NOT reinterpret already-written messages — each message retains its write-time effective_scope and old-scope history/key eligibility. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (reducer-managed, reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the reducer stamps it on accept.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Message ContentBlock.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a message_metadata object.

state.description: Top-level lifecycle state for messages. Messages do not have a separate deleted/tombstone state; retention or moderation removal uses ak.message.redact and state=redacted so the message slot and audit metadata remain stable.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.message.redact Event. Aligns with the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

revision_root.description: First revision in this message's edit chain. The first revision MUST have revision_root == id. Maintained by ak.message.revise reducer.

redaction_ref.description: Required when state=redacted; references the ak.message.redact event that produced this state. MUST be absent for other states.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent materialized message update, such as ak.message.revise or ak.message.redact.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Mirror of event-payload.schema.json $defs.content_block: reject discriminator field `type` (canonical: `kind`), composite child array name `blocks` (canonical: `parts`), and byte-count field `size` (canonical: `size_bytes`). Keeps materialized Message and Event payload schemas in lockstep so that the materialized Message.content cannot smuggle through wire-forbidden field names.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

sidecar_exchange_binding.description: Agent Sidecar exchange binding. Legal only inside encrypted_metadata plaintext of an event whose effective scope is the Sidecar backing Circle; forbidden in plaintext metadata and in shared Realm/Circle events (see forbidden-wire-fields.json and zh/models/sidecar.md §7.2).

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Message metadata fields. Reducer-owned lifecycle and revision fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

schemas/message.schema.json.$comment: Top-level uses unevaluatedProperties (not additionalProperties) because the top-level oneOf branches contribute evaluated properties; additionalProperties at the top level would not see those and could wrongly reject legitimate oneOf-branch fields (JSON Schema additionalProperties/oneOf pitfall).

schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.title: Arkret MIMI Interoperability
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.description: Provider directory, room binding, and content mapping receipt objects for ak.profile.mimi_interop.v1.
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.$comment: Intentionally relaxed interop-extension surface: this profile tracks evolving IETF MIMI Internet-Drafts (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §1), so additionalProperties is left open at the top level and on the mimi/binding_scope/payload subtrees to forward-carry draft fields without a breaking schema bump. Known fields are pinned; unknown draft fields are tolerated rather than rejected. The proof object below gives a minimal required core so the openness is limited to known extension subtrees and does not mask a missing signature. Unknown fields anywhere on this surface are security-inert (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §9.2): receivers MUST ignore them for all security decisions and MUST NOT let them affect authorization, identity binding, policy_root, MLS epoch/group state, routing, or any signature/digest transcript.

mls_cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

room_binding.description: MIMI room binding effect payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the cell subject is payload.mimi_room_uri for ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

status.description: Room binding lifecycle status. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are proposed->accepted, proposed->revoked, accepted->migrating, accepted->revoked, migrating->accepted (verified migration proof), migrating->revoked. revoked is the only terminal state; illegal transitions are rejected with mimi_room_binding_status_transition_invalid. Normative state machine: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

migration_outcome.description: Outcome of a migrating->accepted transition: completed (new topology in effect) or rolled_back (original topology restored). MUST be present on a migrating->accepted Control Move so the result is auditable; MUST be absent on other transitions. Normative: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

receipt_kind.description: Interop-audit object discriminator. This object is not an Event Envelope and this value is not an event kind.

schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret MIMI Operation DTOs
schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for MIMI provider interop operation bindings.

schemas/mls-governance-proof-bundle.sche.title: Arkret MLS Governance Proof Bundle
schemas/mls-governance-proof-bundle.sche.description: Bounded chunk of a complete-materialization proof bundle used by a light client to verify an MLS full-profile governance binding against an accepted Seal. The fixed-size manifest commits every ordered chunk through chunks_root; the verifier accepts only after fetching all chunks, checking contiguous collection ranges, and recomputing the accepted Seal roots. proof_request_digest binds the acquisition identity, bundle_digest addresses the complete logical bundle, and each chunk_digest addresses one bounded transport chunk. accepted_seal_id alone is not a Bundle cache key.

proof_request_digest.description: sha256(UTF-8('arkret-mls-governance-proof-request-v1\n') || RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes of the proof identity object containing realm_id, effective_scope, mls_group_id, previous_epoch, next_epoch, binding_profile, reducer_profile and trusted_anchor_seal_id). Transport fields chunk_index and expected_bundle_digest are excluded. The verifier MUST recompute it before using or caching any chunk.

bundle_digest.description: Content address of the complete logical bundle: sha256(UTF-8('arkret-mls-governance-proof-bundle-v1\n') || RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes of all top-level response members except bundle_digest and chunk). chunk_manifest.chunks_root transitively commits every chunk. A verifier MUST recompute this digest for every response.

materialization_profile.description: The only v1 profile. Across every committed chunk, covered_event_digests is the entire recursive covered_set of accepted_seal_id and control_state is the entire sorted set of non-bottom joined control cells committed by its state_root.

trusted_anchor_seal_id.description: MUST equal proof_request.trusted_anchor_seal_id bit-for-bit. This is a Seal id the verifier already trusts through authenticated Realm bootstrap or prior successful verification. Presence in this bundle never makes an anchor trusted.

accepted_seal_id.description: Id of the accepted Seal whose control_event_set_root and state_root authenticate this bundle. It MUST identify the final Seal assembled from the seal_path chunks.

trusted_anchor_seal_id.description: Seal id already trusted by this verifier. The service MUST construct seal_path from this exact anchor (or its direct successor) and MUST NOT silently substitute a newer, older, or service-selected anchor. A bootstrap client uses the Realm genesis/compaction Seal only after validating it through its authenticated Realm bootstrap, join, snapshot, or equivalent trust package.

chunk_index.description: Zero-based global chunk index. The first request MUST use 0. Later requests use an index below chunk_manifest.chunk_count and include expected_bundle_digest.

expected_bundle_digest.description: Required when chunk_index is greater than 0 and forbidden for chunk_index 0. It pins later reads to the exact manifest returned by the initial request.

proof_request.description: Authenticated account-client query input. The service derives all governance roots and membership_frontier from one accepted Seal view; callers MUST NOT supply any root or frontier. chunk_index and expected_bundle_digest select transport chunks and are excluded from proof_request_digest. The caller MUST name one locally trusted anchor. If the service cannot prove a path from that exact anchor to the target accepted Seal, it returns mls_governance_anchor_unreachable and MUST NOT suggest or substitute an untrusted anchor. Genesis requests MUST use previous_epoch=0 and next_epoch=0; commit requests MUST use next_epoch=previous_epoch+1.

chunks_root.description: Merkle root over chunk_digest raw bytes in chunk_index order, using SHA-256(0x00 || chunk_digest_raw) leaves and SHA-256(0x01 || left || right) internal nodes.

total_item_bytes.description: Sum of the UTF-8 byte lengths of RFC 8785 canonical JSON for every individual item across all four collections. Array delimiters and repeated response metadata are excluded. A verifier recomputes this incrementally and MUST NOT allocate from the declaration.

chunk_manifest.description: Fixed-size commitment to the complete chunk sequence. Chunk order is all seal_path chunks, then covered_event_digests, control_state and frontier_events; within a collection start_index is contiguous and items retain canonical collection order. Empty collections emit no chunk.

chunk_proof.description: RFC 6962-style inclusion path for chunk_digest at chunk_index under chunk_manifest.chunks_root. At most 10 siblings are needed for the 1024-chunk limit.

proof_chunk.description: One bounded collection slice. chunk_digest = sha256(UTF-8('arkret-mls-governance-proof-chunk-v1\n') || RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes of {chunk_index, collection, start_index, items}); chunk_proof authenticates that digest under chunk_manifest.chunks_root.

schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.title: Arkret Moderation Appeal
schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.description: Payload shapes for the four ak.moderation.appeal.* event kinds (submit / review / decision / close) that close the moderation appeal loop. Each kind writes the ak.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell on a deterministic state machine: (none) → submitted → under_review → decided → closed; close from submitted/under_review is allowed only for appellant withdrawal (closer == appellant and close_reason=appellant_withdrawn). The decided state additionally records the verdict (uphold / overturn / modify); overturn MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event referencing the original decision. Modify MUST atomically lift the original decision and add the replacement decision named by modify_decision_ref. Lifting a decision does not resurrect an irreversible redaction tombstone or destroyed content key. All payloads carry realm_id and reducers MUST require it to equal the enclosing Event.realm_id and the appealed decision's Realm. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand). Capability: ak.moderation.appeal.submit (any member, low risk) for submit; ak.moderation.appeal.review (moderator) for review/decision/manual reviewer close after decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the ak.moderation.decision event being appealed.

target_ref.description: The original moderation target (message, strand, member, blob, etc.) — same typed-id form as the appealed decision's target.

evidence_visibility.description: Who may decrypt / read the appeal evidence narrative. Default per Realm policy; SHOULD be reviewers_only for sensitive disputes. The visibility tag MUST enter projection / redaction decisions; it does NOT change wire encryption of the envelope, only the plaintext audience for evidence fields.

submit_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.submit — opens the appeal. Writes appeal cell (state=submitted). MUST be issued by an appellant who is the original moderation target's controller (member appealing their own ban / message removal) or by an authorized advocate listed in Realm policy. A Realm member appellant is admitted by baseline membership; a non-member advocate MUST be authorized by Realm policy / ak.moderation.appeal.submit capability.

appellant.description: Actor lodging the appeal. MUST be the original moderation target's controller or an authorized advocate.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference (typically blob_ref or in-line short string) to the appeal narrative / supporting argument. For E2EE Realms this is an encrypted reference.

evidence_refs.description: Optional supporting evidence (blob refs, prior message ids, witness DIDs).

review_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.review — reviewer takes the appeal under review. Transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Reviewer MUST hold ak.moderation.appeal.review capability; the same actor MUST NOT review their own moderation decision (separation of duties enforced by reducer).

decision_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.decision — reviewer's verdict. Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Verdict semantics: uphold = original decision stands, no further action; overturn = original decision is lifted for future governance evaluation, this event MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event whose target equals decision_ref (reducer rejects with appeal_overturn_missing_lift otherwise), and irreversible redaction/key-destruction effects are not resurrected; modify = original decision is atomically replaced, requiring both a same-batch lift of decision_ref and a new ak.moderation.decision whose event id is modify_decision_ref.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference to the verdict rationale. MUST be present for audit trail; visibility follows evidence_visibility on the submit event.

modify_decision_ref.description: Required iff verdict=modify. Points to the replacement ak.moderation.decision event in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction; that transaction MUST also contain a ak.moderation.decision.lift for the original appealed decision.

close_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.close — closes the appeal from decided, or from submitted/under_review only for appellant withdrawal. Reviewer close and a deployment's authorized close service use the review capability after the appeal is decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant plus close_reason=appellant_withdrawn while state is submitted or under_review. close is a manual/authorized action: the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer, timeout duration, or cool-off duration — deployment/Realm policy decides those. Idempotency only: the same (decision_ref, appellant) pair MUST NOT have two non-closed appeals concurrently; a fresh appeal_id is allowed once the prior appeal cell is closed.

closer.description: Actor or service closing the appeal (reviewer, appellant, or a deployment's authorized close service). Reducer authorizes the close via the normal capability gate (or closer == appellant for withdrawal); the protocol does not mandate any timer service DID or timeout window.

auto_closed.description: Informational marker: true iff the close was emitted by a deployment's automated close service rather than a human actor. The protocol attaches no special timer/window enforcement to this flag; deployment policy defines when (if ever) automated close fires.

close_reason.description: Machine-readable close cause. appellant_withdrawn is valid only when closer is the appellant and the appeal is still submitted or under_review; timer_expired is an optional label for a deployment's automated close (auto_closed=true) and carries no protocol-mandated timeout semantics.

status.description: Authoritative moderation queue-item lifecycle. v1 is intentionally minimal: 'submitted' = report accepted and awaiting handling; 'resolved' = handling complete (terminal). The disposition (action taken vs no violation) lives on the separate ak.moderation.decision event; the appeal loop lives in the independent ak.moderation.appeal.* subsystem (§5.5). Additional intermediate states MAY be introduced in a later revision if a workflow phase needs them. See governance/content-moderation.md §3.3.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for this report. When absent, the report is Realm-default. Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

franking_proof.description: Optional franking proof metadata block. Mirrors the franking_proof object spec'd in zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4. It proves service receipt of ciphertext metadata; it does not prove plaintext authorship and does not grant moderators any MLS epoch/exporter secret.

status.description: Non-authoritative status mirror for client / UI convenience. The authoritative moderation lifecycle (submitted → resolved) lives on the moderation-queue-item produced by the reducer (see schemas/moderation-queue-item.schema.json + governance/content-moderation.md §3.3). Reducers MUST NOT read this field for routing or state-machine decisions; if present on submit it MUST be either absent or 'submitted'.

routing_metadata_digest.description: Digest of canonical event routing metadata covered by the receiving service.

mls_group_id_digest.description: Digest of the MLS group id; raw group ids MUST NOT appear in franking proofs.

replay_nonce.description: Opaque anti-replay nonce generated by the receiving service and covered by the franking proof signature.

signature.description: Receiving service signature over the canonical franking proof transcript.

schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.title: Arkret Morph Customer Risk Extension Example
schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.description: Reference additive extension business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example, used by the ak.morph.schema_migrate transformation conformance vectors. It declares the optional fields a transformation migration may introduce (renamed score / backfilled priority) on top of ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1.
schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.$comment: Logical schema id is ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.ext.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name. This is a v1 additive extension profile, not a version bump of customer_risk.v1.

schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.title: Arkret Morph Customer Risk Example
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.description: Reference business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example. It constrains the fields object carried by a ak.schema.morph.v1 container.
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.$comment: Logical schema id is ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. Reducer enforces scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and stamps immutable effective_scope onto emitted events.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative schema set for Morph fields and transition validation. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_kind and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

state.description: Morph lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.morph.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=morph_not_active); ak.morph.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else morph_not_archived); ak.redaction targeting the morph MUST come from {'active','archived'} (else morph_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.morph.archive / ak.morph.restore / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Morph business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle). A morph_kind profile MAY require it; generic mirror/data Morphs may omit it. If absent, the first ak.morph.stage.set initializes the axis to any registered value; later changes follow the normal transition rules. ak.morph.update / ak.morph.schema_migrate patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected. Stage transitions do not carry a reason/note; explanations belong in a referenced Message. See models/common-fields.md §5.3.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.morph.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions MUST NOT update this field.

morph_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Morph metadata. Morph business fields stay in the top-level fields object; metadata carries display-oriented fields such as title and summary. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields and Morph business fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.
Strand track keys use track_name; track is forbidden.

id.description: Profile-local approval_request_id. It is not a durable ak:<kind> object id.

source_account_artifact.description: Closed account-private artifact source for notifications that are not derived from a durable Realm Event.

source_ref.description: Optional canonical-object reference for clients that want to render the notification target without resolving source_event_id. Reducers MUST treat source_event_id as authoritative; source_ref is a render-only hint.

strand_id.description: Optional Strand context for routing the notification.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key on the source Strand.

preview.description: Render summary. Under E2EE / redaction / history-limited scopes this MUST be empty or an authorized redacted digest; sender/reducer-enforced. A notification projection MUST NOT widen the plaintext visibility of the source Message. See models/private-objects.md §3.4.

schemas/object-addressing.schema.json.title: Arkret Object Addressing
schemas/object-addressing.schema.json.description: Canonical target descriptors and signed authorization-token claims for object-address links.

address_link_kind.description: Closed URL-resolution classification. Signed authorization tokens use only invite or preview.

schemas/patch.schema.json.title: Arkret Field Patch (ak.schema.patch.v1)
schemas/patch.schema.json.description: Canonical field-patch format embedded in event payloads (typically at payload.patch) for non-create updates. This is a registered schema id (ak.schema.patch.v1) describing the structural form of a patch map; the embedded format identifier 'ak.patch.v1' remains the in-prose name for the same wire shape. Implementations MUST resolve ak.patch.v1 references in spec prose to this schema artifact. Grammar, parser responsibilities, selector semantics, redactable-field protection and reducer-managed-field protection are defined normatively in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.

propertyNames.$comment: Patch path syntax. Snake_case identifier, optional dot-separated segments, optional stable-key selectors (`field[<key>=<canonical-json-string>]`) and backtick-quoted literals for non-snake_case keys. Full ABNF in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.1. Maximum length 1024 bytes, maximum nesting depth 16 segments — exceeding either MUST yield reason_code patch_path_invalid.

oneOf.$comment: Direct value form: equivalent to {"$op":"set","value":<value>}. Any JSON value EXCEPT a JSON object containing a $op discriminator may use this form.
Explicit op object form. $op is required; value is required for set/add/remove; value MUST be absent for unset.

schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.title: Arkret Peer Contact and Direct Conversation Fact Delivery Request
schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.description: Private service-to-service request used by an issuer-side Principal Server to deliver an original signed contact fact or ak.direct_conversation.bound fact to the other participant's Principal Server. The recipient verifies and projects the original signed envelope without re-signing it. These facts are principal-scoped and cross-Realm, so this carrier is distinct from shared Realm Event federation and invite delivery.

contact_event.description: The issuer-signed contact or direct-conversation binding EventEnvelope being delivered with its original signature, so the recipient can verify and project it without re-signing.

fact_kind.description: The principal-scoped fact kind carried by contact_event. MUST equal contact_event.kind.

introduction_evidence.description: Required when fact_kind is ak.contact.requested. Explains why the requester may attempt first contact; the recipient applies its subject-private receive policy and deployment constraints before notifying the holder.

signer_key_evidence.description: Transport-only source-service attestation used to verify an original participant device proof without changing contact_event. Covered by the outer HTTP Message Signature.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the contact fact recipient (the request target, or the original requester for an accept/reject travelling back). The recipient Principal Server projects the fact into this holder's contact projection.

recipient_service_id.description: Principal Server service DID that hosts subject_id and accepts contact delivery for it.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows Principal Server contact delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of a target-issued ak.consent.grant whose scope covers the requested contact action, or any.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the requester used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to contact_address.subject_id. The receiver MUST verify binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

resolved_by.description: Optional Directory or issuer service DID that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether the holder's receive policy suppressed the fact, beyond the optional disclosed_outcome graded disclosure that mirrors ak.peer.invites.command.submit.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, closed to delivered|blocked. Present ONLY when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer; omitted (opaque) otherwise. delivered: the invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST NOT be disclosed: it reveals holder-private consent state (identity/consent-model.md 6.1.1) and MUST be reported as status='deferred' with no disclosed_outcome, in the same response and timing equivalence class as rate-limit silent drop, timeout drop, holder-not-found and holder policy deny.

schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.title: Arkret Personal Productivity Account Data
schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.description: Plaintext shapes that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.personal_productivity.v1 account-data values.

policy_rule.description: Closed policy rule. Extension rules must carry an explicit schema_ref/profile_ref instead of adding undeclared fields to the signed policy body.

domain_name.description: Lowercase DNS A-label domain. Matching semantics are label-boundary based and defined by governance/content-moderation.md.

server_selector.description: Selector for federation server policy rules. Domain rules match normalized DNS labels only; service_id exact rules take precedence in policy evaluation.

schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.title: Arkret Principal Locator
schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.description: Signed online locator returned from a holder-controlled Principal Server locator ref. It asserts the invite address used for private invite delivery; it is not a Realm membership grant and not a member_delivery_binding.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

recipient_service_id.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_kind.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

expires_at.description: Time after which the locator MUST NOT be used to initiate invite delivery.

locator_ref_digest.description: Digest of the private locator ref material. The raw locator token MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

delivery_modes.description: Invite-delivery capability hints only; join-time member_delivery_binding is still materialized by Realm policy.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

proofs.description: At minimum contains recipient_service_acceptance. High-assurance deployments SHOULD also require subject_locator_authorization.

proof.description: Detached proof over canonical_json(principal_locator_without_proofs). proof.payload_digest MUST equal that canonical payload digest.

locator_token.description: Opaque base64url locator token with at least 128 bits of entropy. It SHOULD be a server-side handle and MUST NOT plaintext-encode subject_id, recipient_service_id, expiry, policy state, or other invitee-identifying material. It MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested locator lifetime. The Principal Server MAY shorten it but MUST NOT exceed the v1 one-hour ceiling.

one_time_use.description: When true, the first successful resolve atomically consumes the locator.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested replacement-locator lifetime. When omitted, preserve the old locator's granted lifetime (old expires_at minus old issued_at). The Principal Server MAY shorten it but MUST NOT exceed the v1 one-hour ceiling.

one_time_use.description: Whether the first successful resolve atomically consumes the replacement locator. When omitted, preserve the old locator's one_time_use value.

display_hint.description: Replacement display hint. When omitted, preserve the old hint; null explicitly clears it.

locator_token.description: Fresh opaque bearer secret generated from at least 192 bits of CSPRNG entropy and returned exactly once. Clients MUST keep it out of logs, analytics, caches, and ordinary durable local state; an explicit user-directed out-of-band handoff is permitted and inherits the token's TTL and revocation risks.

locator_id.description: Non-secret administrative identifier used only on the authenticated self surface.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

schemas/public-key.schema.json.title: Arkret Canonical Public Key DTO
schemas/public-key.schema.json.description: Canonical wire shape of a public key carried in Arkret DTOs. It is defined in its own document so that device, agent and account surfaces reference one shared definition instead of reverse-referencing each other's bundles. Prose examples MUST use this exact shape: kty/kid/alg/key, no public_key alias.

public_key.description: Canonical public key. key carries the base64url key material; kid is the typed identifier of the key holder (for a device key, ak:device:<uuidv7>). There is no public_key member: that spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected.

schemas/push-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Push Gateway Operation DTOs
schemas/push-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.edge.push.command.register_device, ak.edge.push.command.unregister_device, and ak.push.notify.

push_target_id.description: Typed pairwise pseudonym for one (recipient_service_id, principal, device, push_route) tuple. It MUST NOT be a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, or stable cross-Realm correlation key.

push_route_token.description: Opaque service-generated routing token. It MUST NOT contain, encode, or be reversibly derived from a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Circle id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, handle, platform push token, or stable cross-context correlation key.

registration_id.description: Push gateway local registration id. It is not a registered ak:<kind> protocol object id.

badge.description: Coarse unread indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute unread count (activity side channel); only a boolean presence flag or a policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

missed_call.description: Coarse missed-call indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute count; only a boolean presence flag or the policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

target_route_token.description: Gateway-internal mention-redirect routing token for this device route. Paired with notification.route_tokens.mention_redirect_target_route_tokens to drive the fail-closed per-device routing gate. MUST be stripped before any provider call; MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. See push-notifications.md §4.5 / §5.1.

visible_notification_opt_in.description: Receiver device authorization state for ak.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1. Missing or false means this device MUST receive only blind_wakeup output even if the caller service is plaintext-visible; visible metadata requires an explicit per-device opt-in.

route_tokens.description: Gateway-internal opaque routing fragment shared by blind and visible notifications. Every field here drives gateway-side routing / dedup / circuit-breaker state and MUST be stripped before the gateway calls any push provider; it MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. Tokens are issued by the recipient Sync or Principal Service and bound to recipient_service_id, push gateway service DID, purpose, scope, and salt epoch.

realm_route_token.description: Opaque token for Realm-level routing / dedup / circuit-breaker keying.

scope_route_token.description: Opaque token for the effective Realm or Circle scope of this wakeup.

mention_redirect_target_route_tokens.description: Mention-redirect routing allow-list. When non-empty, each device's device_route.target_route_token MUST appear here or that device is failed closed (no provider call, no body decryption). Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

delivery_binding_frontier_token.description: Opaque token representing the receiver's delivery-binding frontier for stale-route detection.

audit_envelope.description: `ak.audit.accessed` envelope routing fragment carried alongside a notify request. When present, the request is an audit-pipeline event (e.g. an `e2ee_late_recovery` access notice), not a push notify: the gateway writes the audit event, acks 200, and skips the push pipeline.

access_kind.description: ak.audit.accessed.access_kind. The gateway branches on `e2ee_late_recovery` to skip the push pipeline.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: REQUIRED (at the application layer) when access_kind == e2ee_late_recovery. References the original event the late recovery targets.

timing_profile_hint.description: Closed timing/profile hint from Sync Service. traffic_metadata_hardened means the source Realm or route declares ak.profile.traffic_metadata_hardened.v1 and the Push Gateway MUST use a 300s or coarser provider-visible timing bucket. Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §2.4 / §4.5 / §5.1.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key". MUST be an l10n key token, never plaintext body or any identifying metadata.

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved (E2EE client-side rule fallback). Pure local-evaluation signal; carries no metadata. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

timing_profile_hint.description: Closed timing/profile hint from Sync Service. traffic_metadata_hardened means the source Realm or route declares ak.profile.traffic_metadata_hardened.v1 and the Push Gateway MUST use a 300s or coarser provider-visible timing bucket. Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §2.4 / §4.5 / §5.1.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key".

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

push_notify_request_body.description: Closed Arkret notify body. Product-private notification bodies, provider adapter payloads, APNs/FCM/WebPush data dictionaries, `content`, `content_*`, `provider_payload`, DND/snooze state, and push-rule plaintext are outside this wire surface and MUST be consumed before this body is built. Provider-facing payloads are reconstructed by the gateway from this closed shape and MUST strip route_tokens / reason_code / event_kind / audit_envelope before provider dispatch.

event_kind.description: Originating Event kind (e.g. `ak.message`) used by the gateway to route Phase-P2 `ak.agent.*` lifecycle / actor-private kinds to a no-fanout aak. Coarse routing selector; carries no Realm / sender / event identifier.

reason_code.description: Caller-supplied wire-safe reason code. The well-known value `historical_only` marks a diagnostic replay that MUST NOT trigger a fresh push fanout (the gateway answers a 200 idempotency-style ack). Other values are honored only where the operation defines them.

schemas/query.schema.json.title: Arkret Query / Search Request Shapes
schemas/query.schema.json.description: Canonical wire schema for client query / projection and search request bodies and their reusable building blocks (filters, sort, relation query). The OpenAPI document references these $defs so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md. facet_name / view_renderer are copies of the shared OpenAPI enums (kept local so this file is self-contained); the authoritative facet / renderer enums also live in the OpenAPI components and MUST stay in lockstep.

context_ref.description: Optional timeline / renderer context object reference. This is not a Seal.

schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.title: Arkret Range-bound Completeness Attestation
schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.description: A range-bound completeness attestation. Event kind: ak.attestation.range_completeness (active in event-kind-registry; the event kind itself carries NO .v1 suffix). Payload schema id: ak.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1 (schemas keep the .v1 versioning). The attestation asserts that the issuer (and any witnesses) have observed every reducer-input event in a declared range — (from_frontier, to_frontier) bounded by explicit per-actor seq intervals — where each frontier is a Realm-scoped frontier (property name realm_frontier; the security/replication boundary for completeness in v1 is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container). Distinct from ak.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity over an arbitrary chosen subset) and ak.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event RYW hint). Used when verifiers need a completeness claim — i.e., 'no event has been silently withheld from this range' — not just 'the events given are unmodified'. Standalone single-issuer attestations are NOT sufficient for sovereign / multi-writer trust models; deployments requiring strong completeness MUST use a witness_attestation block following the ak.audit.ryw_receipt model (zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1.1).

schema.description: Payload schema id (versioned). The owning Event kind in event-kind-registry.json is ak.attestation.range_completeness (NO .v1 suffix on the event kind).

from_frontier.description: Lower bound of the range (exclusive). The attestation covers events causally after this frontier.

from_seq_exclusive.description: Per-actor seq lower bound (exclusive). -1 means 'from actor genesis'.

to_seq_inclusive.description: Per-actor seq upper bound (inclusive). Issuer asserts completeness of every actor_seq in the half-open interval (from_seq_exclusive, to_seq_inclusive].

actor_seq_ranges.description: Per-actor seq intervals attested. Silent forks frequently appear as a missing slice in a single actor's seq sequence while the global frontier still advances monotonically — explicit per-actor ranges close that gap. MUST cover every actor that produced reducer-input events in (from_frontier, to_frontier].

root.description: Canonical Merkle root over the sorted set of (actor_id, actor_seq, event_id, event_digest) tuples for every reducer-input event in scope. Digest algorithm agility per Realm.digest_algorithm.

count.description: Number of reducer-input events in scope. MUST match the number of leaves used to compute root.

observed_at.description: When the issuer finished observing the scope and computed the attestation.
