kind.description: Same semantics as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.witness_attestation: 'federation_witness_attested' requires witnesses[].length >= 2 with pairwise-distinct issuer/controlling_organization/verification_method, each listed by Realm policy in audit.range_completeness_witnesses[]. 'single_source' is the honest declaration for self-attested deployments. Mismatch between kind and witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / policy listing MUST be rejected. Receivers SHOULD treat single_source attestations as advisory only and not as a sovereign-grade completeness proof.

schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Read Cursor Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface read cursor operations (ak.self.read_cursor.*). set builds a ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private write; the durable cursor object model and read_scope / position field shapes are read-cursor.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/read-receipts.md.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='strand' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with container_ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

container_ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, strand, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Strand's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.title: Arkret Read Cursor
schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.description: Actor-private multi-device read cursor. Stored in encrypted account data or actor-private stream; NEVER published into a shared Realm Event history. Bound to (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position, HLC, device_id) per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §6.6 so that concurrent updates from multiple devices converge by HLC max.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for multi-device convergence: when two devices race on the same (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) the receiver picks the entry with greater HLC; device_id provides a deterministic actor_id-scoped tiebreaker when HLCs are equal.

schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Read Receipt
schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.description: Public/shared read receipt for Strand timeline UI hint. NOT canonical truth, NOT a multi-device cursor (see read-cursor.schema.json for that). MUST NOT generate push notifications. Privacy is governed by Realm policy: Realms MAY allow public, members-only, or actor-private receipt sharing.

event_id.description: ID of the most recent Event the actor has read. Causality implies all causal predecessors are also read.

hlc.description: Optional. HLC of the read position; required when Sync Service must compare receipts under merge / debounce rules across devices for the same actor.

kind.description: Read-scope discriminator from the same family as read-cursor.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset (receipt additionally supports view/message/morph; cursor additionally supports circle/space). kind='thread' selects the reply sub-timeline rooted at a message (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector, not a first-class protocol object.

object_ref.description: Required when kind is anything other than 'realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' and the receipt scopes a single track.

track_scope.description: Only valid when kind='strand'. Use track_scope='all' for an entire Strand regardless of track.

schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.title: Arkret Realm Join Candidate
schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.description: Time-bounded routing hint for submitting Realm join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join material through a qualified Realm service. This object is not membership authorization and is distinct from member_delivery_binding.

realm_id.description: Realm this candidate is bound to. Verifiers MUST reject a candidate used for any other Realm.

service_id.description: Service DID that can receive or relay join-side submissions for this Realm.

service_kind.description: Service class. principal_server is the normal candidate; sync_node and notary are allowed only when Realm policy authorizes them to receive join-side submissions.

role.description: Routing role within the Realm candidate set. This is a hint for ordering and diagnostics, not an authorization grant.

endpoint.description: Optional endpoint hint. Callers MUST re-resolve the service DID document before transport and MUST NOT treat this field as authority.

operations.description: Endpoint-callable operation ids available at this candidate. Join-side routing requires ak.events.submit.

join_methods.description: Join-side strands this candidate claims to support for this requester and Realm.

priority.description: Lower values are preferred. Ties are broken deterministically by service_id.

source.description: Where this routing hint came from. Receivers still validate against current Realm policy and service DID documents.

source_refs.description: Realm or directory source events that justify this candidate, such as discovery, service-binding, or sync endpoint state.

frontier_ref.description: Optional digest of the candidate service's advertised Realm frontier at as_of; used only to detect stale hints.

seal_basis.description: Full single-leaf Control Move basis for the candidate service's current accepted Realm Seal at as_of. Principal-server candidates MUST include this so pre-join Realm join / invite-accept Control Moves can be signed without a separate membership-gated frontier read. This is a routing/anchoring hint, not membership authorization: the receiving service still validates the submitted basis and invite.

as_of.description: Time when the issuer observed or refreshed this candidate.

expires_at.description: Time after which clients MUST NOT use this candidate without re-resolving the Realm.

proofs.description: Optional proof set binding realm_id, service_id, role, operations, join_methods, as_of, and expires_at. Required when the candidate is carried outside a freshly resolved Directory response.

schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret Realm Link Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface cross-Realm link operations (ak.self.realm_link.*). Each write builds a ak.realm.link Move and routes it through the local accept pipeline so the reducer validates self-reference and link kind. General link-graph cycles are legal; traversal uses a visited set and does not reject a write merely for forming a cycle. The durable link payload is the canonical ak.realm.link; see spec/v1/zh/models/realm-links.md.

link_kind.description: Core value or machine-registered extension kind using x.<reverse-dns>.<name>; unregistered extension values fail closed.

commitment.description: Optional opaque commitment / proof reference linking this edge to an external attestation.

realm_effective_policy_outcome.description: Merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy declaration.

inheritance_mode.description: explicit when the Realm has projected a ak.realm.inheritance_policy; none otherwise (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.title: Arkret Realm Organization-Relationship Read Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.description: Closed response DTO for the self-surface Realm organization-relationship read operation (ak.self.realm_organization.query.list). Returns the projected ak.realm.organization statements (active / revoked / expired) for a Realm plus the declared owning_organizations hints that have no verified statement. The verified rows mirror the canonical realm_organization_payload field order; lifecycle_phase is reducer-derived. A row here is a projection only: an organization relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active, and actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy / notary / capability / service-binding event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.0 and schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload.

lifecycle_phase.description: Reducer-derived lifecycle phase of the projected statement. verified_active = latest accepted statement for (organization_id, relationship) is status=active and within its validity window. revoked_or_expired = the relationship has been revoked or is outside its not_before/expires_at window. Declared-only organization hints with no statement are carried in declared_organization_hints, not as rows.

delegation_ref.description: Resolved authorization.delegation_ref for delegated issuer roles (governance_service / account_authority).

relationships.description: Projected ak.realm.organization statement rows (verified_active and revoked_or_expired), latest-per-(organization_id, relationship).

declared_organization_hints.description: owning_organizations declared hints (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0) that have NO verified ak.realm.organization statement. These are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.title: Arkret Realm Policy-Server Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm policy-server config operations (ak.self.realm_policy_server.*). The PUT builds a ak.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage). This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical ak.realm.policy_server payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode); see spec/v1/zh/authz/policy-server.md §2.

from_org_fallback.description: True when the config was resolved via the governed_by / org-fallback chain rather than a row on the Realm itself.

schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret Realm Read + Moderation-Policy Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm read operations and moderation-policy management (ak.self.realm.*). Realm read returns the lifecycle projection; export returns a full event-log + operation dump; effective moderation-policy returns the organization-inherited merged view; the moderation-policy override write builds a ak.realm.moderation_policy fact (subject to organization approval). See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md and spec/v1/zh/governance/content-moderation.md.

operations.description: Operation dump rows {operation_id, realm_id, object_kind, operation_type, payload, created_at}.

events.description: Event-log dump rows {event_id, realm_id, event_kind, operation_type, operation_id, sender, payload, created_at}.

realm_effective_moderation_policy.$comment: Open extension surface: the merged moderation-policy view carries deployment-defined organization/realm policy layers and fanout metadata; additionalProperties intentionally true so servers may surface implementation-specific layer detail without a wire-breaking change.

inheritance_chain.description: Organization DIDs (or deployment-local organization identifiers) contributing policy layers, parent-first.

realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.$comment: Open extension surface: the ak.realm.moderation_policy document body is a free-form governance object (rules[], targets[], allow_override[], organization_approval[]); additionalProperties intentionally true so the override schema can evolve without a wire-breaking change. The document is canonical-JSON validated server-side.
realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.description: Realm moderation-policy override body. Free-form ak.realm.moderation_policy document. When the override targets actions an organization policy denies, it requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document.

not.$comment: forbidden Realm authorship field; canonical name is created_by

security_class.description: Optional security class. 'high_assurance' forbids federation_policy=open and SHOULD use stricter resolver/E2EE/audit defaults. Omitted = 'standard'.

trust_domain.description: Immutable deployment trust domain captured by ak.realm.create. Receivers MUST require this to match the current Realm trust domain before accepting cross-domain replay-sensitive proofs.

owning_organizations.description: Declared or projected organization principals associated with this Realm. Each DID MUST resolve to an Organization principal. This field alone is not a verified ownership/governance endorsement; clients and directories MUST require an active ak.realm.organization statement for verified badges or organization-controlled semantics.

fields.description: Product/profile fields. Security-relevant discriminators such as purpose=principal_control and collaboration_role=direct_conversation are schema constrained below; other product fields remain extension-defined.

relation_profiles.description: Optional Relation cardinality and conflict profiles declared by this Realm schema/profile.

on_conflict.description: Conflict handling for mutually unreachable Relation candidates. deterministic_winner selects the candidate with the bytewise-greatest canonical event_digest per the single canonical tie-break rule (zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2); it MUST NOT use HLC, actor id, event_id, local receive order, database id, or service insertion order.

preview_policy_id.description: Optional materialized pointer to the effective preview / peek policy. Canonical writes use ak.realm.preview_policy; absence means directory card / stripped state only, no history stub/snippet preview.

default_strand_id.description: Optional / nullable. AUTHORITATIVE single pointer to the Realm's default discussion Strand (last value projected from ak.realm.set_default_strand; cell ak.component.realm.set_default_strand.v1, cas_register, bottom=reject). A single pointer avoids multi-default dirty state. null / absent means the Realm has no designated default Strand. The reducer rejects a set_default_strand whose strand_id does not resolve to a projected non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm (failed_precondition), so this pointer never dangles. The Strand projection's derived is_default flag is computed as strand_id == this value; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from this field (or the Strand is_default marker) and MUST NOT rely on any Strand-reuses-Realm-UUID implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

content_scheme.description: Content-envelope encryption scheme for MLS-backed Realms (crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10). Orthogonal to encryption_profile, which only declares whether an MLS group exists. mls_rfc9420 = MLS PrivateMessage (per-message forward secrecy, NOT shareable to later joiners; only valid with history_visibility=joined/restricted on MLS-backed Realms). mls_exporter_aead_v1 = MLS-Exporter-derived per-epoch history_secret AEAD (history shareable to authorized later joiners via ak.realm_key.share; per-epoch forward secrecy; does not itself force pre-join delivery). MUST be carried in the MLS governance binding policy_root so receivers can determine, per epoch T0, which scheme applies. Absent: mls_rfc9420 for encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420 Realms; not applicable when encryption_profile=none/external.

content_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide content encryption floor (models/circle.md §7, models/realm-and-space.md §4). This is the Realm's actual content-encryption on/off switch. When e2ee_required, the effective_scope of Strand / Message / Morph / Blob content MUST be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS); reducer MUST failed_precondition (reason=content_encryption_floor_violation) on plaintext content. Independent of encryption_profile, which only declares the encryption MECHANISM (whether an MLS group exists), not which Arkret fields enter ciphertext. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with content_encryption_floor_downgrade. Defaults to allow_plaintext when absent.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide metadata encryption floor (models/circle.md §7), binary and symmetric with content_encryption_floor. allow_plaintext lets user-readable metadata stay wire-plaintext; e2ee_required forces it into encrypted_metadata. Comparison order allow_plaintext < e2ee_required. Effective floor = max(parent Realm value, Circle metadata floor, object profile requirement); any write below the effective floor MUST failed_precondition (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_violation). MUST NOT be relaxed by Circle, Space, or object profile. Space does not carry a metadata floor value. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade. When absent, reducers default to e2ee_required for mls_rfc9420 or content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required Realms, otherwise allow_plaintext.

agent_participation.description: Realm agent participation ceiling: { native_agent: { reply, accept_third_party_mention, act_on_behalf } } — the maximum native personal agent behavior permitted Realm-wide, written by a holder of ak.realm.admin via ak.realm.policy_components. It is the top of the deployment ⊇ Realm ⊇ Circle ⊇ Strand tighten-only chain (inner ceilings MUST NOT widen it; reducer rejects with agent_participation_ceiling_widen). When absent, inherits the deployment-default ceiling (deny-default under sovereign profiles). native_agent and applet_agent ceilings MUST be declared separately. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md.

durability_policy.description: Realm Recovery Key (RRK) durability policy (models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.1, crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10.8). Declares who can recover Realm history after all member devices are lost or all members leave. Confidentiality-axis durability, orthogonal to notary / notary.recovery_* (finality axis: who signs Seals). Recovery recipients are offline HPKE public keys, NOT MLS members. Only effective (mode != none) when content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1; declaring mode != none on an mls_rfc9420 Realm MUST failed_precondition (durability_scheme_incompatible). Granularity = organization composition (point a sensitive Realm's owning_organizations at a finer org), not a per-Realm knob; parent-org retention = list the parent org RRK in recovery_recipients (explicit, member-visible). Written via ak.realm.policy_components.

mode.description: none = no organizational recovery path (total member loss = permanent loss). org_recovery_key = single org RRK. threshold = k-of-n recovery recipients.

recovery_recipients.description: Recovery recipients (RRK holders). MUST be non-empty when mode != none. Each verification_method MUST point to a verification method designated by an active ArkretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry published by principal_id, domain-separated from the principal's did_recovery key.

threshold.description: k-of-n threshold parameters, required when mode=threshold. k <= n and n MUST equal len(recovery_recipients).

then.$comment: The arithmetic rule 1 <= k <= n == len(recovery_recipients) is reducer/conformance validation because JSON Schema cannot compare threshold.n to array length portably.

sync_endpoints.description: Realm-level service binding list for shared notary / sync / mirror / federation peer surfaces. Directory resolve responses expose a requester-filtered join_candidates projection for join-side ingress; raw sync_endpoints are not a public candidate list. Member-level delivery_binding remains on ak.member.state and MUST NOT be inferred from this list.

notary_profile.description: Create-locked Seal finality profile. single_did and threshold deployments require signed Seal single-chain uniqueness; open_set deployments allow multiple Seal leaves and deterministic joined control views; mixed deployments use a primary notary plus fallback recovery notary.

availability_policy.description: Realm policy component governing independently signed byte-availability receipts before Seal inclusion and before snapshot/backfill availability claims. Absent means {min_holders:1, holder_roles:['notary'], applies_to:['seal_include']}. Holder roles are resolved from the accepted notary/service-binding state at the Seal basis; a self-asserted role is insufficient.

audit_policy.description: Realm policy component for range-completeness and seal-transparency witness admission. If absent, receivers MUST NOT accept a seal-transparency auditor attestation as verified v1 evidence, and federation_witness_attested range completeness has no admissible witness set.

digest_algorithm.description: Digest suite (canonicalization x hash tuple) used for DataEvent ids, Control Move ids, Seal ids, state_root, and Merkle leaves within this Realm. It is locked at create except for ak.realm.digest_suite_transition under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. Defaults to sha256. Value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json (this enum MUST be regenerated when a row flips active, e.g. cbor.sha256); bare ids denote canonical-JSON canonicalization, dotted ids denote alternate canonical encodings. Exactly one live suite per Realm; migration uses the control-plane transition Move and dual-root Seal defined by event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

notary.description: Genesis value for the Realm notary cell. Subsequent changes are Control Moves finalized by the previous notary. For single_did profiles, recovery_members and controller organization evidence are required so reducer/authz can reject single-organization recovery setups.

forensic_attribution.$comment: Required for type=threshold (enforced by allOf below). MUST be quorum_intersection when 2*threshold > members.length (two conflicting quorums then intersect in at least one attributable double-signer; see authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1 and BFT Protocol Forensics). MUST be waived when 2*threshold <= members.length, declaring that automatic culprit attribution is unavailable. JSON Schema cannot compare threshold against members.length, so the arithmetic side is reducer/conformance validation (ak.vector.cba_lattice.threshold_forensic_attribution.v1).
forensic_attribution.description: Equivocation culprit-attribution mode for threshold notary committees: quorum_intersection (2k>n, automatic attribution available) or waived (k<=n/2, deployment explicitly waives automatic attribution and relies on committee-level handling).

controller_organization.description: DID of the organization controlling the primary notary, when the resolver or deployment policy can derive it. Required for single_did profile so recovery diversity can be verified.

recovery_controller_organizations.description: Organization DIDs controlling recovery_members. Reducer MUST verify at least one differs from controller_organization for single_did profile.

revocation_freshness_window_ms.description: Realm-level maximum control-plane seal distance/time window for accepting DataEvents whose seal_ref predates an observed revocation seal. Receivers evaluate this window by seal topology and policy (the notary-committed seal-time delta along the Seal DAG per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.3), not by unverified event signing time. risk_tier=high capabilities get no grace (effective 0). High-risk Realms SHOULD use a short value or move the affected cell family to control plane.

recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms.description: Maximum signed Seal.sealed_at distance from the conflict-detecting frontier to a state_witness used by a conflict-recovery Move. Receivers compute the non-negative DAG time delta from the witness Seal to the recovery Move's seal_basis leaves; exceeding this value fails closed with recovery_witness_revoke_lagging.

receipt_sla_ms.description: Realm-level deadline within which a pending control-plane Control Move MUST receive a signed receipt or signed rejection (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Measured by notary-committed seal time, not local receive time. Silent omission past this SLA (modulo bounded defers, see max_receipt_defers) is censorship evidence.

max_receipt_defers.description: Maximum cumulative number of signed defers a single pending Control Move may receive before include / signed-reject is mandatory (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Exceeding it without include/signed-reject is treated as silent omission / censorship evidence.

seal_compaction_max_interval_ms.description: Structural obligation, not advisory: maximum interval between compaction Seals (Seals carrying covered_event_digests[] or an equivalent verifiable full-coverage manifest). Because the cumulative control-plane covered set is defined recursively from predecessor_refs + delta, compaction Seals are the only bounded bootstrap points for new verifiers; a notary that exceeds this interval degrades bootstrap to walking the chain to genesis. open_set deployments MUST use <= 86400000 (24h); threshold deployments MUST use <= 604800000 (7d); single_did SHOULD use <= 86400000. Receivers SHOULD raise governance health alarms when the live chain exceeds the declared interval. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.2 and conformance vector ak.vector.cba_lattice.seal_compaction_interval_enforced.v1.

max_delegation_lifetime_ms.description: Realm-level maximum lifetime window used when an otherwise unbounded parent grant first delegates. Reducers freeze delegation_expiry_seal = first_delegation_sealed_at + effective max_delegation_lifetime_ms and MUST NOT refresh it on re-delegation. Effective value is the minimum of this field and any stricter grant, policy, deployment, or profile override. Defaults to 86400000 ms (24h). See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.1.

bottom_escalation_after_ms.description: Optional timeout after which unresolved bottom diagnostics should be escalated to recovery governance. Expiry does not choose a winner automatically.

cell_lattices.description: Optional Realm-specific lattice declarations for extension cell families.

co_write_policy.description: Optional whitelist constraining which cell families may be written by the same Move.

allOf.$comment: single_did notary profiles bind one DID as the primary notary. controller_organization / recovery_controller_organizations / recovery_members are required ONLY when the deployment can derive a controlling organization (see notary.controller_organization 'when ... can derive it'; decisions/0003 §7 — personal / orgless Realms legitimately omit them and fall back to per-user recovery). When a controller_organization IS declared, an explicit recovery-notary diversity path MUST accompany it. The distinct-controller arithmetic stays semantic/reducer validation because JSON Schema cannot compare DID-controller derivations across resolver evidence.
Org-controlled single_did Realms MUST declare the recovery-notary diversity path alongside the controlling organization.

Threshold notary committees must declare their equivocation culprit-attribution mode at Realm create time. The arithmetic rule (quorum_intersection iff 2*threshold > members.length) is reducer/conformance validation; see notary.forensic_attribution $comment.

Principal control Realms are ordinary ak.schema.realm.v1 objects, but the profile discriminator must be closed at schema level: fields.purpose and schema_refs must appear together, the Realm MUST be MLS-backed, and both encryption floors MUST be pinned to e2ee_required (key-management §4.1 / §5.0.1, realm-and-space §2.8.1). There is no plaintext-floor PCR in v1.
The inverse guard prevents a profile-tagged Realm from omitting the machine-readable purpose discriminator, and pins the encryption floors symmetrically with the forward guard.

Direct Conversation Realms are ordinary Collaboration Realms with a closed machine role. The discriminator and profile must appear together; create-locked Realm security fields are pinned here while the exact-two membership, participant identity, no-Space and main-Strand rules are reducer/profile invariants.
The inverse Direct Conversation guard prevents a profile-tagged ordinary Realm from omitting its collaboration role discriminator.
Principal Control and Direct Conversation are mutually exclusive Realm roles.
content_scheme is only meaningful for MLS-backed Realms. Plaintext or external encryption Realms MUST NOT declare an MLS content envelope scheme.

recipient_id.description: Realm-unique stable id for this recovery recipient.

principal_id.description: Principal holding the RRK private key. SHOULD resolve to an Organization Principal for org_recovery_key/threshold; MAY be a personal principal for personal Realms.

verification_method.description: Reference to a verification method in principal_id's DID Document designated by an active ArkretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry (identity/identity-did.md §8.3). The RRK HPKE public key; history-recovery domain, separate from did_recovery.

controller_organization.description: Organization DID controlling this recovery recipient, when derivable; receiver MAY use it to verify org attribution.

cell_role.description: Semantic role declared by Realm schema. Security-root roles are restricted to control-plane lattice semantics by the allOf rules below.

plane.description: CBA plane for this cell family. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST be control. Ordinary content / draft / cosmetic cells SHOULD be data unless sealed=true.

sealed.description: Opt-in control-plane finality for an otherwise data-like cell family. When true, plane MUST be control. A data-like family reused as an authorization input for any risk_tier=high capability MUST set sealed=true; ordinary authorization_root declarations are already required to use plane=control.

initial_value.description: Optional cell schema initial value (cas_register only). When defined, the cas_register `join` algorithm initialises `current` to this value (rather than null) before applying any Move. Combined with a `head_eq: <initial_value>` predicate on the first set Move, this implements singleton-once-set cells via the empty sentinel pattern. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

sentinel_writers.description: Optional companion to `initial_value` (cas_register only). When `initial_value` is declared, set ops whose effect equals the sentinel are rejected by default (initial_value_reserved). Listing event_kinds here permits those event_kinds to write the sentinel back — typically the cleanup event_kind in a singleton-once-set / explicit-reset workflow. Capability authorization remains a separate independent check. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

allOf.$comment: Security-root roles are always control-plane.
sealed=true is the explicit data-to-control opt-in.
initial_value is only defined for cas_register (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1). Other lattices reject the field.

sentinel_writers is the companion of initial_value; it only makes sense on a cas_register cell that has declared initial_value. Reject declarations on other lattices, and reject declarations on cas_register cells that lack initial_value (since there is no sentinel to authorise writing back).

schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Policy
schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.description: Normative grammar for a principal's recovery policy. Bound to the Principal Control Realm via signed publish / rotate / revoke control events; receivers MUST reject `recover`, `rotate`, `ak.device.authorize` and Cross-Signing Reset evidence whose proof family / threshold / approval requirement is not allowed by the currently accepted recovery policy. See identity/key-management.md §3.3 / §7 / §8 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

version.description: Monotonically increasing counter scoped by principal_id. Receivers MUST reject a publish whose version is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy.

supersedes.description: Predecessor policy_id. Null only for the genesis policy of a principal.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier the policy applies to. Cross-domain proofs MUST fail.

allowed_proof_kinds.description: Which proof families this policy authorizes for recovery and cross-signing reset. Each entry constrains the matching proof kind defined in device-lifecycle.md §14. Empty array is valid only for an explicit revocation policy that also sets expires_at.

threshold.description: Threshold-recovery configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'threshold_recovery'.

k.description: Minimum share count required to reconstruct the recovery secret. MUST be >= 2; threshold=1 is forbidden because it collapses to a single-holder bearer.

n.description: Total number of shares issued. MUST equal shares.length and MUST be >= k.

vss_root_commitment.description: Optional VSS root commitment binding all shares' polynomial commitments. SHOULD be present for Feldman / Pedersen schemes.

reshare_policy.description: Proactive secret sharing / re-share cadence. Holders MUST be able to refresh shares without reconstructing the secret. Implementations SHOULD re-share at least once per `max_share_age_seconds`.

device_quorum.description: Device-quorum configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'device_quorum'.

trusted_recovery_services.description: Recovery services explicitly declared in the principal's DID Document (or sovereign trust seal). Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'trusted_recovery_service'.

recovery_keys.description: Recovery signing keys this principal authorizes to satisfy a 'recovery_unlock' proof. Each entry binds a verification method (24-word Recovery Key derived signing key, or hardware-released equivalent) to the principal. A recovery_unlock proof's recovery_secret_ref MUST resolve to one of these entries that is non-revoked and within its validity window at the proof's binding time; the proof signature MUST verify under that entry's public key. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'recovery_unlock'. See identity/key-management.md §7.5.2 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4 / §15.

recovery_key_agreements.description: Backup-only HPKE recipient keys. These entries are cryptographically and semantically distinct from recovery_keys[] signing keys. key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref resolves only here in the envelope's referenced accepted policy, never to a DID Document-only key agreement or a recovery signing verification_method.

approval_requirement.description: Two-person rule / cooldown enforcement layered on top of cryptographic proofs.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wall-clock window between recovery announcement and effective key change. Receivers MUST reject control-stream Events whose accepted_at is earlier than announcement_at + cooldown_seconds.

announcement_required.description: When true, recovery MUST be announced on the principal control stream and visible to authorized devices before effective key change.

audit.description: Where the recovery strand MUST emit auditable records (recovery announcement, holder participation, completion receipt).

receipt_required.description: When true, recovery completion MUST produce a ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 record.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the authorized issuer: bootstrap-accepted first device for genesis; current SSK for later A-model updates; current-generation accepted device for later B-model updates; or a coordinator satisfying the superseded policy quorum. Receivers resolve this semantic authority from accepted principal-control state, not from arbitrary DID Document membership.

recovery_key_entry.description: A recovery signing key the principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs. The verification_method is the stable recovery_secret_ref; public_key_multibase carries the actual signing public key so B-model principals do not depend on a DID Document verificationMethod. key_agreement_ref pairs this signer with a distinct backup-only recovery_key_agreements[] entry.

verification_method.description: DID URL (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-1`) identifying this recovery signing key. This is the value a recovery_unlock proof carries in recovery_secret_ref / verification_method and MUST be unique within recovery_keys[].

public_key_multibase.description: Multikey for the recovery proof signature algorithm. MUST NOT equal or be converted into the paired HPKE key.

key_agreement_ref.description: MUST identify exactly one non-revoked recovery_key_agreements[] entry in the same policy.

alg.description: Signature algorithm used by the recovery key. Values mirror active signature-alg-registry rows; ML-DSA-65 use additionally requires the corresponding PQ-capable implementation profile.

not_before.description: Earliest instant this recovery key may authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this recovery key MUST NOT authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

revoked_at.description: When set, the entry is revoked from this instant onward and MUST NOT satisfy any recovery_unlock proof whose binding time is at or after it.

recovery_key_agreement_entry.description: Dedicated X25519 HPKE recipient for key-backup envelopes. It cannot verify recovery_unlock or authorize DID/Event operations.

key_agreement_ref.description: Stable identifier used by key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref.

recovery_policy_summary.description: Read-model summary of the currently accepted recovery policy. `policy` carries the original ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object when the service can disclose it to the caller.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple equivalent to `{policy_id, policy_version: version}`. When present, it MUST match policy_id/version.

policy.description: Full accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object. Omitted only when the caller is authorized to learn that a policy exists but not to receive holder/share details.

control_frontier.description: Optional principal control-stream frontier under which the active policy was observed.

recovery_policy_active_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.resource.get. `active_policy=null` is a successful read meaning no accepted recovery policy currently exists for the resolved principal.

principal_id.description: Resolved principal. Required when the request used an explicit principal_id selector; SHOULD be present on all authenticated reads.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple for the active policy. MUST be absent or null-equivalent when active_policy is null, and MUST match active_policy.policy_id/version when active_policy is present.

recovery_policy_publish_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish after accepting a ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 publish or rotation.

holder.description: DID of the share holder. MAY be a user, a hardware module identified by did:key, or a custodial service. The holder DID does NOT inherit any business capability of the principal.

schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Receipt
schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed completion receipt for a principal recovery strand. Bound to the recovery_session_id, identity model, model generation, accepted device authorization path, every proof, backup unlock, and MLS Welcome replay action. Formal recovery receipts are signed only after the recovering device has been accepted via ak.device.authorize; pre-authorization failures use server outcome/audit evidence instead. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

recovery_session_id.description: Stable session identifier used by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof, and MLS Welcome replay during this recovery. Receivers MUST reject receipts that reuse a session id already accepted for the same principal.

previous_model_generation_ref.description: Server-snapshotted generation at recovery-session creation: accepted SSK generation for cross_signing or pre-reanchor DID versionId for enrollment_authority.

result_model_generation_ref.description: Accepted generation after completion. Equals previous_model_generation_ref for an A-model fresh-device recovery without reset; equals the re-anchor did_version_id for B-model recovery.

proof_digest.description: Canonical-JSON digest of the proof transcript used to satisfy the active recovery policy. Auditors recompute against the originating proof event to verify.

quorum_participant_count.description: Required for device_quorum and threshold_recovery; equals the number of participating members / shares.

share_ids.description: When kind=threshold_recovery, the share_ids that participated. MUST be a subset of the active policy's shares[].

welcome_count.description: Number of MLS Welcomes successfully replayed for the recovering device.

outcome_reason_code.description: Free-form reason code; MUST be present when outcome != 'completed'.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the new_device_id's accepted device key. Receivers MUST resolve it through the principal control stream and verify that ak.device.authorize for new_device_id was accepted before this receipt was signed; service keys and unauthorised fresh-device keys MUST NOT sign a formal recovery_receipt.

schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.title: Arkret Recovery Session
schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.description: Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine. The root object is the recovery session state shape; request body/result helper shapes and kind-specific recovery proof transcripts live in $defs. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

challenge.description: base64url(no padding) encoding of 256 bits from a CSPRNG. The value is single-use and bound to one recovery_session_id.

identity_model.description: A-model cross-signing or B-model external enrollment authority. Server derives and verifies this value from accepted DID/control state.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that satisfied this session.

ssk_generation.description: Accepted cross-signing generation snapshotted when the session is created. Reducers MUST reject completion if the current accepted generation no longer equals this value.

current_device_generation_ref.description: B-model reducer-managed generation snapshotted at session creation.

registry_head.description: Digest of the B-model accepted identity-registry head snapshot.

rejection_reason_code.description: Closed enum. proof_failed: proof verification failures reached the server policy limit; operator_rejected: explicit operator/admin rejection; risk_policy: server risk policy rejection; superseded: replaced by a newer recovery session for the same principal/device.

expires_at.description: Session expiration. Default TTL is 900 seconds; deployments MAY shorten it and MUST NOT lengthen it unless a future recovery_policy field explicitly permits the override.

created_at.description: Recovery session creation/signing time. This is the created_at value used in the recovery proof transcript.

expected_recovery_policy_ref.description: Optional client CAS hint. Servers MUST snapshot the currently accepted policy; if this hint is present and differs, the request fails with recovery_policy_mismatch.

challenge.description: Echo of the server-issued session challenge. Mismatch fails as recovery_session_challenge_mismatch.

verification_method.description: Principal-grade DID control verification method authorized by the active recovery policy.

recovery_secret_ref.description: DID URL or recovery-policy key ref for the recovery key entry authorized at the session's created_at.

unlock_commitment.description: Public binding hash over the session transcript and recovery_secret_ref. Possession is proven by signature; this commitment prevents proof-shell substitution.

attestation_ref.description: Reference to service attestation evidence when required by the active recovery policy.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the holder's share release transcript bound to share_id, holder, recovery_session_id, requesting_device_id, audience, and issued_at. For threshold_recovery / recovery_unlock the requesting device may be a not-yet-authorized new device; holder validation binds proof-of-possession and the recovery session instead of requiring an existing device record.

proof.description: Kind-specific recovery proof. Receivers reconstruct the canonical transcript from stored session state and the proof body, then verify that the active recovery policy allows this proof kind and its threshold/service/share constraints.

recovery_session_complete_request_body.description: Recovery completion references only accepted artifacts; the server derives the identity model and snapshotted generation from recovery_session_state. A references accepted authorize/list-update events. B references the accepted atomic re-anchor/authorize unit and its batch receipt; isolated event-store presence is insufficient.

authorization_event_id.description: event_id of the client-submitted, accepted ak.device.authorize.

device_list_update_event_id.description: event_id of the client-submitted, accepted ak.device.list_update.

authorization_event_id.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize event emitted to the principal control stream.

device_list_update_event_id.description: Accepted ak.device.list_update event emitted to the principal control stream.

model_generation_ref.description: SSK generation for cross_signing; DID versionId for enrollment_authority.

created_at.description: Session creation/signing time, not client proof creation time.

generic_recovery_transcript.description: Canonical transcript field set shared by recovery_unlock, device_quorum, trusted_recovery_service, and threshold_recovery proofs before adding kind-specific proof_body. Producers and receivers MUST bind exactly this session tuple.

proof_body.description: The selected proof object with signature bytes omitted where the kind-specific verification rule says so.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For agent_sidecar_of it MUST equal the owning Agent Sidecar object's reducer-derived backing_circle_id and callers cannot choose another Circle (models/sidecar.md). The resulting effective_scope=circle prevents non-members from enumerating the edge from the public endpoint. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1).

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from scope_circle_id at create time (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. Immutable across any later scope rebind. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (reducer-managed, reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the reducer stamps it on accept.

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows conformance/encoding.md §9. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

state.description: Relation state. 'tombstoned' covers both deletion and redaction; the originating reason is preserved on the ak.relation.tombstone / ak.redaction event, not on the materialized object.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.relation.tombstone / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

object_ref.description: Typed canonical reference. Allowed kinds: realm, space, actor_profile, strand, message, morph, relation, event, view, blob metadata ID, content-addressed blob ref (active digest suites per artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json; v1: sha256 / blake3), or DID. Space is a valid Relation endpoint (board/list containers, e.g. board --contains--> list). The blob ref suite set is aligned with blob.schema.json and notification.schema.json so any content-addressed blob ref accepted in those schemas is also accepted as a Relation endpoint.

relation_conflict_diagnostic.description: Projection-only conflict diagnostic emitted for deterministic_winner losers and require_review output. reducer_input MUST be false; MUST NOT be treated as canonical event bytes or dedupe authority. See zh/models/relation.md §6.

dedupe_key.description: Canonical projection of the dedupe key under which these candidates collided.

winner.description: The deterministic winner (event_digest bytewise-greatest per the single canonical tie-break rule, zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2), or omitted-equivalent for require_review where no canonical winner is projected.

losers.description: Conflict losers retained for audit and explicit repair. Bounded by the conflict fanout limit (v1 public profile: 16 total candidates including the winner).

event_digest.description: Canonical signed Event digest (<digest-suite>:<hex>), the bytewise tie-break key.

reason.description: Optional reason code for this candidate's disposition (e.g. relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded).

object_ref.description: Canonical object reference. Acceptable typed-id kinds match the v1 resource selector kind enum (see resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1). Notably MUST NOT include 'actor_profile' (use the 'actor' selector with did pattern), nor non-canonical 'board' / 'list' / 'card' / 'subject' / 'room' kinds — board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket are Space objects and MUST use the 'space' kind together with the 'allowed_space_kinds' constraint to restrict which Space kinds the grant covers.

actor_id.description: Concrete principal / service / agent DID. v1 forbids actor:*; actor selectors MUST NOT use a wildcard subject.

match_scope.description: Selector match breadth. exact matches only the named resource; children matches immediate children; subtree matches descendants including nested children; realm_wide is valid only when realm_id is present and limits matching to the named Realm. The normative algorithm is zh/authz/resource-selector-grammar.md ?6.

allOf.$comment: resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1: notification / read_cursor selectors are realm-scoped and the object part is *-only (notification:<realm>:* / read_cursor:<realm>:*). A bare {"kind":"read_cursor"} with no realm_id would otherwise match every principal's read cursors across all Realms (see C04-07). Force realm_id and forbid a precise object id (no notification_id / read_cursor_id field exists; selection is realm-wide *-only).
resource-selector-grammar.md ?3.1/?4.2/?6: space and circle selectors are Realm-scoped in v1; wildcard space/circle selectors MUST carry realm_id to avoid cross-Realm authorization expansion.

Realm-local resource kinds always carry realm_id, including exact-id selectors. This prevents a schema-valid bare kind selector from matching every Realm and keeps authorization scope explicit in signed grant bytes.

resource-selector-grammar.md §4.8/§8.1: actor:* is forbidden and an actor selector MUST carry a concrete principal DID. Force actor_id present so a bare {"kind":"actor"} is rejected at the schema layer rather than only at the reducer (selector_actor_wildcard_forbidden).

schemas/sdk-conformance-claim.schema.jso.title: Arkret SDK Conformance Claim
schemas/sdk-conformance-claim.schema.jso.description: Signed, artifact-bound SDK release claim. The proof covers RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the object with proof omitted, prefixed by the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-sdk-conformance-claim-v1 followed by LF.

build_variants.description: Optional per-build profile inventory for source or multi-variant SDK distributions. Variant IDs MUST be unique and each feature_set_digest binds the exact normalized feature/configuration set used to produce that variant.

schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.title: Arkret SealTransparency
schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.description: Seal transparency wire objects (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.4): an append-only log entry binding one accepted Seal tuple, and an independent auditor attestation over a log range. The log makes split-view attacks (showing different Seal chains to different receivers) detectable: an operator must either publish consistently or fork the log, and a log fork is provable from two signed entries with the same log_index. Top-level object is a log entry; auditor attestations use #/$defs/auditor_attestation.

log_id.description: Stable identifier of the transparency log (operator URL, DID, or registry name).

log_index.description: Zero-based append-only position. Two differently-signed entries with the same (log_id, log_index) are a provable log fork.

prev_entry_digest.description: Digest of the previous entry's canonical bytes (hash chain). null only for log_index 0.

auditor_attestation.description: Signed statement by an independent auditor (peer Realm or third party) that it verified the log range [from_index, to_index]: append-only consistency, Seal signature validity, and control/completeness monotonicity along every Seal DAG predecessor edge represented in the range. Log-index-adjacent concurrent leaves are not compared. A client accepts this as verified v1 evidence only when a concrete operation/profile carries it and the deployment policy's required attestation count is met.

head_entry_digest.description: Digest of the entry at to_index, binding the attested range head.

checks.description: All checks MUST be true. dag_edges_verified means monotonic checks were performed along every represented predecessor edge, not by log_index adjacency; an auditor that cannot assert a check MUST NOT issue the attestation.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical entry / attestation bytes with the signature field omitted.

schemas/seal.schema.json.title: Arkret Seal
schemas/seal.schema.json.description: Wire shape of a Arkret CBA Seal. It finalizes only control-plane Events. `delta[]` is the canonical set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal; cumulative coverage is derived recursively as covered_set(S)=set(S.delta) union covered_set(predecessor_refs[]). `control_event_set_root` authenticates that recursive covered_set and is used for basis, inclusion and non-membership proofs. Optional data_* roots are observational only and MUST NOT gate DataEvents. Identity & signature model (see zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6): the typed `id` (`ak:seal:<algo>:<hex>`) is content-derived — its hex equals H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Seal canonical bytes are the canonical JSON of every signed top-level field EXCEPT id and notary_signature. The `notary_signature` is NOT part of canonical bytes. Receivers MUST recompute H(seal_canonical_bytes) and verify the notary signature over the same bytes.

id.description: Content-derived typed reference. hex part MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm, where seal_canonical_bytes is the canonical JSON of every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`. Receivers MUST recompute and verify; mismatch → digest_mismatch. NEVER include `id` in the hash input — that would create a self-reference.

delta.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal. DataEvent digests MUST NOT appear here. Receivers MUST reject the Seal if any delta entry is already covered by a predecessor, if any entry is not a known valid Control Move digest, or if the list is not canonical sorted and duplicate-free.

control_event_set_root.description: Authenticated root over the recursive covered_set of this Seal. Default construction is RFC6962 Merkle root over canonical bytewise-sorted covered_set(S); inclusion uses Merkle audit path and non-membership uses sorted-neighbor proof. The root is not computed over delta[] alone.

state_root.description: Merkle root of control-plane cell state only.

completeness_root.description: Control-plane per-actor interval / chain-head completeness commitment. It does not prove absence of unknown actors.

notary_seq.description: Per-signer or committee slot sequence used for equivocation detection. Same signer and same realm_id MUST NOT sign two different canonical Seal bodies with the same notary_seq.

data_view_root.description: Optional observational root of KeyView records keyed by data cell id. It is not a DataEvent admission gate.

data_event_set_root.description: Optional observational root over DataEvent digests seen in this seal window. Missing DataEvents are not invalid.

coverage_scope.description: Optional observational coverage declaration for data_view_root / data_event_set_root. The object is intentionally closed only by deployment profiles; core verifiers treat it as signed diagnostic material.

covered_event_digests.description: Optional compaction materialization of the full recursive covered_set(S), canonical bytewise-sorted and duplicate-free. When present, receivers MUST verify it equals set(delta) union all predecessor covered sets and that control_event_set_root is computed over this exact set. Non-compaction Seals normally omit it.

previous_state_root.description: Hash-algorithm transition only: present iff this Seal is a Transition Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. It commits the governance view before the transition Move is applied, computed with previous_digest_algorithm. state_root commits the post-transition governance view with the new suite. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

previous_digest_algorithm.description: Profile id of the previous hash algorithm. Required iff previous_state_root is present; absent on non-transition Seals.

notary_signature.description: Signature over seal_canonical_bytes (every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`). MUST NOT enter the canonical bytes itself — signatures never sign themselves. Seal is not an Event Envelope, so its signature uses the generic non-Event proof field `payload_digest`; that value MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Event Envelope proofs use `event_digest` instead.

sealed_at.description: Normative notary commit timestamp covered by the Seal signature transcript. It is the time input for revocation_freshness_window_ms, recovery_witness_freshness_window_ms, receipt_sla_ms, and reducer-derived projection timestamps. It MUST be >= every predecessor Seal.sealed_at. A value beyond verifier wall time + hard_future_skew_ms produces non-terminal seal_deferred_future_skew and MUST be retried as the clock advances; it is not a permanent rejection or a lattice winner input.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Bare DID is not valid for signatures because verifiers need a stable verification method, not only a controller DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of seal_canonical_bytes for this non-Event Seal signature. Do not rename to event_digest: event_digest is reserved for Event Envelope proofs.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

schemas/service-describe.schema.json.title: Arkret Service Describe
schemas/service-describe.schema.json.description: Canonical service describe response returned by ak.server.query.describe and per-surface describe operations. It combines stable service metadata (service_id, service_kind, protocol_version, profiles, bindings, auth, limits, plaintext visibility and rate-limit policy) with claim-level partitions: implemented_features, claimed_profiles, verified_profiles, experimental_features and compat_surfaces. The `supported_operations` field MUST list endpoint-callable operation_ids. Constraint: when `development_mode=true`, the service MUST NOT advertise any `verified_profiles` entry, and clients MUST verify the referenced verification artifacts before treating verified_profiles as production conformance. See service-surface.md §3.0.

service_id.description: DID of the service endpoint making this describe claim.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_kind.description: One logical role this service plays on the wire. Each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role; co-located roles sharing a public binding use separate role-scoped responses selected by GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>. The value space is registry/service-kind-registry.json filtered to active rows whose valid_in contains service_describe.

profile_bindings.description: Profile-specific carrier declarations keyed by profile id. A profile that mandates one interoperable private carrier must bind it here rather than relying on a product-local route.

supported_operations.description: operation_ids that this endpoint can actually be invoked with. Element format SHOULD match the canonical operation_registry ids (e.g. `ak.self.events.command.submit`).

supported_bindings.description: Transport binding declarations for this service.

supported_features.description: Feature identifiers (`ak.feature.*`) the service supports. Distinct from profile claims.

auth_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations.

methods.description: Authentication methods offered for this principal/account surface. Methods describe proof providers, standard discovery, and the proof kind accepted by the Account Authority. Arkret gate/account routing is always derived from account_authority.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

max_get_query_selectors.description: Maximum total selector count (`realms[]` + `actors[]`) that this service accepts on GET /_arkret/self/events. Clients SHOULD use POST /_arkret/self/events/query when the selector count exceeds this value or filters are sensitive enough to avoid URL logging. If omitted, clients use the v1 default of 8.

mls_governance_proof.description: Required with these exact v1 interoperability bounds when supported_operations contains ak.self.events.query.mls_governance_proof.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible. An empty object means the service claims no plaintext classes; Realm plaintext_visible_services entries MUST match non-empty data_classes here.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service is implemented to receive.

max_visibility.description: Maximum plaintext visibility class the service claims it can receive. Omitted is treated as none unless data_classes is non-empty.

privacy_derivation.description: Machine-readable privacy-preserving identifier derivation claims. Secret material is never published here; only profile and epoch metadata needed for audit and rotation checks.

secret_scope.description: The HMAC salt/pepper is unique to this service context and MUST NOT be shared across Principal Servers, organizations, or push routes.

salt_epoch_id.description: Opaque public epoch label for the active secret. This is not the secret salt value.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound for subject-private invite/contact receive policies. Principal Servers SHOULD expose this in describe so clients can show which user reachability preferences are capped by server policy.

rate_limit_policy_id.description: Identifier for a cacheable, verifiable rate-limit policy object with the same minimum fields as rate_limit_policy. See zh/sync/api-conventions.md §8.

rate_limit_policy.description: Inline rate-limit policy. If the service can return rate_limited, entries[] MUST expose at least endpoint or operation_id, rate_limit_scope, a window/limit tuple or a retry hint; an empty entries[] explicitly means no predictable endpoint-level rate limit beyond generic abuse protection.

egress_network_policy.description: Coarse outbound-network policy for SSRF protection. Public describe MAY omit sensitive allowlist entries; authenticated operator describe MAY return the complete policy. Normative semantics are defined in zh/sync/api-conventions.md §11.2.

resource_kinds.description: Directory-service resource classes indexed by ak.find.directory.query.describe. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

discovery_profiles.description: Directory discovery profiles and extension profile ids advertised by ak.find.directory.query.describe. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

private_contact_discovery.description: Complete machine-readable configuration for ak.private_contact_discovery.v1. Required when supported_operations contains ak.find.directory.query.private_contact_discovery; clients MUST fail closed if any field is absent or unsupported.

oprf_mode.description: RFC 9497 modeVOPRF (0x01), distinct from the ciphersuite identifier.

public_key.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the active 32-byte ristretto255 VOPRF public key. Decoders additionally validate the group encoding and reject the identity element.

key_epoch.description: Epoch accepted for new blind requests. A batch admitted under an older epoch remains bound to its pinned key and cached outcome until its advertised completion TTL expires.

batch_item_count.description: Exact cardinality required for blinded_elements, evaluated_elements, derived_prefixes, hit_bitmap and, when enabled, handoff_stubs. Clients create indistinguishable dummy elements before sending the blind request.

proof_shape.description: One 64-byte RFC 9497 batched DLEQ proof covers the entire fixed-size batch.

handoff_stubs_mode.description: Shape is fixed for the advertised key epoch. always means handoff_stubs is present at every match position with dummy entries where necessary; never means the field is absent for every match outcome.

response_size_buckets_bytes.description: Allowed exact RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 HTTP entity-body Content-Length buckets for PSI success and Class B failures. The phase uses the smallest bucket that can hold its maximal response shape for the advertised batch_item_count.

blind_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest allowed bucket that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal blind success outcome and every allowed blind-phase Class B error projection for this configuration.

match_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest allowed bucket that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal match success outcome and every allowed match-phase Class B error projection for this batch_item_count and handoff_stubs_mode.

batch_completion_ttl_seconds.description: Exact acceptance interval measured from successful blind admission. The provider retains the pinned key epoch, request bindings and cached outcomes throughout this interval; at or after admission_time + this value it rejects the batch as psi_batch_unavailable.

anti_enumeration_delay.description: Origin-side delay distribution shared by success and Class B paths for the same phase, sampled only after authentication and syntax validation.

restricted_query_proof.description: Whether the directory requires holder-approved proof for restricted or privacy-sensitive query classes.

ingest_modes.description: Directory ingest modes supported by this instance.

accept_policy_kind.description: Directory resource acceptance policy advertised by ak.find.directory.query.describe.

accept_policy_ref.description: Optional human-readable or governance reference describing how a resource obtains directory acceptance.

default_ttl_seconds.description: Default directory entry TTL in seconds.

max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum accepted directory entry TTL in seconds.

revalidation_grace_seconds.description: Grace period for refreshing indexed resources after TTL expiry.

accepted_resource_kinds.description: Subset of resource kinds accepted by this directory instance.

accepted_did_methods.description: Principal/governance DID methods accepted by this directory instance.

takedown_contact.description: Operator takedown notification or appeal contact, expressed as a DID or URL.

rate_limits.description: Readable per-DID, per-organization or per-IP directory quota limits.

implemented_features.description: feature_ids the service has implementation code for but does NOT necessarily claim conformance for. Tooling that builds a conformance matrix MUST treat this strictly weaker than `claimed_profiles`.

claimed_profiles.description: Profiles the service self-claims membership in. `claim_kind` MUST be `self_claimed`; verified-only assertions belong under `verified_profiles` and MUST NOT appear here.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a Conformance Verifier run (conformance-suite.md §6.2) has produced a passing verification artifact. Each entry MUST identify the verification run, artifact hash, artifact retrieval reference, verifier DID, verifier signature, and verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty.

artifact_ref.description: URI or transparency-log reference from which the verification artifact can be fetched.

verifier_did.description: DID of the Conformance Verifier that signed the artifact statement.

signature.description: Signature over profile_id, verification_run_id, artifact_digest, artifact_ref, verifier and timestamp.

experimental_features.description: feature_ids that the service exposes but explicitly does NOT promise stable interop for. Clients MUST treat these as non-load-bearing for protocol-level decisions.

compat_surfaces.description: External-interop surfaces this service exposes outside its claimed Arkret v1 conformance.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR string. Parsability and address-family semantics are enforced by the egress policy evaluator.

origin.description: Absolute origin of the client-visible Account Authority.

gate_account_base.description: Absolute base URL from which all client-visible /_arkret/gate/account/* endpoints MUST be derived.

enrollment_authority_did.description: Deployment-pinned authority DID delegated to sign B-model first-device enrollment. REQUIRED when this Account Authority offers account-first onboarding; clients MUST use this pin rather than trusting the Account Authority response being authenticated.

schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.title: Arkret Service Operation DTOs
schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.description: Canonical request and response DTOs for service operations. OpenAPI components reference this artifact so SDK and conformance tooling use one schema source.

grant_jwt.description: The near-expiry DPoP-bound session grant to rotate. Presented with a DPoP holder proof for the key bound into the grant's cnf.jkt.

audience.description: Optional; MUST equal the grant's bound audience if present (audience MUST NOT change across rotation, else audience_mismatch).

device_id.description: Concrete authorized device restoring the soft-logged-out grant chain. MUST match the persisted grant device binding.

proof_kind.description: Fresh proof kind for soft-logout recovery. Current Account Authority implementations MUST accept did_bound_signature or paired_device_proof and fail closed on unsupported kinds.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the soft-logout restore request transcript bound by the proof.

audience.description: MUST equal the session grant audience.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

signature.description: Detached JWS over the soft-logout proof transcript.

verification_method.description: Optional DID URL expected to match the detached JWS kid; the DID component MUST match the session grant subject.

grant_jwt.description: Rotated grant: same subject/scope/audience, cnf.jkt unchanged, fresh minutes-to-hours expiry.

session_public_key.description: JWK the rotated grant is bound to (the device holder key).

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder key (equals the grant's cnf.jkt).

previous_grant_id.description: The prior grant, single-use revoked on success.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ak.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience.description: Audience the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Principal Servers validating /_arkret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ak.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (grant_id, grant_jwt_hash, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Principal Server grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Principal Server. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Principal Server uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

redirect_url.description: Deployment-controlled browser handoff URL. This outcome MUST NOT contain SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance is only via SessionGrantRequestBody.proof.proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ak.self.authz.query.check input — local capability projection / preflight / diagnostic query. `resource` is optional because some actions (e.g. `ak.realm.create`, identity-scoped actions) have no Realm-bound target. The result is not a signed Policy Server decision and MUST NOT be used as Event auth_context, reducer accept proof, or cross-service authorization fact; dynamic policy obligations use ak.self.policy.query.check.

actor_id.description: Subject DID whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, frontier reference, request metadata.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ak.self.authz.query.check diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This shape may include freshness and obligation hints, but any obligation that affects reducer admission or external state MUST be re-issued and signed through PolicyCheckOutcome.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are Policy Server-mediated soft outcomes (the request enters async review). Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Frontier freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.
